Meaning: Express an action in a nominal (noun-like) form or state fact or experience.
Formation: Verb-plain form + こと, Verb-phrase in plain form + こと
Example (Japanese): 日本語を話すことができます。
Example (Romaji): Nihongo wo hanasu koto ga dekimasu.
Example (English): I can speak Japanese.

Meaning: Expresses advice or recommendation; 'should', 'it is important', 'it is necessary'.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + ことだ, い-Adjective + ことだ, な-Adjective + なことだ, Noun + のことだ
Example (Japanese): 毎日運動することだ。
Example (Romaji): Mainichi undou suru koto da.
Example (English): You should exercise every day.

Grammar Point: ～ことにしている (〜koto ni shite iru)
Meaning: Express a personal rule or habit; 'I make it a rule to', 'I always make sure to'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ことにしている
Example (Japanese): 毎日運動することにしている。
Example (Romaji): Mainichi undou suru koto ni shite iru.
Example (English): I make it a rule to exercise every day.

Grammar Point: ～ことになっている (〜koto ni natte iru)
Meaning: Describes something that is decided, arranged, or expected.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ことになっている
Example (Japanese): この会社では、20時には仕事を終えることになっている。
Example (Romaji): Kono kaisha de wa, 20-ji ni shigoto o oeru koto ni natte iru.
Example (English): In this company, it is decided that work will end at 8 pm.

Meaning: Indicates that while something may be true or valid, there is another contrasting point.
Formation: Verb-casual + ことは + が, い-Adjective + ことは + が, な-Adjective + だ + ことは + が, Noun + だ + ことは + が
Example (Japanese): この映画は面白いことは面白いが、ちょっと長すぎる。
Example (Romaji): Kono eiga wa omoshiroi koto wa omoshiroi ga, chotto naga-sugiru.
Example (English): This movie may be interesting, but it is a bit too long.

Meaning: Expresses that something doesn't need to be done or there's no occasion to do it; 'don't have to', 'not necessary'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ことはない, い-Adjective + ことはない, な-Adjective + であることはない, Noun + であることはない
Example (Japanese): お金があるから、無理に貯金することはない。
Example (Romaji): Okane ga aru kara, muri ni chokin suru koto wa nai.
Example (English): Since I have enough money, there's no need to force myself to save.

Meaning: Express the degree or extent of a quality; '-ness', 'degree of'.
Formation: い-Adjective (drop い) + さ, な-Adjective + さ
Example (Japanese): この料理は辛さが強い。
Example (Romaji): Kono ryouri wa karasa ga tsuyoi.
Example (English): The spiciness of this dish is strong.

Meaning: Emphasizes a specific item or action; 'even', 'if only', 'as long as'.
Formation: Noun + さえ, Verb-casual + さえ, い-Adjective + さえ, な-Adjective + でさえ
Example (Japanese): お金さえあれば、世界中を旅行できる。
Example (Romaji): Okane sae areba, sekaijuu wo ryokou dekiru.
Example (English): If only I have money, I can travel around the world.

Meaning: Express the idea of 'only', 'no other option but', 'nothing else but'.
Formation: Verb-casual + しかない, い-Adjective + しかない, な-Adjective + しかない, Noun + しかない
Example (Japanese): この問題を解決する方法は一つしかない。
Example (Romaji): Kono mondai wo kaiketsu suru houhou wa hitotsu shika nai.
Example (English): There is only one way to solve this problem.

Meaning: Express a negative state or action; 'not at all', 'none whatsoever'.
Formation: すこしも + Verb-negative
Example (Japanese): 彼はすこしも悲しそうに見えません。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa sukoshimo kanashisou ni miemasen.
Example (English): He doesn't look sad at all.

Meaning: Express 'without doing' something or 'not doing' something.
Formation: Verb-ない form (Remove ない) + ずに
Example (Japanese): 彼は笑わずに話を聞いていました。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa warawazu ni hanashi wo kiiteimashita.
Example (English): He was listening to the story without laughing.

Meaning: Indicates that something or someone caused an unfortunate result.
Formation: Verb-casual + せいで, い-Adjective + せいで, な-Adjective + なせいで, Noun + のせいで
Example (Japanese): 雨のせいで試合が中止になりました。
Example (Romaji): Ame no sei de shiai ga chuushi ni narimashita.
Example (English): The game was cancelled because of the rain.

Meaning: Requesting someone to allow or let you do something (causative request).
Formation: Verb-causative (させ) + て + ください
Example (Japanese): もう一度説明させてください。
Example (Romaji): Mou ichido setsumei sasete kudasai.
Example (English): Please let me explain it once more.

Meaning: For the purpose of; because of; in order to.
Formation: Sentence/phrase 1 + そのために + Sentence/phrase 2
Example (Japanese): 試験に合格するために、毎日勉強しています。そのために、早く寝て早く起きるようにしています。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ni goukaku suru tame ni, mainichi benkyou shiteimasu. Sono tame ni, hayaku nete hayaku okiru you ni shiteimasu.
Example (English): I study every day to pass the exam. For that reason, I go to bed early and wake up early.

Meaning: Shows the result or consequence of a previous action or situation; 'as a result', 'in consequence'.
Formation: Situation/ACTION 1 + その結果 + RESULT
Example (Japanese): 彼女は毎日練習した。その結果、試合に勝った。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa mainichi renshuu shita. Sono kekka, shiai ni katta.
Example (English): She practiced every day. As a result, she won the match.

Meaning: Used to link two or more items; 'and', 'also'.
Formation: Item1 + それと + Item2
Example (Japanese): 買い物に行くつもりです。それと、郵便局にも行かなくては。
Example (Romaji): Kaimono ni iku tsumori desu. Sore to, yuubinkyoku ni mo ikanakute wa.
Example (English): I plan to go shopping, and I also have to go to the post office.

Meaning: Presents two alternatives or choices; 'or', 'either...or'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ？それとも + Verb-casual + ？, etc.
Example (Japanese): コーヒーを飲む？それとも紅茶を飲む？
Example (Romaji): Koohii o nomu? Sore tomo koucha o nomu?
Example (English): Do you want to drink coffee? Or tea?

Meaning: Emphasizes the scarcity or insufficiency of something; 'only', 'nothing but'.
Formation: Noun/Quantity + だけ + しか + Negative Verb
Example (Japanese): 今日は1時間だけしか勉強できなかった。
Example (Romaji): Kyou wa ichijikan dake shika benkyou dekinakatta.
Example (English): Today, I could study for only one hour.

Meaning: Expresses a contrast or contradiction; 'but', 'however', 'even though'.
Formation: Sentence 1 + だけど + Sentence 2, or Sentence 1 + 。だけど、Sentence 2
Example (Japanese): 試験に合格したけど、まだ勉強しなければならない。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ni goukaku shita kedo, mada benkyou shinakereba naranai.
Example (English): I passed the exam, but I still have to study.

Meaning: Indicates an action that has just been completed; 'freshly', 'just'.
Formation: Verb-stem + たて
Example (Japanese): このパンは焼きたてで、まだ温かいです。
Example (Romaji): Kono pan wa yakitate de, mada atatakai desu.
Example (English): This bread is freshly baked and still warm.

Meaning: Express a condition with 'even if'; 'no matter how'.
Formation: たとえ + Verb-casual + ても, たとえ + い-Adjective + くても, たとえ + な-Adjective + であっても, たとえ + Noun + であっても
Example (Japanese): たとえ雨が降っても、出かけましょう。
Example (Romaji): Tatoe ame ga futte mo, dekakemashou.
Example (English): Even if it rains, let's go out.

Meaning: Expresses the result or outcome of an action; 'after', 'just when', 'upon'.
Formation: Verb-た form + ところ
Example (Japanese): 宿題をしたところ、先生からもう一つ課題が出された。
Example (Romaji): Shukudai wo shita tokoro, sensei kara mou hitotsu kadai ga dasareta.
Example (English): Just when I finished my homework, the teacher gave us another assignment.

Meaning: Express the moment something happens; 'as soon as', 'the moment', 'the instant'.
Formation: Verb-た form + とたん
Example (Japanese): ドアを開けたとたん、猫が逃げ出した。
Example (Romaji): Doa wo aketa totan, neko ga nigedashita.
Example (English): As soon as I opened the door, the cat ran away.

Meaning: Express 'every time' or 'whenever'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + たびに, Noun + のたびに
Example (Japanese): 彼女に会うたびに、心が弾む。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo ni au tabi ni, kokoro ga hazumu.
Example (English): Every time I meet her, my heart leaps.

Meaning: Express the reason or cause, often used to justify something.
Formation: Verb-casual + んだものだ, い-Adjective + んだものだ, な-Adjective + なんだものだ, Noun + なんだものだ (often with から as んだものだから)
Example (Japanese): 疲れたんだものだから、休みたい。
Example (Romaji): Tsukareta n da mono da kara, yasumitai.
Example (English): I want to rest because I'm tired.

Meaning: Express an unintentional action or a regretful action; 'ended up doing', 'did accidentally'.
Formation: Verb-て/で form → ちゃった/じゃった (e.g. 食べてしまった → 食べちゃった)
Example (Japanese): 忘れ物をしちゃった。
Example (Romaji): Wasuremono o shichatta.
Example (English): I accidentally left something behind.

Meaning: Do something while or after completing another action; 'while', 'by the way'.
Formation: Verb (dictionary or た-form) + ついでに, Noun + の + ついでに, or Verb-て form + いる + ついでに
Example (Japanese): 買い物に行くついでに、郵便局で手紙を出しましょう。
Example (Romaji): Kaimono ni iku tsuide ni, yuubinkyoku de tegami wo dashimashou.
Example (English): Let's drop off a letter at the post office while going shopping.

Meaning: Used to express that one is trying to recall some information.
Formation: Verb-casual + っけ?, い-Adjective + かったっけ?, な-Adjective/Noun + だっけ?
Example (Japanese): 彼は何時に来るっけ？
Example (Romaji): Kare wa nanji ni kuru kke?
Example (English): What time is he coming again?

Meaning: Expresses fullness or completeness; 'full', 'full of', 'filled with'.
Formation: Noun + で + いっぱい (Note: written as いっぱい, read as 'ippai')
Example (Japanese): 部屋が荷物でいっぱいです。
Example (Romaji): Heya ga nimotsu de ippai desu.
Example (English): The room is full of luggage.

Meaning: Indicate a state where an action is left as is (unchanged or unfinished).
Formation: Verb-ますstem + っぱなし
Example (Japanese): 窓を開けっぱなしにすると、虫が入ってくる。
Example (Romaji): Mado o akeppanashi ni suru to, mushi ga haitte kuru.
Example (English): If you leave the window open, bugs will come in.

Meaning: Summarizing, restating, or clarifying a point: 'in other words', 'that is to say'.
Formation: Sentence A + つまり + Sentence B (rephrasing)
Example (Japanese): 彼は大学の教授です。つまり、専門家です。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa daigaku no kyouju desu. Tsumari, senmonka desu.
Example (English): He is a university professor. In other words, he is an expert.

Meaning: Expressing a past intention or plan; 'was planning to', 'meant to'.
Formation: Verb-casual (dictionary form) + つもりでした
Example (Japanese): 昨日は友達に会うつもりでしたが、風邪を引いてしまいました。
Example (Romaji): Kinou wa tomodachi ni au tsumori deshita ga, kaze o hiite shimaimashita.
Example (English): I was planning to meet my friend yesterday, but I caught a cold.

Meaning: Quote someone's request (telling someone to do something).
Formation: Verb-て form + くれと (言う / 頼む / 伝える, etc.)
Example (Japanese): 電話をかけてくれと言われました。
Example (Romaji): Denwa o kakete kureto iwaremashita.
Example (English): I was told to make a phone call.

Meaning: Suggest or invite someone to try doing something; 'Why don't you try...'.
Formation: Verb-て form + ごらん
Example (Japanese): そのゲームをやってごらん。
Example (Romaji): Sono geemu o yatte goran.
Example (English): Why don't you try playing that game?

Meaning: Expresses reason or cause; 'because', 'since', 'so'.
Formation: Sentence A + ですから + Sentence B
Example (Japanese): 今日は寒いですから、コートを着てください。
Example (Romaji): Kyou wa samui desu kara, kooto o kite kudasai.
Example (English): It's cold today, so please wear a coat.

Meaning: Realization or action done for the first time; 'only after', 'not until'.
Formation: Verb-て form + はじめて
Example (Japanese): 海外に行ってはじめて、日本の良さが分かりました。
Example (Romaji): Kaigai ni itte hajimete, Nihon no yosa ga wakarimashita.
Example (English): Only after going abroad did I realize how great Japan is.

Meaning: Express a desire for someone else to do something; 'I want you to do...'.
Formation: Verb-て form + ほしい
Example (Japanese): 子供にもっと勉強してほしい。
Example (Romaji): Kodomo ni motto benkyou shite hoshii.
Example (English): I want my child to study more.

Meaning: 'Even if', 'even though', or 'although'.
Formation: Verb-て form + も, い-Adjective (～く) + ても, な-Adjective/Noun (～で) + も
Example (Japanese): 雨が降っても、運動会は開催されます。
Example (Romaji): Ame ga futte mo, undoukai wa kaisai saremasu.
Example (English): Even if it rains, the sports festival will be held.

Meaning: Express a wish or hope; 'it would be nice if', 'I hope that'.
Formation: Verb-casual + といいなあ, い-Adjective + といいなあ, な-Adjective + だといいなあ, Noun + だといいなあ
Example (Japanese): 明日晴れるといいなあ。
Example (Romaji): Ashita hareru to ii naa.
Example (English): I hope it's sunny tomorrow.

Meaning: Used for quoting, defining, or giving an example; 'called', 'that is to say', 'like'.
Formation: Noun + という + Noun, Verb-casual + という + Noun, い-Adjective + という + Noun, な-Adjective + という + Noun
Example (Japanese): 本屋で「ハリー・ポッター」という本を買いました。
Example (Romaji): Hon'ya de 'Harry Potter' to iu hon o kaimashita.
Example (English): I bought a book called 'Harry Potter' at the bookstore.

Grammar Point: ～ということだ (〜to iu koto da)
Meaning: Express a conclusion or hearsay; 'I heard', 'it means', 'it can be said'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ということだ, い-Adjective + ということだ, な-Adjective + だということだ, Noun + だということだ
Example (Japanese): 彼は来週結婚するということだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa raishuu kekkon suru to iu koto da.
Example (English): I heard that he is getting married next week.

Meaning: Used to provide an example or characteristic related to the topic; 'when it comes to', 'speaking of'.
Formation: Noun + というと
Example (Japanese): 日本料理というと、寿司が思い浮かぶ。
Example (Romaji): Nihon ryouri to iu to, sushi ga omoiukabu.
Example (English): When it comes to Japanese cuisine, sushi comes to mind.

Meaning: Explain or emphasize the reason for a situation or action.
Formation: Verb-casual + というの, い-Adjective + というの, な-Adjective + だというの, Noun + だというの
Example (Japanese): 遅刻したのは、電車が遅れたというのだ。
Example (Romaji): Chikoku shita no wa, densha ga okureta to iu no da.
Example (English): The reason I was late is because the train was delayed.

Meaning: Used to provide an explanation or definition; 'that is to say...', 'by that, I mean...'.
Formation: Phrase/sentence + というのは + explanation/definition
Example (Japanese): 日本に行くというのは、日本に旅行することです。
Example (Romaji): Nihon ni iku to iu no wa, Nihon ni ryokou suru koto desu.
Example (English): Going to Japan, that is to say, traveling to Japan.

Meaning: Express a comparison with preference; 'rather than', 'more like', 'instead of'.
Formation: Verb-casual + というより, い-Adjective + というより, な-Adjective + だというより, Noun + だというより
Example (Japanese): この部屋は狭いというより、居心地がいい。
Example (Romaji): Kono heya wa semai to iu yori, igokochi ga ii.
Example (English): Rather than saying this room is small, it's more like it's cozy.

Meaning: Express the meaning 'even though', 'although', 'but'.
Formation: Verb-casual + といっても, い-Adjective + といっても, な-Adjective + だといっても, Noun + だといっても
Example (Japanese): 彼は有名だといっても、みんなに知られているわけではありません。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa yuumei da to ittemo, minna ni shirarete iru wake de wa arimasen.
Example (English): Even though he's famous, it doesn't mean everyone knows him.

Meaning: Expresses that something is done 'as is', 'as stated', or 'as instructed'.
Formation: Verb-て form + とおり, Noun + のとおり
Example (Japanese): 先生が言ったとおり、宿題をやりました。
Example (Romaji): Sensei ga itta toori, shukudai wo yarimashita.
Example (English): I did my homework exactly as the teacher said.

Meaning: Express doing something in advance or for future convenience (casual form of ～ておく).
Formation: Verb-て form + とく (e.g., 食べておく→食べとく, 読んでおく→読んどく)
Example (Japanese): 夜遅くなるから、今晩のご飯を作っとく。
Example (Romaji): Yoru osoku naru kara, konban no gohan wo tsukutoku.
Example (English): Since it will be late tonight, I'll prepare dinner in advance.

Meaning: Expresses a contrast or unexpected outcome; 'however', 'but', 'even though'.
Formation: Phrase 1 (expected situation) + ところが + Phrase 2 (unexpected result)
Example (Japanese): 彼はいつも遅刻するところが、今日は早く来ました。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa itsumo chikoku suru tokoro ga, kyou wa hayaku kimashita.
Example (English): He's always late, but today he arrived early.

Meaning: Expresses a near miss or a situation that almost happened; 'was just about to', 'almost', 'nearly'.
Formation: Verb (dictionary form or ている form) + ところだった
Example (Japanese): もう少しで遅れるところだった。
Example (Romaji): Mou sukoshi de okureru tokoro datta.
Example (English): I was just about to be late.

Meaning: Used for changing the topic or bringing up a new topic; 'by the way', 'speaking of'.
Formation: ところで + new topic or question
Example (Japanese): ところで、昨日の宿題はもう終わりましたか？
Example (Romaji): Tokorode, kinou no shukudai wa mou owari mashita ka?
Example (English): By the way, did you finish yesterday's homework?

Meaning: Express a hypothetical situation; 'if', 'suppose', 'assuming'.
Formation: Verb-casual + としたら, い-Adjective + としたら, な-Adjective + だとしたら, Noun + だとしたら
Example (Japanese): 明日雨が降るとしたら、傘を持って行きましょう。
Example (Romaji): Ashita ame ga furu to shitara, kasa wo motte ikimashou.
Example (English): If it rains tomorrow, let's bring an umbrella.

Meaning: Indicates a role, capacity, or identity; 'as', 'in the capacity of'.
Formation: Verb-casual + として, い-Adjective + として, な-Adjective + だとして, Noun + だとして
Example (Japanese): 彼は弁護士として働いています。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa bengoshi to shite hataraite imasu.
Example (English): He is working as a lawyer.

Meaning: Expresses the extent of something or emphasizes the degree of a condition or situation.
Formation: どんなに + Adjective + ことか, どんなに + Verb + ことか
Example (Japanese): どんなに疲れたことか、言葉では表せません。
Example (Romaji): Donna ni tsukareta koto ka, kotoba de wa arawasemasen.
Example (English): I can't put into words how tired I am.

Grammar Point: どんなに～ても (donna ni ~ temo)
Meaning: Expresses 'no matter how much' or 'even if'; emphasizes the degree of a situation.
Formation: どんなに + Verb-てform + も, どんなに + い-Adjective-てform + も, どんなに + な-Adjective + でも
Example (Japanese): どんなに勉強しても、まだわからないことがある。
Example (Romaji): Donna ni benkyou shite mo, mada wakaranai koto ga aru.
Example (English): No matter how much I study, there are still things I don't understand.

Grammar Point: ～ないことはない (〜nai koto wa nai)
Meaning: Express the idea that 'it's not that it's impossible' or 'it's not that it cannot be done'.
Formation: Verb-ない form + ことはない
Example (Japanese): この問題を解けないことはないが、時間がかかりそうだ。
Example (Romaji): Kono mondai wo tokenai koto wa nai ga, jikan ga kakari sou da.
Example (English): It's not that I can't solve this problem, but it seems like it will take time.

Meaning: Express a condition; 'if... not', 'unless', 'must'.
Formation: Verb-negative form + ないと
Example (Japanese): 朝食を食べないと、お腹が空く。
Example (Romaji): Asa gohan wo tabenai to, onaka ga suku.
Example (English): If I don't eat breakfast, I will be hungry.

Meaning: Express a reason or explanation; 'because', 'the reason is'.
Formation: Sentence/Statement + なぜなら + Reason + から/だから
Example (Japanese): このレストランが大好きだ。なぜなら料理が美味しいから。
Example (Romaji): Kono resutoran ga daisuki da. Nazenara ryouri ga oishii kara.
Example (English): I love this restaurant because the food is delicious.

Meaning: Indicates a non-exhaustive list of examples; 'such as', 'things like', 'among others'.
Formation: Noun + など
Example (Japanese): 魚、果物などを市場で買いました。
Example (Romaji): Sakana, kudamono nado wo ichiba de kaimashita.
Example (English): I bought fish, fruits, and such at the market.

Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'things like' or 'something like', used for listing examples or downplaying something.
Formation: Noun + なんか, Verb-casual + なんか, い-Adjective + なんか, な-Adjective + なんか
Example (Japanese): お金なんかいらない。
Example (Romaji): Okane nanka iranai.
Example (English): I don't need money or anything like that.

Meaning: Indicates the place, time, or context where an action or situation takes place.
Formation: Noun (Place/Time/Context) + において
Example (Japanese): 日本において、お盆は家族が集まる大切な行事です。
Example (Romaji): Nihon ni oite, obon wa kazoku ga atsumaru taisetsu na gyouji desu.
Example (English): In Japan, Obon is an important event where families gather.

Meaning: Expresses 'in place of', 'on behalf of', or 'instead of'.
Formation: Noun + にかわって
Example (Japanese): 彼が病気なので、私が会議に出席することになりました。私が彼にかわって会議に出席します。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga byouki na no de, watashi ga kaigi ni shusseki suru koto ni narimashita. Watashi ga kare ni kawatte kaigi ni shusseki shimasu.
Example (English): He is sick, so I will attend the meeting. I will attend the meeting on his behalf.

Meaning: Express 'for' or 'considering' in the sense of being unusual or unexpected.
Formation: Verb-casual + にしては, い-Adjective + にしては, な-Adjective + にしては, Noun + にしては
Example (Japanese): 彼女は初心者にしては、上手に水泳ができる。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa shoshinsha ni shite wa, jouzu ni suiei ga dekiru.
Example (English): Considering she is a beginner, she can swim well.

Meaning: Expresses 'even if', 'no matter', 'regardless of'.
Formation: Verb-casual + にしても, い-Adjective + にしても, な-Adjective + だにしても, Noun + だにしても
Example (Japanese): 雨が降るにしても、学校へ行かなければなりません。
Example (Romaji): Ame ga furu ni shitemo, gakkou e ikanakereba narimasen.
Example (English): Even if it rains, I have to go to school.

Meaning: Expressing 'about', 'concerning', or 'regarding'.
Formation: Noun + について
Example (Japanese): 日本の文化について学びたいです。
Example (Romaji): Nihon no bunka ni tsuite manabitai desu.
Example (English): I want to learn about Japanese culture.

Meaning: Express the meaning 'for', 'to', 'from the perspective of'.
Formation: Noun (person or thing) + にとって + Verb/Adjective/Noun
Example (Japanese): 私にとって、健康は一番大切なことです。
Example (Romaji): Watashi ni totte, kenkou wa ichiban taisetsu na koto desu.
Example (English): For me, health is the most important thing.

Meaning: Indicates the reason or cause, difference depending on a factor, or methods used.
Formation: Verb-casual + によって, い-Adjective + によって, な-Adjective + によって, Noun + によって
Example (Japanese): その事故は悪天候によって引き起こされた。
Example (Romaji): Sono jiko wa akutenkou ni yotte hikiokosareta.
Example (English): The accident was caused by bad weather.

Meaning: Means 'according to', 'based on' or 'by'.
Formation: Noun + によれば
Example (Japanese): 天気予報によれば、明日は晴れるでしょう。
Example (Romaji): Tenki yohou ni yoreba, ashita wa hareru deshou.
Example (English): According to the weather forecast, it will be sunny tomorrow.

Meaning: Indicates a target or contrast; 'toward', 'against', 'in contrast to', 'in response to'.
Formation: Verb-casual + に対して, い-Adjective + に対して, な-Adjective + に対して, Noun + に対して
Example (Japanese): 子供たちに対して、親は常にやさしくあるべきです。
Example (Romaji): Kodomotachi ni taishite, oya wa tsune ni yasashiku aru beki desu.
Example (English): Parents should always be kind towards their children.

Meaning: Comparing to; in comparison with; as opposed to.
Formation: Verb-casual + に比べて, い-Adjective + に比べて, な-Adjective + だ/である + に比べて, Noun + だ/である + に比べて
Example (Japanese): 夏に比べて、冬は寒いです。
Example (Romaji): Natsu ni kurabete, fuyu wa samui desu.
Example (English): Winter is cold compared to summer.

Meaning: Regarding, concerning, about, with respect to.
Formation: Noun + に関して
Example (Japanese): 健康に関して気を付けることが大切です。
Example (Romaji): Kenkou ni kanshite ki wo tsukeru koto ga taisetsu desu.
Example (English): It is important to be careful regarding health.

Meaning: Indicates possession, attribution, or connection between two nouns.
Formation: Noun1 + の + Noun2
Example (Japanese): これは私の傘です。
Example (Romaji): Kore wa watashi no kasa desu.
Example (English): This is my umbrella.

Meaning: Expresses 'only', 'nothing but', 'always', 'just'.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + ばかり, い-Adjective + ばかり, な-Adjective + ばかり, Noun + ばかり
Example (Japanese): 彼はゲームばかりしている。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa geemu bakari shite iru.
Example (English): He is always playing games.

Meaning: Not only... but also; more than just; not just
Formation: Verb-casual + ばかりか/も, い-Adjective + ばかりか/も, な-Adjective + だ + ばかりか/も, Noun + だ + ばかりか/も
Example (Japanese): 彼女は英語ばかりか、フランス語も話せます。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa eigo bakarika, furansugo mo hanasemasu.
Example (English): Not only can she speak English, but she can also speak French.

Meaning: Expresses an expectation, 'should' or 'it is supposed to'.
Formation: Verb-casual + はずだ, い-Adjective + はずだ, な-Adjective + なはずだ, Noun + のはずだ
Example (Japanese): 彼はもう着いたはずだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa mou tsuita hazu da.
Example (English): He should have arrived by now.

Meaning: Expresses regret or dissatisfaction; 'if only', 'wish'.
Formation: Verb-ば form + ～のに, い-Adjective-ば form + ～のに, な-Adjective + であれば + ～のに, Noun + であれば + ～のに
Example (Japanese): もっと早く来れば、電車に間に合ったのに。
Example (Romaji): Motto hayaku kureba, densha ni maniatta noni.
Example (English): If only I had come earlier, I would have made it to the train.

Meaning: Expresses 'the more ~, the more ~'; a proportional relationship between two phrases.
Formation: Verb-casual + ば + Verb-casual + ほど, い-Adjective + ば + い-Adjective + ほど, な-Adjective + であれば + な-Adjective + ほど
Example (Japanese): 早く起きれば起きるほど、時間がたくさんある。
Example (Romaji): Hayaku okireba okiru hodo, jikan ga takusan aru.
Example (English): The earlier you wake up, the more time you have.

Meaning: Used for emphasizing that not only one thing but also another thing is included. It means 'not only... but also' or 'of course... and...'.
Formation: Noun1 + はもちろん + Noun2 + も
Example (Japanese): 彼は数学はもちろん、英語も得意です。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa suugaku wa mochiron, eigo mo tokui desu.
Example (English): Not only is he good at math, but he is also good at English.

Meaning: Express a sense of regret; 'I wish', 'it would have been better if'.
Formation: Verb-ば-form + よかった, い-Adjective-く + ばよかった, な-Adjective + ならよかった
Example (Japanese): もっと早く起きればよかった。
Example (Romaji): Motto hayaku okireba yokatta.
Example (English): I wish I had woken up earlier.

Meaning: Pretending or acting as if; 'pretend', 'act like'.
Formation: Verb (dictionary form) + ふりをする, い-Adjective + ふりをする, な-Adjective + ふりをする, Noun + ふりをする
Example (Japanese): 彼は知らないふりをしました。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa shiranai furi wo shimashita.
Example (English): He pretended not to know.

Meaning: Express an obligation or something that should be done (mainly with verbs).
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + べきだ
Example (Japanese): 勉強するべきだ。
Example (Romaji): Benkyou suru beki da.
Example (English): You should study.

Meaning: Expresses the degree or extent; 'about', 'to the extent', 'as much as'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ほど, い-Adjective + ほど, な-Adjective + ほど, Noun + ほど
Example (Japanese): 彼女は私ほど速く走ることができません。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa watashi hodo hayaku hashiru koto ga dekimasen.
Example (English): She cannot run as fast as me.

Meaning: Used to express a wish or hope for oneself or someone else.
Formation: Verb-ます form, remove final る + ように
Example (Japanese): 明日のテストで良い点をとりますように。
Example (Romaji): Ashita no tesuto de ii ten wo torimasu you ni.
Example (English): I hope I get good grades on tomorrow's test.

Meaning: Completely not; not at all.
Formation: まったく + Verb-negative, まったく + い-Adjective-negative, まったく + な-Adjective-negative
Example (Japanese): 彼は、まったく覚えていない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa, mattaku oboete inai.
Example (English): He doesn't remember at all.

Meaning: Express 'until', 'up to', or 'as far as' to indicate the end point of an action or range.
Formation: Verb-casual + まで, い-Adjective + まで, な-Adjective + まで, Noun + まで
Example (Japanese): 10時まで働きます。
Example (Romaji): Ju-ji made hatarakimasu.
Example (English): I will work until 10 o'clock.

Meaning: Expresses the state or condition remaining unchanged.
Formation: Verb-ます stem + まま, い-Adjective + まま, な-Adjective + なまま, Noun + のまま
Example (Japanese): 部屋の窓を開けたまま寝ました。
Example (Romaji): Heya no mado wo aketa mama nemashita.
Example (English): I slept with the window of the room open.

Meaning: Used to express a strong resemblance or similarity; 'as if', 'just like', 'as though'.
Formation: まるで + phrase/sentence + よう
Example (Japanese): 彼女はまるで天使のように美しい。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa maru de tenshi no you ni utsukushii.
Example (English): She is as beautiful as an angel.

Meaning: A grammar structure used to express the action of trying or attempting something to see what happens.
Formation: Verb-て form + みる
Example (Japanese): 彼は走ってみたが、まだ膝が痛いと感じた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa hashitte mita ga, mada hiza ga itai to kanjita.
Example (English): He tried running, but he still felt pain in his knee.

Meaning: Express similarity or appearance; 'like', 'seems', 'looks'.
Formation: Verb-casual + みたいだ, い-Adjective + みたいだ, な-Adjective + みたいだ, Noun + みたいだ
Example (Japanese): 彼は怒っているみたいだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa okotte iru mitai da.
Example (English): He seems to be angry.

Meaning: Used to express that something rarely, hardly ever or seldom happens.
Formation: めったに + Verb[ない-form] / めったに + い-Adjective[ない-form] / めったに + な-Adjective[じゃない/ではない-form]
Example (Japanese): 彼はめったに外食しない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa metta ni gaishoku shinai.
Example (English): He hardly ever eats out.

Meaning: Expresses the rarity of an action, event or state; 'hardly', 'rarely', 'seldom'.
Formation: Verb-negative + めったにない, い-Adjective-negative + めったにない, な-Adjective-negative + めったにない, Noun-negative + めったにない
Example (Japanese): この町では雪が降ることはめったにない。
Example (Romaji): Kono machi de wa yuki ga furu koto wa metta ni nai.
Example (English): It hardly ever snows in this town.

Grammar Point: もしかすると〜かもしれない (moshikasuru to 〜kamoshirenai)
Meaning: Express the possibility of something; 'maybe', 'perhaps', 'might'.
Formation: もしかすると + Sentence + かもしれない
Example (Japanese): もしかすると彼は遅刻するかもしれない。
Example (Romaji): Moshikasuru to kare wa chikoku suru kamoshirenai.
Example (English): Maybe he might be late.

Meaning: Express a hypothetical condition, 'if' or 'in case'.
Formation: もし + Verb-casual past + なら, もし + い-Adjective-casual past + なら, もし + な-Adjective + だったなら, もし + Noun + だったなら
Example (Japanese): もし雨が降ったなら、傘を持って行きましょう。
Example (Romaji): Moshi ame ga futta nara, kasa wo motte ikimashou.
Example (English): If it rains, let's bring an umbrella.

Meaning: Express a hypothetical situation or assumption with the nuance of 'even if'.
Formation: もし + Verb-て form + も / もし + い-Adjective(く) + ても / もし + な-Adjective/Noun + でも
Example (Japanese): もし雨が降っても、ピクニックに行きます。
Example (Romaji): Moshi ame ga futtemo, pikunikku ni ikimasu.
Example (English): Even if it rains, we will go on a picnic.

Meaning: Express a hypothetical condition or situation; 'if', 'in case', 'suppose'.
Formation: Verb-casual + なら, い-Adjective + なら, な-Adjective + なら, Noun + なら
Example (Japanese): もしも明日雨が降ったなら、出かけません。
Example (Romaji): Moshimo ashita ame ga futta nara, dekakemasen.
Example (English): If it rains tomorrow, I won't go out.

Meaning: Not showing any sign or intention to do something.
Formation: Verb-volitional form + としない
Example (Japanese): 彼は勉強しようとしない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa benkyou shiyou to shinai.
Example (English): He doesn't show any sign of trying to study.

Meaning: Expresses the speaker's intention or plan to do something.
Formation: Verb-volitional + と思う
Example (Japanese): 今日は早く寝ようと思います。
Example (Romaji): Kyou wa hayaku neyou to omoimasu.
Example (English): I think I will go to bed early today.

Meaning: Expressing a purpose, a goal or a way of doing something; 'in order to', 'so that', 'like', 'as'
Formation: Verb-casual + ように, い-Adjective + ように, な-Adjective + に, Noun + のように
Example (Japanese): 早く家に帰るように、仕事を急いで終わらせました。
Example (Romaji): Hayaku ie ni kaeru you ni, shigoto wo isoide owarasemashita.
Example (English): In order to get home early, I hurried to finish my work.

Grammar Point: ～ようにしましょう (〜you ni shimashou)
Meaning: A suggestion to make an effort or try to do something; 'let's try to', 'let's make sure to'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ようにしましょう / Verb-negative form + ようにしましょう
Example (Japanese): 毎日運動するようにしましょう。
Example (Romaji): Mainichi undou suru you ni shimashou.
Example (English): Let's try to exercise every day.

Meaning: Express an event or state that became possible; 'became able to', 'started to', 'now can'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ようになった
Example (Japanese): 彼は料理を作るようになった。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa ryouri wo tsukuru you ni natta.
Example (English): He became able to cook.

Meaning: To convey a message, instruction or request to someone; 'to tell (someone) to', 'to say to (someone)'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ように言う / Verb-nai form + ように言う
Example (Japanese): 先生は私にもっと勉強するように言った。
Example (Romaji): Sensei wa watashi ni motto benkyou suru you ni itta.
Example (English): The teacher told me to study more.

Meaning: Expresses hearsay; 'I heard', 'it seems', 'apparently'.
Formation: Verb-casual + らしい, い-Adjective + らしい, な-Adjective + だらしい, Noun + だらしい
Example (Japanese): 彼はインフルエンザらしい。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa infuruenza rashii.
Example (English): Apparently, he has the flu.

Meaning: Express a passive action, 'was/were', 'has/have been'.
Formation: Verb (passive form, past tense) + られた
Example (Japanese): この本はたくさんの人に読まれた。
Example (Romaji): Kono hon wa takusan no hito ni yomareta.
Example (English): This book was read by many people.

Meaning: Expresses a continuing action or a resulting state; 'is ~ing', 'has been', 'has'.
Formation: Verb-て form + いる
Example (Japanese): 窓が開けられている。
Example (Romaji): Mado ga akerarete iru.
Example (English): The window is open (someone opened it and it remains open).

Meaning: Expresses that something is impossible or unreasonable; 'there's no way', 'can't be'.
Formation: Verb-casual + わけがない, い-Adjective + わけがない, な-Adjective + なわけがない, Noun + のわけがない
Example (Japanese): 彼がそんなことを言うわけがない。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga sonna koto wo iu wake ga nai.
Example (English): There's no way he would say something like that.

Meaning: Expresses a logical conclusion or reason based on information; 'that's why', 'no wonder', 'it means'.
Formation: Verb-casual + わけだ, い-Adjective + わけだ, な-Adjective + なわけだ, Noun + のわけだ
Example (Japanese): 彼は風邪を引いている。だから、声がかすれているわけだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kaze wo hiite iru. Dakara, koe ga kasurete iru wake da.
Example (English): He has a cold. That's why his voice is hoarse.

Meaning: Denies a general assumption; 'it does not mean that', 'it's not the case'.
Formation: Verb-casual + わけではない, い-Adjective + わけではない, な-Adjective + だわけではない, Noun + だわけではない
Example (Japanese): 彼が忙しいからといって、友達がいないわけではない。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga isogashii kara to itte, tomodachi ga inai wake dewa nai.
Example (English): Just because he's busy doesn't mean he has no friends.

Grammar Point: ～わけにはいかない (〜wake ni wa ikanai)
Meaning: Expresses that something cannot be allowed or permitted due to social/moral obligations.
Formation: Verb-casual + わけにはいかない
Example (Japanese): こんなところで寝るわけにはいかない。
Example (Romaji): Konna tokoro de neru wake ni wa ikanai.
Example (English): I can't possibly sleep in a place like this.

Meaning: Expresses contrast between expectation and reality; 'despite', 'considering', 'even though'.
Formation: Verb-casual + わりには, い-Adjective + わりには, な-Adjective + だわりには, Noun + だわりには
Example (Japanese): 彼はあまり勉強しないわりには、テストの点数が高いです。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa amari benkyou shinai wari ni wa, tesuto no tensuu ga takai desu.
Example (English): Despite not studying much, he gets high scores on tests.

Meaning: Conveys information heard from someone else; 'I heard', 'They said'.
Formation: Verb-casual + んだって, い-Adjective + んだって, な-Adjective + なんだって, Noun + なんだって
Example (Japanese): 彼は東京に行くんだって。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa Toukyou ni iku n datte.
Example (English): I heard he's going to Tokyo.

Meaning: Used to convey a sense of justification; 'because', 'that's why', 'it's just that'.
Formation: Verb-casual + んだもん, い-Adjective + んだもん, な-Adjective + なんだもん, Noun + なんだもん
Example (Japanese): 遅れたんだもん、ごめん。
Example (Romaji): Okureta nda mon, gomen.
Example (English): I was late, that's why I'm sorry.

Meaning: Indicates to finish doing something completely.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + 上げる
Example (Japanese): レポートを書き上げるまで、寝られません。
Example (Romaji): Repooto o kakiageru made, neraremasen.
Example (English): I cannot sleep until I finish writing the report.

Meaning: Expresses inability to completely finish or do something.
Formation: Verb-stem + 切れない
Example (Japanese): この本を一晩で読み切れない。
Example (Romaji): Kono hon wo hitoban de yomikirenai.
Example (English): I cannot finish reading this book in one night.

Grammar Point: 必ずしも～とは限らない (kanarazushimo ～ towa kagiranai)
Meaning: Not necessarily; not always.
Formation: 必ずしも + Statement + とは限らない
Example (Japanese): 高いものが必ずしも良いとは限らない。
Example (Romaji): Takai mono ga kanarazushimo yoi to wa kagiranai.
Example (English): Expensive things are not necessarily better.

Meaning: In the middle of / while doing something.
Formation: Verb-て form + いる + 最中に, Noun + の + 最中に
Example (Japanese): 昼寝をしている最中に電話が鳴った。
Example (Romaji): Hirune o shiteiru saichuu ni denwa ga natta.
Example (English): The phone rang while I was taking a nap.

Meaning: Express 'never', 'by no means', or 'not at all' when negating a statement.
Formation: 決して + Verb (negative form)
Example (Japanese): 彼は決して遅刻しない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kesshite chikoku shinai.
Example (English): He never arrives late.

Grammar Point: A あるいは B (A aruiwa B)
Meaning: Indicates alternatives; 'A or B', 'either A or B'.
Formation: Phrase A + あるいは + Phrase B
Example (Japanese): 今日は映画を見るあるいはショッピングをする予定です。
Example (Romaji): Kyou wa eiga wo miru aruiwa shoppingu wo suru yotei desu.
Example (English): Today, I plan to either watch a movie or go shopping.

Meaning: Expresses that in addition to A, there is also B; 'moreover', 'besides', 'not only', 'but also'.
Formation: Sentence A + おまけに  + Sentence B
Example (Japanese): 彼は遅刻した。おまけに宿題も忘れた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa chikoku shita. Omake ni shukudai mo wasureta.
Example (English): He was late. Moreover, he forgot his homework.

Meaning: Indicates a sudden change or shift in the topic or situation; 'now then', 'well', 'so'.
Formation: A + さて + B
Example (Japanese): 今日の仕事が終わった。さて、これから帰るか。
Example (Romaji): Kyou no shigoto ga owatta. Sate, kore kara kaeru ka.
Example (English): Today's work is done. Now then, shall we go home?

Meaning: Expressing additional information; 'moreover', 'besides', 'furthermore'.
Formation: Statement A + 。しかも + Statement B。
Example (Japanese): この料理は美味しいです。しかも、安いです。
Example (Romaji): Kono ryouri wa oishii desu. Shikamo, yasui desu.
Example (English): This dish is delicious. Moreover, it is cheap.

Grammar Point: A。したがって B。(A. Shitagatte B.)
Meaning: Express a cause-and-effect relationship; 'therefore', 'consequently', 'so'.
Formation: A + したがって + B
Example (Japanese): 今日は雨が降っています。したがって、傘を持って行きましょう。
Example (Romaji): Kyou wa ame ga futteimasu. Shitagatte, kasa wo motte ikimashou.
Example (English): It is raining today. Therefore, let's bring an umbrella.

Grammar Point: A すなわち B。 (A sunawachi B)
Meaning: Express that A is equivalent to B; 'in other words', 'namely', 'that is to say'.
Formation: Phrase A + すなわち + Phrase B
Example (Japanese): 私は立派な成果を出したい、すなわち、成功したいのです。
Example (Romaji): Watashi wa rippana seika wo dashitai, sunawachi, seikou shitai no desu.
Example (English): I want to achieve great results, in other words, I want to succeed.

Meaning: Indicates that when action A is done, action or event B follows; 'then', 'when', 'if'.
Formation: A (Sentence) + すると + B (Sentence)
Example (Japanese): 電話をかけると、彼女が出ました。
Example (Romaji): Denwa wo kakeru to, kanojo ga demashita.
Example (English): When I made the phone call, she answered.

Meaning: Recalling something related to A; 'speaking of which', 'by the way', 'now that you mention it'.
Formation: A + そういえば + B
Example (Japanese): 映画。そういえば、彼は映画館で働いているんだ。
Example (Romaji): Eiga. Souieba, kare wa eigakan de hataraite irun da.
Example (English): Movies. Speaking of which, he works at a movie theater.

Meaning: Expresses 'therefore' or 'because of that'.
Formation: A + そこで + B
Example (Japanese): 明日は試験があります。そこで今晩勉強しようと思います。
Example (Romaji): Ashita wa shiken ga arimasu. Soko de konban benkyou shiyou to omoimasu.
Example (English): There is an exam tomorrow. Therefore, I plan to study tonight.

Meaning: Expressing 'that's exactly what A is; in other words, B'.
Formation: A (Statement)。それが B (Restatement or explanation of A)。
Example (Japanese): 彼は勉強ができる。それが天才というものだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa benkyou ga dekiru. Sore ga tensai to iu mono da.
Example (English): He can study well. That's what you call a genius.

Meaning: Express a sequence of events or cause-and-effect; 'and then', 'so', 'because of that'.
Formation: Sentence A +。それで+ Sentence B。
Example (Japanese): 昨日は雨が降っていた。それで公園に行かなかった。
Example (Romaji): Kinou wa ame ga futte ita. Sore de kouen ni ikanakatta.
Example (English): It was raining yesterday. So, I didn't go to the park.

Meaning: Expresses 'even so', 'nevertheless', 'still', or 'but'; used to contrast two statements.
Formation: A (situation) + 。それでも + B (action or thought)
Example (Japanese): 今日は日曜日です。それでも、仕事に行かなければなりません。
Example (Romaji): Kyou wa nichiyoubi desu. Sore demo, shigoto ni ikanakereba narimasen.
Example (English): Today is Sunday. Nevertheless, I have to go to work.

Meaning: Express contrast or a contradiction between two situations or facts; 'even though', 'despite', 'but still'.
Formation: A。それなのに B。
Example (Japanese): 彼は頭がいい。それなのに、試験に落ちた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa atama ga ii. Sore nanoni, shiken ni ochita.
Example (English): He is smart. Despite that, he failed the exam.

Grammar Point: A。それなら B。(A. Sore nara B.)
Meaning: Express 'if that's the case, then'; used to show a logical consequence or decision based on a given situation.
Formation: Situation A (sentence) + 。それなら + Situation B (sentence)
Example (Japanese): 試験が近い。それなら、もっと勉強しなければならない。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ga chikai. Sore nara, motto benkyou shinakereba naranai.
Example (English): The exam is coming soon. If that's the case, I must study more.

Grammar Point: A それはそうと B。 (A Sore wa sou to B)
Meaning: Changing the topic; 'by the way', 'speaking of which'.
Formation: Sentence A + それはそうと + Sentence B
Example (Japanese): それはそうと、今日の天気はいいですね。
Example (Romaji): Sore wa sou to, kyou no tenki wa ii desu ne.
Example (English): By the way, the weather is nice today, isn't it?

Meaning: Expresses contrasting ideas or statements; 'but', 'however'.
Formation: Sentence A + だが + Sentence B
Example (Japanese): このレストランは値段が高い。だが、味はとてもいい。
Example (Romaji): Kono resutoran wa nedan ga takai. Daga, aji wa totemo ii.
Example (English): This restaurant is expensive. But, the taste is very good.

Meaning: Express contrast between two situations; 'although', 'but', 'however'.
Formation: Sentence A + ただ + Sentence B
Example (Japanese): 彼は頭がいい。ただ、努力はあまりしない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa atama ga ii. Tada, doryoku wa amari shinai.
Example (English): He is smart; however, he doesn't make much effort.

Meaning: Adding a condition or exception to a statement; 'however', 'provided that', 'but only if'.
Formation: Statement A + ただし + Condition B
Example (Japanese): この部屋を使ってもいいです。ただし、使った後で掃除してください。
Example (Romaji): Kono heya wo tsukatte mo ii desu. Tadashi, tsukatta ato de souji shite kudasai.
Example (English): You can use this room. However, please clean up after you use it.

Meaning: Used to give a reason, express cause or bring up a topic; 'because', 'since', 'it's just that'.
Formation: Verb-casual + だって、い-Adjective + だって、な-Adjective + だって、Noun + だって
Example (Japanese): 暇だって、映画を見に行こうよ。
Example (Romaji): Hima datte, eiga wo mi ni ikou yo.
Example (English): Since we are free, let's go watch a movie.

Grammar Point: A。ちなみに B。(A. Chinamini B.)
Meaning: Used to give additional information about the topic; 'by the way', 'incidentally'.
Formation: A。ちなみに B。
Example (Japanese): 今日は授業がありません。ちなみに、明日も休みです。
Example (Romaji): Kyou wa jugyou ga arimasen. Chinamini, asu mo yasumi desu.
Example (English): There's no class today. By the way, tomorrow is also a day off.

Grammar Point: A。ということは B。 (A. To iu koto wa B.)
Meaning: Expresses the meaning 'if A, that means B' or 'A implies B'.
Formation: A + ということは + B
Example (Japanese): 彼女が泣いている。ということは何か悲しいことがあったに違いない。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo ga naite iru. To iu koto wa nanika kanashii koto ga atta ni chigainai.
Example (English): She is crying. That means something sad must have happened.

Grammar Point: A。というのは B。(Toiu no wa~)
Meaning: Used to give an explanation or provide additional information for A; 'that is to say', 'in other words'.
Formation: [Statement A]。というのは、[Statement B]。
Example (Japanese): 彼は非常に疲れています。というのは、昨夜、車で遠くまで行ってきたためです。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa hijou ni tsukareteimasu. To iu no wa, sakuya, kuruma de tooku made itte kita tame desu.
Example (English): He is very tired. That is to say, because he went far by car last night.

Meaning: Provides additional information; 'moreover', 'besides', 'in addition'.
Formation: A (sentence) + なお + B (sentence)
Example (Japanese): 明日は休みです。なお、月曜日も休みです。
Example (Romaji): Ashita wa yasumi desu. Nao, getsuyoubi mo yasumi desu.
Example (English): Tomorrow is a holiday. Moreover, Monday is also a holiday.

Meaning: Express contrasting opinions or facts; 'although', 'but', 'however'.
Formation: Clause A + もっとも + Clause B
Example (Japanese): 彼は頭がいい。もっとも、勉強も大切だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa atama ga ii. Mottomo, benkyou mo taisetsu da.
Example (English): He is smart. However, studying is also important.

Grammar Point: A。要するに B。(A. Yousuru ni B.)
Meaning: Expressing 'in short', 'in a nutshell', or 'to sum up' when restating or summarizing A as B.
Formation: A。要するに B。
Example (Japanese): このプロジェクトは成功しました。要するに、私たちのチームは素晴らしい仕事をしました。
Example (Romaji): Kono purojekuto wa seikou shimashita. Yousuru ni, watashitachi no chiimu wa subarashii shigoto o shimashita.
Example (English): This project was successful. In short, our team did a great job.

Meaning: Indicates the reason, cause, or condition for something; 'due to', 'regarding', 'per'.
Formation: Noun + につき
Example (Japanese): 試験につき、今日は静かにしてください。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ni tsuki, kyou wa shizuka ni shite kudasai.
Example (English): Due to the exam, please be quiet today.

Meaning: Expresses location or means; 'at', 'in', 'by', 'with'.
Formation: Noun + にて
Example (Japanese): 駅前広場にてイベントが開催されます。
Example (Romaji): Ekimae hiroba nite ibento ga kaisai saremasu.
Example (English): An event will be held at the station square.

Grammar Point: Noun の ことだから (Noun no koto dakara)
Meaning: Used to provide a reason or explanation based on one's knowledge about the noun; 'since', 'because', 'knowing'.
Formation: Noun + のことだから
Example (Japanese): 料理が得意な彼のことだから、美味しい料理を作ってくれるでしょう。
Example (Romaji): Ryouri ga tokui na kare no koto dakara, oishii ryouri wo tsukutte kureru deshou.
Example (English): Since he’s good at cooking, he’ll probably make delicious food.

Grammar Point: Noun を はじめ (Noun wo hajime)
Meaning: Meaning 'starting with', 'including', 'not only... but also'.
Formation: Noun + をはじめ
Example (Japanese): 日本料理をはじめ、さまざまな料理がこのレストランで楽しめます。
Example (Romaji): Nihon ryouri wo hajime, samazama na ryouri ga kono resutoran de tanoshimemasu.
Example (English): You can enjoy various dishes in this restaurant, starting with Japanese cuisine.

Grammar Point: Noun を はじめとして (Noun wo hajime to shite)
Meaning: Expresses 'starting with', 'beginning with', or 'including'.
Formation: Noun + をはじめとして
Example (Japanese): 東京をはじめとして、日本にはたくさんの観光スポットがあります。
Example (Romaji): Tōkyō o hajime to shite, Nihon ni wa takusan no kankō supotto ga arimasu.
Example (English): There are many tourist spots in Japan, starting with Tokyo.

Grammar Point: Noun を はじめとする Noun (Noun o hajime to suru Noun)
Meaning: Indicates a representative example of a group; 'starting with', 'including', 'such as'.
Formation: Noun1 を はじめとする Noun2
Example (Japanese): 彼はフランス語をはじめとする外国語が話せる。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa furansugo o hajime to suru gaikokugo ga hanaseru.
Example (English): He can speak foreign languages, starting with French.

Grammar Point: Noun を めぐって (Noun wo megutte)
Meaning: Concerning; with regard to; about
Formation: Noun + を + めぐって
Example (Japanese): 環境問題をめぐって、多くの議論が行われています。
Example (Romaji): Kankyō mondai o megutte, ōku no giron ga okonawarete imasu.
Example (English): Many discussions are held concerning environmental issues.

Grammar Point: Noun を めぐる Noun (Noun o meguru Noun)
Meaning: Indicate a situation or event revolving around a particular noun; 'concerning', 'regarding', 'pertaining to'.
Formation: Noun1 + を + めぐる + Noun2
Example (Japanese): この事件をめぐる議論が続いています。
Example (Romaji): Kono jiken o meguru giron ga tsudzuite imasu.
Example (English): The debate concerning this incident continues.

Grammar Point: Noun を もとに (Noun o moto ni)
Meaning: Based on; drawing from; using as a reference.
Formation: Noun + をもとに
Example (Japanese): この映画は実話をもとに作られました。
Example (Romaji): Kono eiga wa jitsuwa o moto ni tsukuraremashita.
Example (English): This movie was made based on a true story.

Grammar Point: Noun を もとにして (Noun wo moto ni shite)
Meaning: Based on; using; utilizing.
Formation: Noun + をもとにして
Example (Japanese): 彼の意見をもとにして、計画を変更しました。
Example (Romaji): Kare no iken o moto ni shite, keikaku o henkō shimashita.
Example (English): Based on his opinion, we changed the plan.

Meaning: Means 'without doing', 'not doing', or 'without happening'.
Formation: Verb-stem + ことなく
Example (Japanese): 彼女は泣くことなく帰ってしまいました。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa naku koto naku kaette shimaimashita.
Example (English): She went home without crying.

Grammar Point: Verb ないことには Verb ない (~nai koto ni wa ~ nai)
Meaning: Express that something cannot be done without meeting a certain condition.
Formation: Verb-ない + ことには + Verb-ない
Example (Japanese): 薬を飲まないことには、病気が治らない。
Example (Romaji): Kusuri o nomanai koto ni wa, byōki ga naoranai.
Example (English): Unless you take the medicine, the illness won't get better.

Meaning: Expresses the outcome of a series of actions or events; 'in the end', 'finally', 'after'.
Formation: Verb-た + あげく / Noun + の + あげく
Example (Japanese): 長い時間待ったあげく、電車が来なかった。
Example (Romaji): Nagai jikan matta ageku, densha ga konakatta.
Example (English): After waiting a long time, in the end, the train didn't come.

Meaning: Expresses the result of doing something excessively or beyond a certain point.
Formation: Verb-ます stem + あまり, い-Adjective + あまり, な-Adjective + のあまり, Noun + のあまり
Example (Japanese): 昨日は疲れすぎたあまり、朝まで眠り続けました。
Example (Romaji): Kinō wa tsukare-sugita amari, asa made nemuri tsuzukemashita.
Example (English): Yesterday, I was so tired that I slept until morning.

Meaning: Expresses doing something while a certain condition still holds; 'while', 'before', 'as long as'.
Formation: Verb-casual + うちに, い-Adjective + うちに, な-Adjective + なうちに, Noun + のうちに
Example (Japanese): 元気なうちに、旅行を楽しんでください。
Example (Romaji): Genki na uchi ni, ryokō o tanoshinde kudasai.
Example (English): Enjoy traveling while you are healthy.

Meaning: Expresses 'worth doing' for verbs.
Formation: Verb-stem + がい
Example (Japanese): この本は読みがいがあります。
Example (Romaji): Kono hon wa yomi-gai ga arimasu.
Example (English): This book is worth reading.

Meaning: Used to express that an effort is worth it or has value; 'to be worth the effort' or 'to pay off'.
Formation: Verb-past + かいがあって / Noun + の + かいがあって
Example (Japanese): 毎日勉強したかいがあって、テストに合格しました。
Example (Romaji): Mainichi benkyō shita kai ga atte, tesuto ni gōkaku shimashita.
Example (English): Studying every day paid off—I passed the test.

Meaning: Expresses the meaning of 'without worth', 'in vain', 'fruitless'.
Formation: Verb-た + かいもなく / Noun + の + かいもなく
Example (Japanese): 長い間苦労したかいもなく、失敗してしまった。
Example (Romaji): Nagai aida kurō shita kai mo naku, shippai shite shimatta.
Example (English): I struggled for a long time, but in the end, it was all in vain and I failed.

Meaning: Indicates a process or action is 'in progress' or 'halfway'.
Formation: Verb-stem + かける
Example (Japanese): 彼女は食べかけのリンゴを置いて出かけた。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa tabe-kake no ringo o oite dekaketa.
Example (English): She left a partially eaten apple and went out.

Meaning: Expresses that something tends to occur frequently or habitually.
Formation: Verb-ます stem + がち / い-Adjective stem + がち / な-Adjective stem + がち
Example (Japanese): 彼は風邪を引きがちです。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kaze o hiki-gachi desu.
Example (English): He tends to catch colds easily.

Grammar Point: ～か～ないかのうちに (〜ka〜naika no uchi ni)
Meaning: Expresses an action that occurs immediately after another action; 'as soon as', 'no sooner than', 'the moment'.
Formation: Verb-casual + か + Verb-negative form + かのうちに
Example (Japanese): 駅に着くか着かないかのうちに、雨が降り出した。
Example (Romaji): Eki ni tsuku ka tsukanai ka no uchi ni, ame ga furidashita.
Example (English): No sooner had I arrived at the station than it started raining.

Meaning: Express the likelihood of a negative outcome or consequence.
Formation: Verb-stem + かねない
Example (Japanese): 彼はあまりにも無責任で、約束を破りかねない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa amarini mo musekinin de, yakusoku o yaburi-kane nai.
Example (English): He is so irresponsible that he might break his promise.

Meaning: Express inability or impossibility of doing an action (often as a polite refusal).
Formation: Verb-ます stem + かねる
Example (Japanese): その問題は難しいので、私には解決しかねます。
Example (Romaji): Sono mondai wa muzukashii no de, watashi ni wa kaiketsu shi-kanemasu.
Example (English): Since that problem is difficult, I cannot solve it.

Meaning: Express a similarity or comparison; 'as if', 'like', 'as though'.
Formation: Verb-casual + かのようだ, い-Adjective + かのようだ, な-Adjective + であるかのようだ, Noun + であるかのようだ
Example (Japanese): 彼は犬が怖いかのようだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa inu ga kowai ka no you da.
Example (English): He seems as if he is scared of dogs.

Meaning: Used to express a dilemma or indecision between two options or actions.
Formation: Verb-volitional + か + Verb-volitional + まいか, い-Adjective + であるか + い-Adjective + であるまいか, な-Adjective + であるか + な-Adjective + であるまいか, Noun + であるか + Noun + であるまいか
Example (Japanese): このプロジェクトを引き受けようか引き受けまいか、まだ決めていない。
Example (Romaji): Kono purojekuto o hikiukeyou ka hikiukemai ka, mada kimete inai.
Example (English): I haven't decided whether to take on this project or not.

Meaning: Express the emphasis on the reason; 'precisely because', 'it is precisely because'.
Formation: Verb-casual + からこそ, い-Adjective + からこそ, な-Adjective + だからこそ, Noun + だからこそ
Example (Japanese): 失敗したからこそ、成功の意味がわかる。
Example (Romaji): Shippai shita kara koso, seikou no imi ga wakaru.
Example (English): It is precisely because I failed that I understand the meaning of success.

Meaning: Expresses that something is exceptional, unusual, or negative based on a particular aspect or point.
Formation: Noun + からして
Example (Japanese): 彼の顔つきからして、何か悪いことがあったのだろう。
Example (Romaji): Kare no kaotsuki kara shite, nanika warui koto ga atta no darou.
Example (English): From his facial expression, something bad must have happened.

Meaning: Expresses a judgment or evaluation based on a certain standard; 'from this perspective', 'considering', 'judging from'.
Formation: Noun + からすると
Example (Japanese): 経験からすると、この仕事は難しいでしょう。
Example (Romaji): Keiken kara suru to, kono shigoto wa muzukashii deshou.
Example (English): Considering their experience, this job might be difficult.

Meaning: Expresses 'just because...doesn't mean' or 'even though...not necessarily'.
Formation: Verb-casual + からといって, い-Adjective + からといって, な-Adjective + だからといって, Noun + だからといって
Example (Japanese): 雨が降ったからといって、試合が中止になるわけではありません。
Example (Romaji): Ame ga futta kara to itte, shiai ga chuushi ni naru wake de wa arimasen.
Example (English): Just because it rained doesn't mean the game will be canceled.

Meaning: Expresses a range of time, space, or quantities; 'from...to', 'between...and', 'over'.
Formation: Noun 1 + から + Noun 2 + にかけて
Example (Japanese): 午前９時から午後５時にかけて、仕事をしています。
Example (Romaji): Gozen ku-ji kara gogo go-ji ni kakete, shigoto wo shite imasu.
Example (English): I work from 9 in the morning to 5 in the evening.

Meaning: Express a sense of responsibility or determination; 'since', 'now that', 'if'.
Formation: Noun + だ + からには, な-Adjective + だ + からには, い-Adjective + からには, Verb-casual + からには
Example (Japanese): 試験に合格したからには、一所懸命働かなければならない。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ni goukaku shita kara niwa, isshokenmei hatarakanakereba naranai.
Example (English): Since I passed the exam, I have to work hard.

Meaning: Express a perspective or point of view; 'from the standpoint of', 'in terms of', 'from the perspective of'.
Formation: Noun + から見ると
Example (Japanese): 費用から見ると、このプランはお得です。
Example (Romaji): Hiyou kara miru to, kono puran wa otoku desu.
Example (English): In terms of cost, this plan is a good deal.

Meaning: Express a judgment or opinion based on a specific criterion; 'speaking from', 'in terms of', 'from the viewpoint of'.
Formation: Noun + から言うと (common), [Verb-casual / Adjective + から言って] (less common)
Example (Japanese): 値段から言うと、この商品が最もお得です。
Example (Romaji): Nedan kara iuto, kono shouhin ga mottomo otoku desu.
Example (English): Speaking from the viewpoint of price, this product is the best deal.

Meaning: Used to criticize someone for doing something contrary to what one would expect from their nature or situation.
Formation: Verb (casual) + くせに / い-Adjective + くせに / な-Adjective + な(or の) + くせに / Noun + の + くせに
Example (Japanese): 彼はいつも遅刻してくるくせに、自分が待たされるのが嫌いだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa itsumo chikoku shite kuru kuse ni, jibun ga matasareru no ga kirai da.
Example (English): He’s always late, yet he hates being kept waiting.

Meaning: Indicates the reason or basis for something; 'because', 'since', 'due to'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ことから / い-Adjective + ことから / な-Adjective + なことから / Noun + のことから
Example (Japanese): 彼は毎日運動することから、体が丈夫です。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa mainichi undou suru koto kara, karada ga joubu desu.
Example (English): Because he exercises every day, he is physically strong.

Meaning: Used to express feelings or emotions about a situation, action, or outcome.
Formation: Verb-casual + ことに / い-Adjective + ことに / な-Adjective + なことに / Noun + のことに
Example (Japanese): 彼が急に帰国することに驚いた。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga kyuu ni kikoku suru koto ni odoroita.
Example (English): I was surprised that he suddenly returned to his home country.

Grammar Point: ～ことになっている (〜koto ni natte iru)
Meaning: Expresses that something is supposed to be or has been decided (rule, plan, custom).
Formation: Verb-plain form + ことになっている / い-Adjective + ことになっている / な-Adjective + だ + ことになっている / Noun + だ + ことになっている
Example (Japanese): 日本では、左側を運転することになっています。
Example (Romaji): Nihon de wa, hidarigawa o unten suru koto ni natte imasu.
Example (English): In Japan, it is decided that people drive on the left side.

Meaning: Expresses that, as long as a certain condition is met, something else will follow; 'if only', 'provided that'.
Formation: Noun + さえ + Verb-conditional / Verb-ますstem + さえすれば / etc. (varies by part of speech)
Example (Japanese): お金さえあれば、幸せです。
Example (Romaji): Okane sae areba, shiawase desu.
Example (English): As long as I have money, I’m happy.

Meaning: Have no choice but to; cannot help but.
Formation: Verb-ない form (drop ない) + ざるを得ない
Example (Japanese): この仕事は締め切りが近いので、残業せざるを得ない。
Example (Romaji): Kono shigoto wa shimekiri ga chikai no de, zangyou sezaru wo enai.
Example (English): Since the deadline is near, I have no choice but to work overtime.

Grammar Point: ～ずにはいられない (〜zu ni wa irarenai)
Meaning: Cannot help but; cannot resist doing; an irresistible urge.
Formation: Verb-ない form (drop ない) + ずにはいられない
Example (Japanese): この曲を聞くと、歌わずにはいられない。
Example (Romaji): Kono kyoku o kiku to, utawazu ni wa irarenai.
Example (English): When I hear this song, I can’t help but sing.

Meaning: Express the unlikelihood of something happening; 'not likely', 'doesn't seem'.
Formation: Verb-stem + そうにない / い-Adjective (drop い) + そうにない / な-Adjective + そうにない
Example (Japanese): この雨は止みそうにない。
Example (Romaji): Kono ame wa yami sou ni nai.
Example (English): It doesn't seem like this rain will stop.

Grammar Point: ～たかと思ったら (〜ta ka to omottara)
Meaning: Express a sequence of events happening in quick succession; 'as soon as', 'no sooner than'.
Formation: Verb-た form + かと思ったら
Example (Japanese): 電話をかけたかと思ったら、すぐに彼女が出た。
Example (Romaji): Denwa o kaketa ka to omottara, sugu ni kanojo ga deta.
Example (English): No sooner had I called than she picked up.

Meaning: Express 'since then' or 'after'; used to indicate that an action occurred once and has not been repeated or that a state has continued since a certain event or time.
Formation: Verb-past + きり
Example (Japanese): 彼は会社を辞めたきり、連絡がない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kaisha o yameta kiri, renraku ga nai.
Example (English): Ever since he quit the company, there's been no contact.

Meaning: Expresses that something is as expected or deserves its reputation.
Formation: Verb-casual + だけあって, い-Adjective + だけあって, な-Adjective + なだけあって, Noun + だけあって
Example (Japanese): 彼は日本語が上手だけあって、日本人のように話すことができる。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa nihongo ga jōzu dake atte, nihonjin no yō ni hanasu koto ga dekiru.
Example (English): As expected from his good Japanese skills, he can speak like a native.

Meaning: Expresses that although the situation isn’t ideal, it could be worse; 'it’s not great, but at least...'.
Formation: Verb-casual + だけましだ, い-Adjective + だけましだ, な-Adjective + だけましだ, Noun + だけましだ
Example (Japanese): 失敗するだけましだ。もっと大変なことにならなくてよかった。
Example (Romaji): Shippai suru dake mashi da. Motto taihen na koto ni naranakute yokatta.
Example (English): At least we only failed—it could’ve been much worse.

Meaning: Used to describe an action that has just been completed, often followed by a result or observation.
Formation: Verb-past + ところ
Example (Japanese): 掃除したところ、部屋がずっとキレイになりました。
Example (Romaji): Sōji shita tokoro, heya ga zutto kirei ni narimashita.
Example (English): I just finished cleaning, and the room is so much cleaner now.

Meaning: Express the moment something happens; 'as soon as', 'just when'.
Formation: Verb-past + たとたん
Example (Japanese): ドアを開けたとたん、雨が降り始めた。
Example (Romaji): Doa o aketa totan, ame ga furi-hajimeta.
Example (English): As soon as I opened the door, it started raining.

Meaning: Indicates that something is full of or covered with a certain (usually negative) characteristic.
Formation: Noun + だらけ
Example (Japanese): 彼の部屋はゴミだらけだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare no heya wa gomi darake da.
Example (English): His room is full of trash.

Meaning: Expresses the impossibility or very low probability of something happening; 'no way', 'impossible'.
Formation: Verb-negative stem + っこない
Example (Japanese): こんなに雪が降っているんだから、学校に間に合いっこない。
Example (Romaji): Konna ni yuki ga futteirun dakara, gakkō ni maniai kkonai.
Example (English): With snow falling this heavily, there's no way we'll make it to school on time.

Meaning: Shows two actions happening simultaneously or a contrast; 'while', 'although'.
Formation: Verb-stem + つつ
Example (Japanese): 彼はテレビを見つつ、宿題をしていました。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa terebi o mitsutsu, shukudai o shite imashita.
Example (English): He was doing his homework while watching TV.

Meaning: Expresses an ongoing process or gradual change.
Formation: Verb-stem + つつある
Example (Japanese): 地球温暖化は進行しつつある。
Example (Romaji): Chikyū ondanka wa shinkō shitsutsu aru.
Example (English): Global warming is in progress.

Meaning: Express a continuous action or state; 'left as is', 'non-stop'.
Formation: Verb-ます stem + っぱなし
Example (Japanese): 窓を開けっぱなしにして、部屋が寒くなってしまった。
Example (Romaji): Mado o akeppanashi ni shite, heya ga samuku natte shimatta.
Example (English): I left the window open, and the room got cold.

Meaning: Indicates that something has the appearance, characteristics, or behavior of something else.
Formation: Noun + っぽい, Verb-casual + っぽい, い-Adjective + っぽい, な-Adjective + っぽい
Example (Japanese): 彼女は大人っぽい服を着ている。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa otonappoi fuku o kite iru.
Example (English): She’s wearing clothes that look mature.

Meaning: Expresses that one cannot afford to do something; 'can't keep on', 'unable to continue'.
Formation: Verb-て form + いられない
Example (Japanese): こんなに忙しいのに、無理に遊んでいられない。
Example (Romaji): Konna ni isogashii noni, muri ni asonde irarenai.
Example (English): I'm so busy that I can't afford to just play around.

Meaning: Expresses that something cannot be endured, tolerated, or is unbearable.
Formation: Adjective (〜く / 〜で) + て + かなわない / Verb phrase (reworded to an adjective/negative) + て + かなわない
Example (Japanese): こんなに暑くてかなわない。
Example (Romaji): Konnani atsukute kanawanai.
Example (English): I can’t stand this heat.

Grammar Point: ～てからでないと (〜te kara denai to)
Meaning: Indicates that something cannot be done before a certain action is completed; 'not until', 'only after'.
Formation: Verb-て + からでないと
Example (Japanese): 宿題をしてからでないと、遊びに行けません。
Example (Romaji): Shukudai o shite kara denai to, asobi ni ikemasen.
Example (English): You cannot go play until you’ve finished your homework.

Meaning: Emphasizes the condition; 'only when', 'precisely because'.
Formation: Verb-て form + こそ / い-Adjective + くてこそ / な-Adjective + でこそ / Noun + でこそ
Example (Japanese): 勉強してこそ、テストに合格できる。
Example (Romaji): Benkyō shite koso, tesuto ni gōkaku dekiru.
Example (English): Only when you study can you pass the test.

Meaning: Expresses an intense emotional or physical state; 'extremely', 'can’t help but'.
Formation: い-Adjective(く) + てしょうがない / な-Adjective + で(は)しょうがない / Verb-て form + しょうがない
Example (Japanese): 今日は暇で(は)しょうがない。
Example (Romaji): Kyō wa hima de shō ga nai.
Example (English): I’m extremely bored today.

Meaning: Express extremely strong feelings or sensations; 'can't stand', 'unbearably'.
Formation: い-Adjective (く) + てたまらない / な-Adjective + でたまらない / Verb-て form + たまらない
Example (Japanese): この暑さは本当に暑くてたまらない。
Example (Romaji): Kono atsusa wa hontō ni atsukute tamaranai.
Example (English): This heat is absolutely unbearable.

Meaning: Indicates an uncontrollable emotion or feeling; 'can’t help but', 'overwhelmingly'.
Formation: な-Adjective + でならない / い-Adjective (く) + てならない / Verb-て + ならない
Example (Japanese): 彼の演技が素晴らしくてならない。
Example (Romaji): Kare no engi ga subarashikute naranai.
Example (English): I can’t help but be amazed at his wonderful performance.

Grammar Point: ～でばかりはいられない (〜de bakari wa irarenai)
Meaning: Cannot afford to only do something; cannot always rely on it.
Formation: Verb-て form + ばかりはいられない / Noun + ばかりはいられない (with appropriate particles)
Example (Japanese): いつも助けてもらってばかりはいられない。
Example (Romaji): Itsumo tasukete moratte bakari wa irarenai.
Example (English): I can’t just keep letting people help me all the time.

Meaning: Used to show a strong assertion or emphasis on one’s opinion; 'isn't it?', 'aren't you?', 'right?'.
Formation: Noun + ではないか / い-Adjective + ではないか / な-Adjective + ではないか / Verb-casual + ではないか
Example (Japanese): 彼は優秀な学生ではないか。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa yūshū na gakusei de wa nai ka.
Example (English): Isn’t he an excellent student?

Meaning: Express prohibition; 'must not', 'cannot', 'should not'.
Formation: Verb-て form + はならない
Example (Japanese): ここでタバコを吸ってはならない。
Example (Romaji): Koko de tabako o sutte wa naranai.
Example (English): You must not smoke here.

Meaning: Express the extent someone goes in order to achieve something; 'to the point of', 'even', 'so far as to'.
Formation: Verb-て form + まで
Example (Japanese): 彼は試験に合格するために、徹夜してまで勉強しました。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa shiken ni gōkaku suru tame ni, tetsuya shite made benkyō shimashita.
Example (English): He studied to the point of staying up all night in order to pass the exam.

Meaning: Expresses that something is natural or expected.
Formation: Verb-て form + 当然だ
Example (Japanese): 彼は毎日勉強しているから、試験に合格して当然だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa mainichi benkyō shite iru kara, shiken ni gōkaku shite tōzen da.
Example (English): Since he studies every day, it's only natural that he passes the exam.

Grammar Point: ～というものだ (〜to iu mono da)
Meaning: Expressing a general rule or common sense.
Formation: Sentence + というものだ
Example (Japanese): 若者の熱情は尊敬に値するというものだ。
Example (Romaji): Wakamono no netsujō wa sonkei ni ataisuru to iu mono da.
Example (English): The passion of young people is something that deserves respect.

Grammar Point: どうにか～ないものか (dō ni ka ~ nai mono ka)
Meaning: Express a strong desire or wish for something to be possible.
Formation: どうにか + Verb-negative form + ないものか
Example (Japanese): どうにかこの仕事を終わらせないものか。
Example (Romaji): Dō ni ka kono shigoto o owarasenai mono ka.
Example (English): Isn't there some way to finish this job?

Meaning: Express doing something as instructed or describing how something matches a rule or guideline; 'as', 'according to'.
Formation: Verb-casual + とおり, い-Adjective + とおり, な-Adjective + だとおり, Noun + だとおり
Example (Japanese): 先生が言ったとおりに宿題をしました。
Example (Romaji): Sensei ga itta tōri ni shukudai o shimashita.
Example (English): I did my homework exactly as the teacher said.

Meaning: Used to list examples or express uncertainty; 'such as', 'like', 'or something like that'.
Formation: Verb-casual + とか, い-Adjective + とか, な-Adjective + だとか, Noun + だとか
Example (Japanese): 休日は映画を見るとか、買い物に行くとかして過ごします。
Example (Romaji): Kyūjitsu wa eiga o miru to ka, kaimono ni iku to ka shite sugoshimasu.
Example (English): On my days off, I do things like watch movies or go shopping.

Meaning: Express a specific point in time or state; 'when', 'just about', or 'in the middle of'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ところ, い-Adjective + ところ, な-Adjective + なところ, Noun + のところ
Example (Japanese): 出かけるところです。
Example (Romaji): Dekakeru tokoro desu.
Example (English): I'm just about to go out.

Meaning: Express 'far from', 'not just', 'not only', or 'to say nothing of'.
Formation: Verb-casual + どころか, い-Adjective + どころか, な-Adjective + どころか, Noun + どころか
Example (Japanese): 彼は歌が上手どころか、プロの歌手みたいだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa uta ga jōzu dokoro ka, puro no kashu mitai da.
Example (English): Far from just being good at singing, he sounds like a professional singer.

Grammar Point: ～どころではない (〜dokoro de wa nai)
Meaning: Not the time/place for; far from; can't possibly.
Formation: Verb-casual + どころではない, い-Adjective + どころではない, な-Adjective + どころではない, Noun + どころではない
Example (Japanese): 彼の失敗を笑うどころではない。私たちも同じミスをしている。
Example (Romaji): Kare no shippai o warau dokoro de wa nai. Watashitachi mo onaji misu o shite iru.
Example (English): This is not the time to laugh at his mistakes—we’re making the same ones.

Meaning: Express a hypothetical situation; 'if', 'suppose', 'assuming'.
Formation: Verb-casual + としたら, い-Adjective + としたら, な-Adjective + だとしたら, Noun + だとしたら
Example (Japanese): 明日雨が降るとしたら、傘を持っていきましょう。
Example (Romaji): Ashita ame ga furu to shitara, kasa o motte ikimashō.
Example (English): If it rains tomorrow, let’s bring umbrellas.

Meaning: Even if, despite, although
Formation: Verb-casual + としても, い-Adjective + としても, な-Adjective + だとしても, Noun + だとしても
Example (Japanese): 雨が降るとしても、レースは中止しません。
Example (Romaji): Ame ga furu to shite mo, rēsu wa chūshi shimasen.
Example (English): Even if it rains, we won't cancel the race.

Meaning: Expresses 'together with' or 'along with'; used to describe two events or actions happening simultaneously or in parallel.
Formation: Verb-casual + とともに, い-Adjective + とともに, な-Adjective + とともに, Noun + とともに
Example (Japanese): 彼が来るとともに、パーティーが始まりました。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga kuru to tomoni, paatii ga hajimarimashita.
Example (English): The party started as soon as he arrived.

Meaning: Expresses that something is not necessarily true; 'not always', 'not necessarily'.
Formation: Verb-casual + とは限らない, い-Adjective + とは限らない, な-Adjective + だとは限らない, Noun + だとは限らない
Example (Japanese): いつも勉強しているとは限らない。
Example (Romaji): Itsumo benkyou shite iru to wa kagiranai.
Example (English): It's not always true that I'm studying.

Grammar Point: ～ないことはない (〜nai koto wa nai)
Meaning: Express that something is not impossible, meaning it is possible or could be done.
Formation: Verb-ないform + ことはない
Example (Japanese): 彼が来ないことはない。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga konai koto wa nai.
Example (English): It's not that he won't come (it's possible that he will come).

Grammar Point: ～ないこともない (〜nai koto mo nai)
Meaning: Used to express an action or state is 'not impossible', but emphasizes reluctance or doubt.
Formation: Verb-ないForm + こともない, い-adjective + こともない
Example (Japanese): この問題は解けないこともないけど、難しいです。
Example (Romaji): Kono mondai wa tokenai koto mo nai kedo, muzukashii desu.
Example (English): It's not that I can't solve this problem, but it's difficult.

Grammar Point: ～ないではいられない (〜nai de wa irarenai)
Meaning: Cannot help but; cannot avoid; unable to refrain from.
Formation: Verb-ない form + ではいられない or じゃいられない
Example (Japanese): この映画はとても感動的で、泣かないではいられなかった。
Example (Romaji): Kono eiga wa totemo kandouteki de, nakanai de wa irarenakatta.
Example (English): This movie was so touching, I couldn't help but cry.

Meaning: Express doing two things simultaneously or at the same time.
Formation: Verb-stem + ながら
Example (Japanese): テレビを見ながら宿題をしています。
Example (Romaji): Terebi wo minagara shukudai wo shiteimasu.
Example (English): I am doing my homework while watching TV.

Meaning: Expresses the meaning of 'at the time of', 'in', 'on', or 'upon'.
Formation: Noun + にあたり
Example (Japanese): 入学にあたり、必要な書類を準備してください。
Example (Romaji): Nyuugaku ni atari, hitsuyou na shorui wo junbi shite kudasai.
Example (English): Please prepare the necessary documents upon entering the school.

Meaning: Indicates the place, time, or context where an action or event occurs; 'in', 'at', 'on', 'regarding'.
Formation: Noun + において
Example (Japanese): この大学において、英語のクラスが一番人気があります。
Example (Romaji): Kono daigaku ni oite, eigo no kurasu ga ichiban ninki ga arimasu.
Example (English): In this university, English classes are the most popular.

Meaning: Regardless of; irrespective of; (often used as) 'whether or not'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + にかかわらず, い-Adjective + にかかわらず, な-Adjective + にかかわらず, Noun + にかかわらず
Example (Japanese): 天気にかかわらず、今日の試合は行われます。
Example (Romaji): Tenki ni kakawarazu, kyou no shiai wa okonawaremasu.
Example (English): The game today will be held, regardless of the weather.

Meaning: Indicates a specific area or aspect in which someone or something excels.
Formation: Noun + にかけては
Example (Japanese): 料理の腕前にかけては、彼女は誰にも負けません。
Example (Romaji): Ryouri no udemae ni kakete wa, kanojo wa dare ni mo makemasen.
Example (English): When it comes to cooking skills, she is second to none.

Meaning: Expresses a natural consequence or a change that occurs according to something else; 'as', 'with', 'in accordance with'.
Formation: Noun + にしたがって
Example (Japanese): 成長にしたがって、この植物の葉が大きくなります。
Example (Romaji): Seichou ni shitagatte, kono shokubutsu no ha ga ookiku narimasu.
Example (English): As it grows, the leaves of this plant become larger.

Meaning: Express a point of view; 'from the perspective of', 'if I were'.
Formation: Noun + にしたら, Pronoun + にしたら
Example (Japanese): 彼にしたら、早く帰りたいだろう。
Example (Romaji): Kare ni shitara, hayaku kaeritai darou.
Example (English): From his perspective, he probably wants to go home early.

Meaning: Expresses 'either way', 'in any case', 'be it...', used when presenting two alternatives.
Formation: Verb (dictionary form or negative form) + にしろ, い-Adjective + にしろ, な-Adjective + にしろ, Noun + にしろ
Example (Japanese): 行くにしろ行かないにしろ、早く決めてください。
Example (Romaji): Iku ni shiro ikanai ni shiro, hayaku kimete kudasai.
Example (English): Either way, whether you go or not, please decide quickly.

Meaning: Expresses 'whenever', 'each time', 'whether...or'.
Formation: Verb-casual + につけ, い-Adjective + につけ, な-Adjective + につけ, Noun + につけ
Example (Japanese): 外国へ行くにつけ、勉強するにつけ、言葉の壁にぶつかる。
Example (Romaji): Gaikoku e iku ni tsuke, benkyou suru ni tsuke, kotoba no kabe ni butsukaru.
Example (English): Whether I go abroad or study, I always encounter language barriers.

Meaning: Expresses the idea that as one thing changes, so does another; 'as', 'along with', 'while'.
Formation: Verb (dictionary form) + につれて, Noun + につれて
Example (Japanese): 年を取るにつれて、健康に気をつけなければなりません。
Example (Romaji): Toshi wo toru ni tsurete, kenkou ni ki wo tsukenakereba narimasen.
Example (English): As you get older, you have to pay more attention to your health.

Meaning: Expresses 'along with' or 'as a result of'; indicates that one event occurs along with another.
Formation: Noun (event) + にともなって, Verb-casual + にともなって
Example (Japanese): 人口が増えるにともなって、交通渋滞も悪化しています。
Example (Romaji): Jinkou ga fueru ni tomonatte, koutsuu juutai mo akka shiteimasu.
Example (English): As the population increases, traffic congestion is also getting worse.

Meaning: Express that something is 'nothing but' or 'none other than'.
Formation: Verb-plain + にほかならない, い-Adjective + にほかならない, な-Adjective + にほかならない, Noun + にほかならない
Example (Japanese): 彼の成功は努力にほかならない。
Example (Romaji): Kare no seikou wa doryoku ni hoka naranai.
Example (English): His success is nothing but hard work.

Meaning: Expresses 'despite', 'in spite of' or 'even though'.
Formation: Verb (any tense/form) + にもかかわらず, い-Adjective + にもかかわらず, な-Adjective (or Noun) + であるにもかかわらず
Example (Japanese): 忙しいにもかかわらず、彼は毎日運動しています。
Example (Romaji): Isogashii ni mo kakawarazu, kare wa mainichi undou shiteimasu.
Example (English): Despite being busy, he exercises every day.

Meaning: Indicates the reason, method, or means by which something happens; 'by', 'through', 'due to'.
Formation: Noun + により, Verb + により
Example (Japanese): この事故は運転手の不注意により起こりました。
Example (Romaji): Kono jiko wa untenshu no fuchuui ni yori okorimashita.
Example (English): This accident occurred due to the driver's carelessness.

Meaning: Indicates a range or extent; 'over', 'throughout', 'across'.
Formation: Noun + にわたって
Example (Japanese): 彼女は一年にわたって日本語を勉強しました。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa ichinen ni watatte nihongo wo benkyou shimashita.
Example (English): She studied Japanese for over a year.

Meaning: Express an action or event that occurs before another; 'before', 'prior to', 'preceding'.
Formation: Noun + に先立ち / Verb-dictionary form + に先立って
Example (Japanese): 会議に先立ち、資料を確認しましょう。
Example (Romaji): Kaigi ni sakidachi, shiryou wo kakunin shimashou.
Example (English): Before the meeting, let's check the materials.

Meaning: Contrary to, against, in spite of
Formation: Noun + に反して
Example (Japanese): 天気予報に反して、今日は雨が降っている。
Example (Romaji): Tenki yohou ni hanshite, kyou wa ame ga futte iru.
Example (English): Contrary to the weather forecast, it is raining today.

Meaning: Based on, according to, depending on
Formation: Noun + に基づいて
Example (Japanese): 研究結果に基づいて、新しい治療法が開発されました。
Example (Romaji): Kenkyuu kekka ni motozuite, atarashii chiryouhou ga kaihatsu saremashita.
Example (English): A new treatment method was developed based on the research results.

Meaning: Expresses 'toward', 'against', 'in contrast to', or 'in response to'.
Formation: Noun + に対して
Example (Japanese): 日本の文化に対して尊敬の念を持っています。
Example (Romaji): Nihon no bunka ni taishite sonkei no nen wo motte imasu.
Example (English): I have a sense of respect towards Japanese culture.

Meaning: Responding to; living up to; meeting.
Formation: Noun + に応えて
Example (Japanese): お客様の要望に応えて、新しいメニューを作りました。
Example (Romaji): Okyaku-sama no youbou ni kotaete, atarashii menyuu o tsukurimashita.
Example (English): Responding to the customers' requests, we created a new menu.

Meaning: In accordance with, depending on, in response to.
Formation: Noun + に応じて
Example (Japanese): 仕事の量に応じて給料が変わります。
Example (Romaji): Shigoto no ryou ni oujite kyuuryou ga kawarimasu.
Example (English): The salary changes depending on the amount of work.

Meaning: Express certainty; 'it is obvious', 'it must be', 'no doubt'.
Formation: Verb-casual + に決まっている, い-Adjective + に決まっている, な-Adjective + だに決まっている, Noun + だに決まっている
Example (Japanese): こんなに暑い日に運動したら、汗をかくに決まっている。
Example (Romaji): Konna ni atsui hi ni undou shitara, ase wo kaku ni kimatte iru.
Example (English): It's obvious that you'll sweat if you exercise on such a hot day.

Meaning: Along with; in accordance with; following
Formation: Noun + に沿って
Example (Japanese): 川に沿って歩いていくと、橋が見えてきます。
Example (Romaji): Kawa ni sotte aruite iku to, hashi ga miete kimasu.
Example (English): If you walk along the river, you will see a bridge.

Meaning: Expresses that something is 'just' or 'nothing more than'; 'merely', 'only', 'simply'.
Formation: Verb-casual + に過ぎない, い-Adjective + に過ぎない, な-Adjective + に過ぎない, Noun + に過ぎない
Example (Japanese): 彼の失敗はミスに過ぎない。
Example (Romaji): Kare no shippai wa misu ni suginai.
