Example (English): His failure is nothing more than a mistake.

Meaning: Indicates that something is related to or influenced by a certain matter or factor; 'concerning', 'in connection with', 'regarding'.
Formation: Verb-casual + に関わって, い-Adjective + に関わって, な-Adjective + に関わって, Noun + に関わって
Example (Japanese): 試験の内容に関わって、先生に質問があります。
Example (Romaji): Shiken no naiyou ni kakawatte, sensei ni shitsumon ga arimasu.
Example (English): I have a question for the teacher regarding the content of the exam.

Meaning: Expresses limitation; 'only', 'limited to', 'exclusive to'.
Formation: Noun + に限り
Example (Japanese): 今日に限り、この商品が半額です。
Example (Romaji): Kyou ni kagiri, kono shouhin ga hangaku desu.
Example (English): Today only, this product is half price.

Meaning: Used to express the moment or the occasion of an action; 'at the time of', 'upon', 'when'.
Formation: Noun + に際して
Example (Japanese): 卒業式に際して、校長先生がスピーチをします。
Example (Romaji): Sotsugyoushiki ni saishite, kouchou sensei ga supiichi wo shimasu.
Example (English): At the graduation ceremony, the principal gives a speech.

Meaning: Expresses obligation or necessity; 'must', 'have to', 'need to'.
Formation: Verb-ない form → (remove い) → ね + ばならない
Example (Japanese): 試験に合格するために、もっと勉強せねばならない。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ni goukaku suru tame ni, motto benkyou se neba naranai.
Example (English): To pass the exam, I must study more.

Meaning: Not only... but also; as well as.
Formation: Verb-casual + のみならず + (も), い-Adjective + のみならず + (も), な-Adjective + のみならず + (も), Noun + のみならず + (も)
Example (Japanese): 彼は英語のみならず、フランス語も話せます。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa eigo nomi narazu, furansugo mo hanasemasu.
Example (English): He can speak not only English but also French.

Grammar Point: ～のももっともだ (〜no mo mottomo da)
Meaning: Express that something is understandable or reasonable.
Formation: Verb-casual + のももっともだ, い-Adjective + のももっともだ, な-Adjective + なのももっともだ, Noun + なのももっともだ
Example (Japanese): 彼が緊張するのももっともだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga kinchou suru no mo mottomo da.
Example (English): It's understandable that he is nervous.

Meaning: Indicates 'on the basis of', 'in terms of', or 'from the standpoint of'.
Formation: Noun or Phrase + の上では
Example (Japanese): 効率の上では、この方法が最適です。
Example (Romaji): Kouritsu no ue de wa, kono houhou ga saiteki desu.
Example (English): In terms of efficiency, this method is the best.

Meaning: Under the context or condition of; under.
Formation: Verb-casual + の下で, い-Adjective + の下で, な-Adjective + の下で, Noun + の下で
Example (Japanese): 先生の下で勉強するのはとても楽しいです。
Example (Romaji): Sensei no shita de benkyou suru no wa totemo tanoshii desu.
Example (English): Studying under the teacher is very enjoyable.

Meaning: Expresses 'not only... but also'; emphasizing the extent of something.
Formation: Noun/Verb/Adjective + ばかりか + Noun/Verb/Adjective + も
Example (Japanese): 彼はかわいいばかりか、賢くもある。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kawaii bakari ka, kashikoku mo aru.
Example (English): He is not only cute but also smart.

Meaning: Express a continuing state or negative tendency; 'just', 'only', 'always'.
Formation: Verb-てform + ばかりだ, い-Adjective + ばかりだ, な-Adjective + ばかりだ, Noun + ばかりだ
Example (Japanese): 彼は文句を言ってばかりだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa monku wo itte bakari da.
Example (English): He is always complaining.

Meaning: Express an undesired situation or result caused by something; 'simply because', 'due to', 'on account of'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ばかりに, い-Adjective + ばかりに, な-Adjective + なばかりに, Noun + なばかりに
Example (Japanese): 雨が降ったばかりに、試合が中止になりました。
Example (Romaji): Ame ga futta bakari ni, shiai ga chuushi ni narimashita.
Example (English): Simply because it rained, the match was cancelled.

Grammar Point: ～ば～というものでもない (〜ba 〜to iu mono demo nai)
Meaning: Not necessarily true that if A, then B.
Formation: Verb-ば form + というものでもない
Example (Japanese): 高いものがいいものばかりではない。
Example (Romaji): Takai mono ga ii mono bakari de wa nai.
Example (English): Expensive things are not always good.

Meaning: Used to compare or contrast two elements; 'as for...'.
Formation: Noun1 はともかく Noun2 は
Example (Japanese): デザインはともかく、機能はこの携帯電話が一番です。
Example (Romaji): Dezain wa tomokaku, kinou wa kono keitai denwa ga ichiban desu.
Example (English): As for design, the functionality of this phone is the best.

Meaning: Expresses that while the first item is somewhat acceptable, the second item is not.
Formation: Noun1 + はまだしも + Noun2
Example (Japanese): 失敗するのはまだしも、やらないで後悔する方がつらい。
Example (Romaji): Shippai suru no wa mada shimo, yaranai de koukai suru hou ga tsurai.
Example (English): Failing is one thing, but regretting not even trying is worse.

Meaning: Expressing that something is obvious, and there is also something else.
Formation: Noun1 + はもとより, Noun2 + も
Example (Japanese): 英語はもとより、スペイン語も勉強しています。
Example (Romaji): Eigo wa moto yori, supeingo mo benkyou shite imasu.
Example (English): I'm studying not only English, but also Spanish.

Grammar Point: ～は抜きにして (〜wa nuki ni shite)
Meaning: Leaving aside, excluding.
Formation: Noun + は抜きにして
Example (Japanese): 値段は抜きにして、味は美味しい。
Example (Romaji): Nedan wa nuki ni shite, aji wa oishii.
Example (English): Leaving aside the price, the taste is delicious.

Meaning: Express that an action should not be done; 'should not', 'ought not to'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + べき + ではない
Example (Japanese): 遅れる理由がないなら、遅れるべきではありません。
Example (Romaji): Okureru riyuu ga nai nara, okureru beki dewa arimasen.
Example (English): If there's no reason to be late, you shouldn’t be late.

Meaning: Express a negative conjecture or determination; 'probably not' or 'I will not'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + まい
Example (Japanese): 彼は今晩来るまい。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa konban kuru mai.
Example (English): He probably won't come tonight.

Meaning: Express doing something until a certain time or condition; 'until', 'to'.
Formation: Time/Noun + まで + Verb(て-form)
Example (Japanese): 9時まで働いて、その後休憩しました。
Example (Romaji): Ku-ji made hataraite, sono ato kyuukei shimashita.
Example (English): I worked until 9 o'clock, and then took a break.

Meaning: Act according to; leave as is; unchanged.
Formation: Verb-て + まま, い-Adjective + のまま, な-Adjective + なまま, Noun + のまま
Example (Japanese): 子供が寝ているままに、静かに部屋を出ました。
Example (Romaji): Kodomo ga nete iru mama ni, shizuka ni heya o demashita.
Example (English): I quietly left the room while the child was still sleeping.

Meaning: Express indifference or disregard; 'without hesitating', 'without worrying about'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + もかまわず, Noun + もかまわず
Example (Japanese): 彼は周りの人もかまわず、大声で話しました。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa mawari no hito mo kamawazu, oogoe de hanashimashita.
Example (English): Without worrying about the people around him, he spoke loudly.

Meaning: Definitely not; no way; no chance.
Formation: Verb-casual + ものか, い-Adjective + ものか, な-Adjective + (な)ものか, Noun + (な)ものか
Example (Japanese): そんなこと、僕がやりたいものか。
Example (Romaji): Sonna koto, boku ga yaritai mono ka.
Example (English): No way do I want to do such a thing.

Meaning: Express a strong impression or feeling; 'there's something about it that...'
Formation: Verb-casual + ものがある, い-Adjective + ものがある, な-Adjective + なものがある
Example (Japanese): 彼のスピーチには心を打たれるものがある。
Example (Romaji): Kare no supiichi ni wa kokoro o utareru mono ga aru.
Example (English): There's something moving about his speech.

Meaning: Expresses something natural or expected; 'it is normal that...', 'should', 'ought to'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ものだ, な-Adjective + なものだ, (Also: Verb-た form + ものだ for recollections)
Example (Japanese): 若い時はたくさん遊ぶものだ。
Example (Romaji): Wakai toki wa takusan asobu mono da.
Example (English): It is natural to have a lot of fun when you are young.

Meaning: Express the reason or cause for something; 'because', 'since', 'due to'.
Formation: Verb-plain + ものだから, い-Adjective + ものだから, な-Adjective + なものだから, Noun + なものだから
Example (Japanese): 試験が近いものだから、毎日勉強しています。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ga chikai mono dakara, mainichi benkyou shiteimasu.
Example (English): Because the exam is near, I'm studying every day.

Meaning: Expresses a strong negative suggestion or prohibition: 'should not', 'must not'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ものではない
Example (Japanese): そんなことを言うものではありません。
Example (Romaji): Sonna koto o iu mono dewa arimasen.
Example (English): You should not say such a thing.

Meaning: Expresses a conditional wish or unlikely possibility; 'if only', 'if it were possible'.
Formation: Verb-(potential/plain) form + ものなら, etc.
Example (Japanese): 帰れるものなら、今すぐ国へ帰りたい。
Example (Romaji): Kaereru mono nara, ima sugu kuni e kaeritai.
Example (English): If I could possibly go back, I'd return to my country right now.

Meaning: Indicates contrast or contradiction between two clauses; 'although', 'but'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ものの, い-Adjective + ものの, な-Adjective + なものの, Noun + であるものの
Example (Japanese): 早起きしたものの、バスに間に合わなかった。
Example (Romaji): Hayaoki shita mono no, basu ni maniawanakatta.
Example (English): Even though I got up early, I didn't catch the bus in time.

Meaning: Lists multiple attributes or actions applying to the same subject: 'both…and…', 'not only…but also…'.
Formation: Noun/Verb/Adjective + も + (Verb/Adjective in ば-form) + も + (Verb/Adjective)
Example (Japanese): 彼は勉強もできればスポーツもできる。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa benkyou mo dekireba supootsu mo dekiru.
Example (English): He is good at studying and also at sports.

Meaning: Indicates 'as good as', 'virtually', or 'practically' the same as something.
Formation: Noun + (も)同然だ, Verb-casual + (も)同然だ, etc.
Example (Japanese): 彼とは長い付き合いだから、家族も同然だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare to wa nagai tsukiai dakara, kazoku mo douzen da.
Example (English): I've known him for so long that he's practically family.

Meaning: Expresses various items or actions, 'things like..., and so on'.
Formation: Verb-casual + やら, い-Adjective + やら, な-Adjective + やら, Noun + やら
Example (Japanese): 宿題やら掃除やら、やることがたくさんある。
Example (Romaji): Shukudai yara souji yara, yaru koto ga takusan aru.
Example (English): I have lots of things to do, like homework and cleaning.

Meaning: Expresses that there is no way (method) to do something; it's impossible to do.
Formation: Verb-ます stem + ようがない
Example (Japanese): 彼の連絡先がわからないので、助けようがない。
Example (Romaji): Kare no renrakusaki ga wakaranai node, tasukeyou ga nai.
Example (English): I don't know his contact information, so there's no way I can help him.

Meaning: Express that there is no other choice; 'have no choice but', 'cannot do anything but'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + よりほかない
Example (Japanese): 試験が近いので、勉強するよりほかない。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ga chikai node, benkyou suru yori hoka nai.
Example (English): Since the exam is near, there is no choice but to study.

Meaning: Expresses 'there’s no way' or 'it’s impossible', indicating a high degree of certainty.
Formation: Verb-casual + わけがない, い-Adjective + わけがない, な-Adjective + なわけがない, Noun + のわけがない
Example (Japanese): 彼が怪我をしたから、試合に勝てるわけがない。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga kega wo shita kara, shiai ni kateru wake ga nai.
Example (English): He got injured, so there's no way he can win the match.

Meaning: Express a logical conclusion or reason; 'it means', 'no wonder', 'the reason is'.
Formation: Verb-casual + わけだ, い-Adjective + わけだ, な-Adjective + なわけだ, Noun + のわけだ
Example (Japanese): 彼女が遅れたのは、電車が遅れたわけだ。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo ga okureta no wa, densha ga okureta wake da.
Example (English): The reason she was late is that the train was delayed.

Meaning: Not necessarily; it doesn't mean that ~.
Formation: Verb-plain + わけではない, い-Adjective + わけではない, な-Adjective + だわけではない, Noun + だわけではない
Example (Japanese): 彼が勉強しないわけではないが、成績があまり良くない。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga benkyou shinai wake dewa nai ga, seiseki ga amari yoku nai.
Example (English): It's not that he doesn't study, but his grades aren't very good.

Grammar Point: ～わけにはいかない (〜wake ni wa ikanai)
Meaning: Expresses that one cannot (or must not) do something due to responsibility, social pressure, etc.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + わけにはいかない
Example (Japanese): 試験が近いから、遊ぶわけにはいかない。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ga chikai kara, asobu wake ni wa ikanai.
Example (English): Since the exam is close, I can't afford to just play around.

Meaning: Indicates that something serves as a trigger or starting point for another action/event.
Formation: Noun + をきっかけに
Example (Japanese): 結婚をきっかけに、彼は真剣に仕事を頑張り始めた。
Example (Romaji): Kekkon o kikkake ni, kare wa shinken ni shigoto o ganbarihajimeta.
Example (English): Getting married was the catalyst for him to start working seriously.

Meaning: Express 'as', 'in the capacity of', or 'taking something as...'.
Formation: Noun1 + を + Noun2 + として
Example (Japanese): 彼は教師を職業として働いています。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kyoushi o shokugyou toshite hataraite imasu.
Example (English): He works as a teacher.

Meaning: Indicates that something is centered around or focused on a main topic or area.
Formation: Noun + を中心に
Example (Japanese): このイベントは音楽を中心に楽しまれています。
Example (Romaji): Kono ibento wa ongaku o chuushin ni tanoshimarete imasu.
Example (English): This event is mainly enjoyed for its music.

Meaning: Means 'regardless of' or 'irrespective of'.
Formation: Noun + を問わず
Example (Japanese): このイベントは、年齢を問わず、誰でも参加できます。
Example (Romaji): Kono ibento wa, nenrei o towazu, dare demo sanka dekimasu.
Example (English): This event is open to everyone, regardless of age.

Meaning: To express that something is done with a certain feeling, intention, or emotion.
Formation: Feeling/emotion/intention Noun + を + 込めて + Verb
Example (Japanese): 愛を込めて料理を作りました。
Example (Romaji): Ai wo komete ryouri wo tsukurimashita.
Example (English): I cooked the meal with love.

Meaning: Expresses 'through', 'throughout', or 'during'.
Formation: Noun + を通じて
Example (Japanese): インターネットを通じて友達と連絡を取ります。
Example (Romaji): Intaanetto wo tsuujite tomodachi to renraku wo torimasu.
Example (English): I keep in touch with my friends through the internet.

Meaning: To rely on or depend on something or someone.
Formation: Noun + を頼りに
Example (Japanese): 彼女は地図を頼りに旅行をしている。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa chizu wo tayori ni ryokou wo shite iru.
Example (English): She is traveling relying on a map.

Meaning: Indicates that while one action or situation is happening, another action or situation is also occurring or is in contrast.
Formation: Verb-casual + 一方(で), い-Adjective + 一方(で), な-Adjective + な/である一方(で), Noun + である一方(で)
Example (Japanese): 技術が進化する一方、生活が忙しくなっている。
Example (Romaji): Gijutsu ga shinka suru ippou, seikatsu ga isogashiku natte iru.
Example (English): While technology advances, life is getting busier.

Meaning: Expresses that a situation or condition is continuing to increase or decrease in one direction.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + 一方だ
Example (Japanese): 世界の人口は増える一方だ。
Example (Romaji): Sekai no jinkou wa fueru ippou da.
Example (English): The world's population continues to increase.

Meaning: Used to express that something is done after or on the basis of something else; 'after', 'upon'.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + 上で, Noun + の上で
Example (Japanese): 調査を行った上で、結論を出しましょう。
Example (Romaji): Chousa wo okonatta ue de, ketsuron wo dashimashou.
Example (English): Let's draw a conclusion after conducting the investigation.

Meaning: Express 'in addition to', 'besides', 'not only... but also'.
Formation: Verb-plain + 上に, い-Adjective + 上に, な-Adjective + な上に, Noun + の上に
Example (Japanese): 彼は頭がいい上に、スポーツも得意です。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa atama ga ii ue ni, supo-tsu mo tokui desu.
Example (English): In addition to being smart, he is also good at sports.

Meaning: Expresses 'now that', 'since', or 'once'.
Formation: Verb-casual + 上は, い-Adjective + 上は, な-Adjective + な上は, Noun + の上は
Example (Japanese): 試験に合格した上は、パーティーを開こう。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ni goukaku shita ue wa, paatii wo hirakou.
Example (English): Now that I've passed the exam, let's have a party.

Meaning: Expresses 'since' or 'as long as' in a conditional context.
Formation: Verb-casual + 以上, い-Adjective + 以上, な-Adjective + な以上, Noun + の以上
Example (Japanese): 彼は忙しい以上、手伝いに行っても無駄だろう。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa isogashii ijou, tetsudai ni itte mo muda darou.
Example (English): Since he's busy, it would be pointless to try helping him.

Meaning: Indicates something happening 'since', 'ever since', or 'after' a particular time.
Formation: Verb-past + 以来, い-Adjective + 以来, Noun + 以来
Example (Japanese): 卒業以来、彼女に会っていない。
Example (Romaji): Sotsugyou irai, kanojo ni atte inai.
Example (English): I haven't seen her since we graduated.

Meaning: To do something completely or thoroughly.
Formation: Verb-stem + 切る
Example (Japanese): 彼は試験勉強をがんばり切るつもりだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa shiken benkyou o ganbari kiru tsumori da.
Example (English): He intends to give his absolute all to exam study.

Meaning: Express contrast between two aspects; 'on the one hand', 'on the other hand'.
Formation: Verb-casual + 反面, い-Adjective + 反面, な-Adjective + である反面, Noun + である反面
Example (Japanese): この車は速い反面、燃費が悪いです。
Example (Romaji): Kono kuruma wa hayai hanmen, nenpi ga warui desu.
Example (English): On the one hand, this car is fast, but on the other hand, it has poor fuel efficiency.

Meaning: Indicating target or intended audience.
Formation: Noun + 向け
Example (Japanese): この雑誌は若者向けです。
Example (Romaji): Kono zasshi wa wakamono-muke desu.
Example (English): This magazine is aimed at young people.

Meaning: Express a concern or fear that something undesirable might occur.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + 恐れがある
Example (Japanese): 地震が来る恐れがあるため、避難所に行ってください。
Example (Romaji): Jishin ga kuru osore ga aru tame, hinanjo ni itte kudasai.
Example (English): Please go to the evacuation center because there is a risk of an earthquake.

Meaning: Expresses 'when' or 'in case of' specific situations or timings.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + 折には, Verb-た form + 折には, い-Adjective + 折には, な-Adjective + な折には, Noun + の折には
Example (Japanese): 喉が渇く折には、このペットボトルの水を飲んでください。
Example (Romaji): Nodo ga kawaku ori ni wa, kono pettobotoru no mizu o nonde kudasai.
Example (English): When you get thirsty, please drink water from this bottle.

Meaning: Express the outcome after a period of time or series of actions; 'after', 'as a result of'.
Formation: Noun + 末
Example (Japanese): 長い議論の末、ようやく意見がまとまった。
Example (Romaji): Nagai giron no sue, youyaku iken ga matomatta.
Example (English): After a long discussion, we finally reached a consensus.

Meaning: Expresses 'as soon as' (when used with Verb-ますstem) or 'depending on' (when used with a noun).
Formation: Verb-ますstem + 次第, Noun + 次第
Example (Japanese): 仕事が終わり次第、帰ります。
Example (Romaji): Shigoto ga owari shidai, kaerimasu.
Example (English): I will go home as soon as I finish work.

Meaning: Indicates 'depending on; based on' a certain factor or situation.
Formation: Noun + 次第で
Example (Japanese): 仕事の終わり次第で、家に帰る時間が変わります。
Example (Romaji): Shigoto no owari shidai de, ie ni kaeru jikan ga kawarimasu.
Example (English): Depending on when I finish work, the time I go home may change.

Meaning: A polite/formal way to say 'it depends on...' or 'as soon as...', often used in concluding statements.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + 次第です (or Noun + 次第です)
Example (Japanese): 天気次第ですが、明日はピクニックに行こうと思います。
Example (Romaji): Tenki shidai desu ga, ashita wa pikunikku ni ikou to omoimasu.
Example (English): It depends on the weather, but I’m thinking of going for a picnic tomorrow.

Meaning: Indicates a slight feeling or tendency toward a particular state.
Formation: Noun + 気味 (e.g., 風邪気味, 寝不足気味, 緊張気味)
Example (Japanese): 最近寝不足気味で、ちょっと疲れています。
Example (Romaji): Saikin nebusoku gimi de, chotto tsukarete imasu.
Example (English): Lately, I'm feeling somewhat sleep-deprived and a bit tired.

Meaning: Expresses 'as long as', 'while', or 'to the extent that' a certain condition holds true.
Formation: Verb-casual + 限り, い-Adjective + 限り, な-Adjective + な限り, Noun + の限り
Example (Japanese): 元気な限り、運動し続けます。
Example (Romaji): Genki na kagiri, undou shi tsuzukemasu.
Example (English): As long as I'm healthy, I'll keep exercising.

Meaning: Means 'when', 'while', or 'on the occasion of' a certain event or situation.
Formation: Verb-casual + 際に, い-Adjective + 際に, な-Adjective + な際に, Noun + の際に
Example (Japanese): 出発の際に、パスポートを忘れないでください。
Example (Romaji): Shuppatsu no sai ni, pasupooto wo wasurenai de kudasai.
Example (English): When departing, please don't forget your passport.

Grammar Point: A うが B うが (A uga B uga)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'no matter how... or', 'even if... or'.
Formation: Verb-volitional form + うが + Verb-volitional form + うが, or Adjective (-かろう) + が + Adjective (-かろう) + が
Example (Japanese): 朝早かろうが夜遅かろうが、いつもバスが遅れる。
Example (Romaji): Asa hayakarou ga yoru osokarou ga, itsumo basu ga okureru.
Example (English): No matter whether it's early morning or late at night, the bus is always late.

Grammar Point: A うと B うと (A uto B uto)
Meaning: Shows that the speaker is indifferent to both conditions; 'whether A or B'.
Formation: い-adjective (-かろう) + と, な-adjective / Noun + であろうと
Example (Japanese): 雨が降ろうと晴れようと、私は毎日ジョギングをします。
Example (Romaji): Ame ga furou to hareyou to, watashi wa mainichi jogingu o shimasu.
Example (English): Whether it's raining or sunny, I jog every day.

Grammar Point: A かたわら B (A katawara B)
Meaning: Expresses 'while also', 'at the same time as'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + かたわら, Noun + のかたわら
Example (Japanese): 彼は仕事をするかたわら、大学に通っている。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa shigoto o suru katawara, daigaku ni kayotte iru.
Example (English): While working, he also attends university.

Grammar Point: A かれ B かれ (A kare B kare)
Meaning: Expresses 'whether A or B'; both situations are included.
Formation: Commonly i-adjective stems + かれ + i-adjective stems + かれ (e.g. 早かれ遅かれ). Also sometimes Noun + かれ + Noun + かれ in older usage.
Example (Japanese): 冬かれ夏かれ、毎日ジョギングする。
Example (Romaji): Fuyu kare natsu kare, mainichi jogingu suru.
Example (English): Whether it's winter or summer, I jog every day.

Grammar Point: A だの B だの (A dano B dano)
Meaning: Used to list examples (often with a critical or complaining tone); 'things like A, B, etc.'.
Formation: Noun/Verb casual + だの + Noun/Verb casual + だの
Example (Japanese): 彼はいつも遅刻だの、仕事を忘れるだので困る。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa itsumo chikoku dano, shigoto o wasureru dano de komaru.
Example (English): I'm troubled because he's always late, forgets work, and so on.

Grammar Point: A であれ B であれ (A deare B deare)
Meaning: Indicates the same statement applies to both A and B; 'whether A or B'.
Formation: Noun A + であれ + Noun B + であれ
Example (Japanese): 雨であれ雪であれ、試合は中止にならない。
Example (Romaji): Ame deare yuki deare, shiai wa chuushi ni naranai.
Example (English): Whether it's rain or snow, the match will not be canceled.

Grammar Point: A というか B というか (A to iu ka B to iu ka)
Meaning: Means 'rather than say A, it's more like B', or 'whether to call it A or B'.
Formation: Phrase A + というか + Phrase B + というか
Example (Japanese): 彼は無礼というか、直接的というか、とにかくはっきりしている。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa burei to iu ka, chokusetsuteki to iu ka, tonikaku hakkiri shite iru.
Example (English): He's rather rude, or maybe just direct; in any case, he is very blunt.

Grammar Point: A とも B とも (A tomo B tomo)
Meaning: Expresses two possibilities; 'either A or B', 'whether A or B'.
Formation: Noun + とも + Noun + とも (or sometimes Verb forms for each A, B)
Example (Japanese): 決断とも誤りとも、結果は時間が教えてくれるでしょう。
Example (Romaji): Ketsudan tomo ayamari tomo, kekka wa jikan ga oshiete kureru deshou.
Example (English): Whether it's a wise decision or a mistake, time will show the result.

Grammar Point: A にしろ B にしろ (A nishiro B nishiro)
Meaning: Means 'whether it is A or B'; 'regardless of A or B'.
Formation: Noun A + にしろ + Noun B + にしろ, or Verb-casual A + にしろ + Verb-casual B + にしろ
Example (Japanese): 暑いにしろ寒いにしろ、毎日運動するべきです。
Example (Romaji): Atsui ni shiro samui ni shiro, mainichi undou suru beki desu.
Example (English): Whether it's hot or cold, you should exercise every day.

Grammar Point: A にせよ B にせよ (A ni seyo B ni seyo)
Meaning: Either A or B; Regardless of whether it's A or B.
Formation: Noun + にせよ + Noun + にせよ (also works with verbs in dictionary form + にせよ)
Example (Japanese): 雨にせよ雪にせよ、試合は中止しない。
Example (Romaji): Ame ni seyo yuki ni seyo, shiai wa chuushi shinai.
Example (English): Whether it's rain or snow, the match won't be cancelled.

Grammar Point: A につけ B につけ (A ni tsuke B ni tsuke)
Meaning: Expresses 'whether... or...', 'both... and...', 'in either case'.
Formation: Phrase A (dictionary/adjective form) + につけ、Phrase B (dictionary/adjective form) + につけ
Example (Japanese): 彼には笑うにつけ泣くにつけ、とても魅力的だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare ni wa warau ni tsuke naku ni tsuke, totemo miryokuteki da.
Example (English): He is very charming whether he’s laughing or crying.

Grammar Point: A のやら B のやら (A no yara B no yara)
Meaning: Used when the speaker is unsure or confused between multiple possibilities.
Formation: Noun1 + のやら + Noun2 + のやら (also works with adjectives and verbs + のやら)
Example (Japanese): 彼が怒っているのやら、悲しいのやら、私には分からない。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga okotte iru no yara, kanashii no yara, watashi ni wa wakaranai.
Example (English): I don't know whether he's angry or sad.

Grammar Point: Noun1 が Noun1 なら、 Noun2 も Noun2 だ (A ga A nara, B mo B da)
Meaning: Indicates a parallel or matching situation; 'if Noun1 is (truly) Noun1, then Noun2 is also Noun2'.
Formation: Noun1 + が + (repeat Noun1) + なら、Noun2 + も + (repeat Noun2) + だ
Example (Japanese): 鬼が鬼なら、人間も人間だ。
Example (Romaji): Oni ga oni nara, ningen mo ningen da.
Example (English): If demons are indeed demons, humans are likewise humans.

Grammar Point: Noun1 も Noun1 なら、Noun2 も Noun2 だ (A mo A nara, B mo B da)
Meaning: Highlights two parallel facts or characteristics; 'if it’s said that ~, then it can also be said that ~'.
Formation: Noun1 + も + (repeat Noun1) + なら、Noun2 + も + (repeat Noun2) + だ
Example (Japanese): 君も君なら、私も私だ。
Example (Romaji): Kimi mo kimi nara, watashi mo watashi da.
Example (English): If you are you, then I am also me.

Grammar Point: Noun + あっての + Noun (A atte no B)
Meaning: Expresses 'B cannot exist without A'; 'B only exists because of A'.
Formation: Noun1 + あっての + Noun2
Example (Japanese): 家族あっての私です。
Example (Romaji): Kazoku atte no watashi desu.
Example (English): I am who I am thanks to my family.

Grammar Point: Noun かたがた (Noun kata gata)
Meaning: Do one thing while also doing another; 'while', 'and at the same time'.
Formation: Noun + かたがた
Example (Japanese): 東京へ出張のかたがた、友人に会いに行った。
Example (Romaji): Toukyou e shucchou no kata gata, yuujin ni ai ni itta.
Example (English): While on a business trip to Tokyo, I also went to see a friend.

Meaning: Means 'while...at the same time', 'on the occasion of', or 'along with'.
Formation: Noun + がてら
Example (Japanese): 散歩がてらに、近くの公園で花を摘みました。
Example (Romaji): Sanpo gatera ni, chikaku no kouen de hana o tsumimashita.
Example (English): While taking a walk, I picked some flowers in the nearby park.

Meaning: Used with large numbers or measurements to emphasize 'at least that many' or 'no less than.'
Formation: Number + Counter + からある
Example (Japanese): 彼のコレクションは500個からある。
Example (Romaji): Kare no korekushon wa gohyaku ko kara aru.
Example (English): He has at least 500 items in his collection.

Grammar Point: Noun からする (Noun kara suru)
Meaning: Used to indicate that something is judged, estimated, or considered from a certain point or aspect.
Formation: Noun + からする
Example (Japanese): 彼の態度からすると、彼はその計画に反対しているようだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare no taido kara suru to, kare wa sono keikaku ni hantai shiteiru you da.
Example (English): Judging from his attitude, he seems to be against the plan.

Meaning: Defines the starting point or the origin; 'from'.
Formation: Noun + からの
Example (Japanese): 日本からの手紙を受け取りました。
Example (Romaji): Nihon kara no tegami wo uketorimashita.
Example (English): I received a letter from Japan.

Grammar Point: Noun から言わせれば (~kara iwasereba)
Meaning: Express the perspective of the noun; 'from ~'s point of view.'
Formation: Noun + から言わせれば
Example (Japanese): 先生から言わせれば、毎日勉強するべきだ。
Example (Romaji): Sensei kara iwasereba, mainichi benkyou suru beki da.
Example (English): From the teacher's point of view, you should study every day.

Meaning: Describes 'entirely', 'all together', or 'as a whole group'.
Formation: Noun + ぐるみ
Example (Japanese): 家族ぐるみで旅行に行きました。
Example (Romaji): Kazoku gurumi de ryokou ni ikimashita.
Example (English): We went on a trip with the whole family.

Meaning: Expresses 'though there is ... (some negative or burdensome aspect), still ...'.
Formation: Noun + こそあれ + (result/continuation)
Example (Japanese): 問題こそあれ、プロジェクトは順調に進んでいます。
Example (Romaji): Mondai koso are, purojekuto wa junchou ni susunde imasu.
Example (English): Though there are problems, the project is progressing smoothly.

Meaning: Emphasizes that 'it is precisely Noun that ...', then adds a contrasting or additional point.
Formation: Noun + こそ + (statement) + が + (contrasting/additional statement)
Example (Japanese): お金こそ必要だが、それだけが人生のすべてではない。
Example (Romaji): Okane koso hitsuyou da ga, sore dake ga jinsei no subete de wa nai.
Example (English): Money is indeed necessary, but it isn't everything in life.

Meaning: An emphatic pattern meaning 'it may be X, but definitely not Y.' Often pairs with a negative statement.
Formation: Noun + こそすれ + (negative or contrasting statement)
Example (Japanese): 感謝こそすれ、非難などできません。
Example (Romaji): Kansha koso sure, hinan nado dekimasen.
Example (English): I might feel grateful, but I could never criticize.

Grammar Point: Noun ごとき / Noun ごとく (〜gotoki/〜gotoku)
Meaning: Means 'like a...', 'as if...', expressing a simile or metaphor.
Formation: Noun + ごとき, Noun + ごとく, Verb-casual + ごとく, い-Adjective + ごとく
Example (Japanese): 彼は天使のごとく純粋だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa tenshi no gotoku junsui da.
Example (English): He is as pure as an angel.

Grammar Point: Noun じゃあるまいし (~ja aru mai shi)
Meaning: Expressing that something 'is not'; 'it's not like...'. Colloquial/masculine form of ではあるまいし.
Formation: Noun or Na-Adjective + じゃあるまいし
Example (Japanese): 彼は子供じゃあるまいし、その問題をしっかりと解決するべきだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kodomo ja aru mai shi, sono mondai o shikkari to kaiketsu suru beki da.
Example (English): He’s not a child, so he should solve that problem properly.

Meaning: Denotes 'entirely' or 'nothing but' the preceding noun.
Formation: Noun + ずくめ
Example (Japanese): 彼は最近、失敗ずくめだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa saikin, shippai zukume da.
Example (English): He has had nothing but failures recently.

Grammar Point: Noun だけではすまない (Noun dake dewa sumanai)
Meaning: Expresses 'it can't be settled with just...', 'cannot be resolved merely by...'.
Formation: Noun + だけではすまない
Example (Japanese): この問題は謝罪だけではすまない。
Example (Romaji): Kono mondai wa shazai dake dewa sumanai.
Example (English): This problem cannot be settled with just an apology.

Grammar Point: Noun たりとも～ない (~tari tomo ~nai)
Meaning: Used to show a strong negative: 'not even ~', 'not a single ~'.
Formation: Noun + たりとも + Negative Verb
Example (Japanese): 一分たりとも無駄にするな。
Example (Romaji): Ippun tari tomo muda ni suru na.
Example (English): Don’t waste even a single minute.

Meaning: Indicates 'being in the position/state of', used for roles or statuses.
Formation: Noun1 + たる + Noun2
Example (Japanese): リーダーたる者は、常に先を見て行動すべきだ。
Example (Romaji): Riidaa taru mono wa, tsune ni saki o mite koudou subeki da.
Example (English): A person who is a leader should always look ahead and act accordingly.

Meaning: Means 'even', 'as much as', used for emphasis in formal contexts.
Formation: Noun + ですら
Example (Japanese): 明日試験があるのに、彼はテキストですら読まない。
Example (Romaji): Ashita shiken ga aru noni, kare wa tekisuto desura yomanai.
Example (English): He doesn’t even read the textbook, despite having a test tomorrow.

Grammar Point: Noun でなくてなんだろう (〜de nakute nandarou)
Meaning: A strong rhetorical question: 'If not X, then what is it?'
Formation: Noun + でなくてなんだろう
Example (Japanese): これが真実でなくてなんだろう。
Example (Romaji): Kore ga shinjitsu de nakute nandarou.
Example (English): If this isn’t the truth, then what is?

Grammar Point: Noun ではあるまいし (~dewa aru maishi)
Meaning: Means 'it’s not as if...', 'it’s not that...', more formal than じゃあるまいし.
Formation: Noun + ではあるまいし
Example (Japanese): 彼女はプロの歌手ではあるまいし、完璧を求めるのは酷だ。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa puro no kashu de wa aru mai shi, kanpeki o motomeru no wa koku da.
Example (English): She’s not a professional singer, so it’s rather harsh to demand perfection.

Grammar Point: Noun と Noun を兼ねて (Noun to Noun o kanete)
Meaning: Used to indicate doing two things at once or fulfilling two roles/purposes.
Formation: Noun + と + Noun + を兼ねて
Example (Japanese): お父さんは社長と経理部長を兼ねています。
Example (Romaji): Otousan wa shachou to keiri buchou o kanete imasu.
Example (English): My father serves as both the company president and the head of accounting.

Grammar Point: Noun といい Noun といい (〜to ii〜to ii)
Meaning: Used to express 'both A and B'; 'whether it's A or B'; 'not to mention A and also B'.
Formation: Noun1 + といい + Noun2 + といい + Comment
Example (Japanese): 日本の食べ物といい観光地といい、すべてが素晴らしいです。
Example (Romaji): Nihon no tabemono to ii kankouchi to ii, subete ga subarashii desu.
Example (English): Both Japanese food and tourist spots are all wonderful.

Meaning: Used to specify or define one noun with another; 'the noun called', 'the noun that is', or 'a certain'.
Formation: Noun1 という Noun2
Example (Japanese): 宮崎駿という人は有名なアニメーション監督です。
Example (Romaji): Miyazaki Hayao to iu hito wa yuumei na animation kantoku desu.
Example (English): The person called Hayao Miyazaki is a famous animation director.

Grammar Point: Noun というところだ (Noun to iu tokoro da)
Meaning: Means 'it's approximately...' or 'it's about...'. Used to show approximation or a general assessment.
Formation: Noun + というところだ
Example (Japanese): 今回の試験の合格者は半数というところだろう。
Example (Romaji): Konkai no shiken no goukakusha wa hansuu to iu tokoro darou.
Example (English): The passers in this exam would be approximately half.

Grammar Point: Noun + というもの (~ to iu mono)
Meaning: Used to express a generic concept: 'all ~', 'any ~ of that kind'.
Formation: Noun + というもの
Example (Japanese): 子供というものは、毎日たくさん遊びます。
Example (Romaji): Kodomo to iu mono wa, mainichi takusan asobimasu.
Example (English): Children, as a group, play a lot every day.

Grammar Point: Noun といったところだ (Noun to itta tokoro da)
Meaning: Expresses 'at most', 'as much as', or 'limited to'.
Formation: Noun + といったところだ
Example (Japanese): 彼の英語レベルは初級といったところだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare no eigo reberu wa shokyuu to itta tokoro da.
Example (English): His English level is at most beginner level.

Grammar Point: Noun といわず Noun といわず (A to iwazu B to iwazu)
Meaning: Expresses 'both A and B' or 'be it A or B'; applies to both without distinction.
Formation: Noun1 + といわず + Noun2 + といわず + (rest of the sentence)
Example (Japanese): 冬といわず夏といわず、彼はいつもアイスクリームを食べます。
Example (Romaji): Fuyu to iwazu natsu to iwazu, kare wa itsumo aisukuriimu o tabemasu.
Example (English): Be it winter or summer, he always eats ice cream.

Meaning: Expresses strong feelings about a topic; 'speaking of', 'when it comes to'.
Formation: Noun + ときたら
Example (Japanese): 寿司ときたら、彼は何も食べられない。
Example (Romaji): Sushi tokitara, kare wa nanimo taberarenai.
Example (English): When it comes to sushi, he can't eat anything.

Grammar Point: Noun とは比べものにならない (~to wa kurabemono ni naranai)
Meaning: Indicates something is not comparable; 'beyond comparison'.
Formation: Noun + とは比べものにならない
Example (Japanese): 新しい車の速さは古い車とは比べものにならない。
Example (Romaji): Atarashii kuruma no hayasa wa furui kuruma to wa kurabemono ni naranai.
Example (English): The speed of the new car is not comparable to the old one.

Meaning: Used to criticize or question unbecoming behavior by someone of a certain status.
Formation: Noun + ともあろう + Noun
Example (Japanese): 先生ともあろう者が、そんな間違いをするなんて。
Example (Romaji): Sensei tomoarou mono ga, sonna machigai o suru nante.
Example (English): For a teacher, it's shocking to make such a mistake.

Grammar Point: Noun ともなると (〜to mo naru to)
Meaning: 'When it comes to...', emphasizes a change of situation or status.
Formation: Noun + ともなると
Example (Japanese): クリスマスともなると、街中がきらきらと輝いて見えます。
Example (Romaji): Kurisumasu to mo naru to, machijuu ga kirakira to kagayaite miemasu.
Example (English): When it comes to Christmas time, the whole city sparkles.

Grammar Point: Noun ともなれば (〜to mo nareba)
Meaning: Expresses 'if it comes to', 'when', or 'once'.
Formation: Noun + ともなれば
Example (Japanese): 試験ともなれば、大抵の人が緊張するものです。
Example (Romaji): Shiken to mo nareba, taitei no hito ga kinchou suru mono desu.
Example (English): When it comes to exams, most people get nervous.

Grammar Point: Noun と相まって (~ to aimatte)
Meaning: Used to express 'in combination with', 'together with', 'along with'.
Formation: Noun + と相まって
Example (Japanese): 天気の良さと相まって、ピクニックは大成功でした。
Example (Romaji): Tenki no yosa to aimatte, pikunikku wa daiseikou deshita.
Example (English): In combination with the good weather, the picnic was a great success.

Grammar Point: Noun なくして～はない (Noun nakushite ~ wa nai)
Meaning: Expresses 'without ~, there can't be ~'; 'can't do ~ without first doing ~'.
Formation: Noun + なくして + Sentence ～はない
Example (Japanese): 努力なくして成功はない。
Example (Romaji): Doryoku nakushite seikou wa nai.
Example (English): There is no success without effort.

Grammar Point: Noun なしでは～ない (Noun nashi de wa ~nai)
Meaning: Expresses the necessity of something; 'cannot do without', 'not possible without'.
Formation: Noun + なしでは～ない
Example (Japanese): 水なしでは生きられない。
Example (Romaji): Mizu nashi de wa ikirarenai.
Example (English): We cannot live without water.

Grammar Point: Noun なしには～ない (Noun nashi ni wa ~nai)
Meaning: Means 'without', 'cannot do without', 'not possible without'.
Formation: Noun + なしには + Verb-negative
Example (Japanese): お金なしには生活ができない。
Example (Romaji): Okane nashi ni wa seikatsu ga dekinai.
Example (English): I cannot get by without money.

Grammar Point: Noun ならいざ知らず (~nara izashirazu)
Meaning: Expresses 'maybe X is possible, but Y is definitely not'. Often 'let alone...'.
Formation: Noun1 + ならいざ知らず + Noun2 (comment)
Example (Japanese): 数学ならいざ知らず、物理なんて全然わからない。
Example (Romaji): Suugaku nara iza shirazu, butsuri nante zenzen wakaranai.
Example (English): Math might be manageable, but as for physics, I'm completely clueless.

Grammar Point: Noun + ならでは (~nara de wa)
Meaning: Expresses something unique or characteristic only of that noun; 'only found in', 'only possible with'.
Formation: Noun + ならでは
Example (Japanese): これは日本ならではの風景ですね。
Example (Romaji): Kore wa Nihon nara dewa no fuukei desu ne.
Example (English): This is a landscape you can only find in Japan.

Grammar Point: Noun なり Noun なり (A nari B nari)
Meaning: Lists alternatives of the same kind; 'either A or B', 'A or B, for example'.
Formation: Noun + なり + Noun + なり
Example (Japanese): 映画なり、音楽なり、何か趣味はありますか。
Example (Romaji): Eiga nari, ongaku nari, nanika shumi wa arimasu ka?
Example (English): Do you have any hobbies, such as movies or music?

Meaning: Indicates even a small amount or degree; 'at least', 'even a little'.
Formation: Noun + なりとも
Example (Japanese): 時間が限られているので、一時間なりとも練習すべきだ。
Example (Romaji): Jikan ga kagirarete iru node, ichi-jikan nari tomo renshuu subeki da.
Example (English): Since time is limited, you should practice for at least an hour.

Grammar Point: Noun に Noun を重ねて (A ni B wo kasanete)
Meaning: This expression is used to describe repeated actions or states, 'one after another' or 'pile up'.
Formation: Noun に Noun を重ねて
Example (Japanese): 彼女は失敗に失敗を重ねて、とうとう会社を辞めた。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa shippai ni shippai wo kasanete, toutou kaisha wo yameta.
Example (English): She piled up failures upon failures and finally quit the company.

Grammar Point: Noun にあっては (Noun ni atte ha)
Meaning: Indicates a specific situation or environment in which something happens or is the case.
Formation: Noun + にあっては
Example (Japanese): 戦争時にあっては、すべての人々が困難に直面していました。
Example (Romaji): Sensouji ni atte wa, subete no hito ga konnan ni chokumen shiteimashita.
Example (English): In wartime, all people were facing difficulties.

Grammar Point: Noun にあるまじき Noun (Noun ni aru majiki Noun)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'unfitting', 'unbecoming' or 'inappropriate'.
Formation: Noun1 にあるまじき Noun2
Example (Japanese): 彼は教師にあるまじき言動をとった。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kyoushi ni aru majiki gendou wo totta.
Example (English): He took actions that are unbecoming of a teacher.

Meaning: Expresses the idea 'even for', 'even though', or 'in spite of'.
Formation: Noun + にして
Example (Japanese): 彼は医者にしてその基本的な知識がないのが信じられない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa isha ni shite sono kihonteki na chishiki ga nai no ga shinjirarenai.
Example (English): I can't believe that even as a doctor, he doesn't have that basic knowledge.

Grammar Point: Noun にして初めて (Noun nishite hajimete)
Meaning: Expresses 'only when/after... for the first time'.
Formation: Noun + にして初めて
Example (Japanese): 大人にして初めて、親の苦労が分かった。
Example (Romaji): Otona ni shite hajimete, oya no kurou ga wakatta.
Example (English): Only when I became an adult did I understand my parents' struggles for the first time.

Meaning: Expresses the concept of 'even'; 'even in', 'even as', 'even to'.
Formation: Noun + にすら
Example (Japanese): 彼にすらその問題は解けなかった。
Example (Romaji): Kare ni sura sono mondai wa tokenakatta.
Example (English): Even he could not solve that problem.

Grammar Point: Noun にとどまらず～も (~ ni todomarazu ~ mo)
Meaning: This expresses the idea of 'not only...but also', 'not stopping at...'.
Formation: Noun + にとどまらず + Noun + も
Example (Japanese): このアプリは、日本語にとどまらず、他の言語もサポートしています。
Example (Romaji): Kono apuri wa, nihongo ni todomarazu, hoka no gengo mo sapooto shite imasu.
Example (English): This app not only supports Japanese, but also other languages.

Grammar Point: Noun にひきかえ Noun は (~ni hikikae ~ wa)
Meaning: Represents 'in contrast to', 'as opposed to'.
Formation: Noun 1 + にひきかえ + Noun 2 + は
Example (Japanese): 彼の親切さにひきかえ、彼女は無感情だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare no shinsetsusa ni hikikae, kanojo wa mukanjou da.
Example (English): In contrast to his kindness, she is emotionless.

Grammar Point: Noun にもまして (〜ni mo mashite)
Meaning: This expresses 'Even more than; exceeding'.
Formation: Noun + にもまして
Example (Japanese): 私は彼にもまして、音楽を愛しています。
Example (Romaji): Watashi wa kare ni mo mashite, ongaku o aishiteimasu.
Example (English): I love music even more than he does.

Meaning: Regardless of, irrespective of.
Formation: Noun + によらず
Example (Japanese): 結果は勉強時間によらず変わらないでしょう。
Example (Romaji): Kekka wa benkyou jikan ni yorazu kawaranai deshou.
Example (English): The result will not change regardless of the study time.

Grammar Point: Noun に先駆けて (〜ni saki gakete)
Meaning: Meaning 'ahead of', 'before', or 'preceding in time'.
Formation: Noun + に先駆けて
Example (Japanese): この映画は日本に先駆けて、アメリカで公開されました。
Example (Romaji): Kono eiga wa Nippon ni sakigakete, Amerika de koukai saremashita.
Example (English): This film was released in America ahead of Japan.

Grammar Point: Noun に即した Noun (A ni sokushita B)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'in accordance with', 'based on'.
Formation: Noun1 + に即した + Noun2
Example (Japanese): 社会のニーズに即した教育改革が必要だ。
Example (Romaji): Shakai no niizu ni sokushita kyouiku kaikaku ga hitsuyou da.
Example (English): We need an educational reform that is in accordance with the needs of society.

Grammar Point: Noun に即して Verb (〜ni soku shite ~)
Meaning: The grammar point Noun に即して Verb is used to mean 'to act in accordance with', 'in line with' or 'based on'.
Formation: Noun + に即して + Verb
Example (Japanese): 会社のポリシーに即して行動しましょう。
Example (Romaji): Kaisha no porishii ni soku shite koudou shimashou.
Example (English): Let's act in accordance with the company's policy.

Grammar Point: Noun に言わせれば (Noun ni iwasereba)
Meaning: Expresses 'according to', 'if you ask', 'in the opinion of'.
Formation: Noun + に言わせれば
Example (Japanese): 先生に言わせれば、毎日勉強することが重要だと言う。
Example (Romaji): Sensei ni iwasereba, mainichi benkyou suru koto ga juuyou da to iu.
Example (English): According to the teacher, it's important to study every day.

Grammar Point: Noun に限ったことではない (〜ni kagitta koto dewa nai)
Meaning: Indicates that something is not only limited to; 'not only', 'not just'.
Formation: Noun + に限ったことではない
Example (Japanese): この問題は日本に限ったことではない。
Example (Romaji): Kono mondai wa Nihon ni kagitta koto dewa nai.
Example (English): This issue is not only limited to Japan.

Grammar Point: Noun に限ったことでもない (~ni kagitta koto demo nai)
Meaning: 'Not limited to'; 'not just', 'not exclusively'.
Formation: Noun + に限ったことでもない
Example (Japanese): この試験が難しいのは、数学に限ったことでもない。
Example (Romaji): Kono shiken ga muzukashii no wa, suugaku ni kagitta koto demo nai.
Example (English): The exam being difficult is not limited to just math.

Meaning: Expresses the idea that 'nothing but', 'nothing is better than'.
Formation: Noun + に限る
Example (Japanese): こういう時には家族に話すに限る。
Example (Romaji): Kou iu toki ni wa kazoku ni hanasu ni kagiru.
Example (English): At times like this, there's nothing better than talking to your family.

Grammar Point: Noun ぬいた Noun (A nuita B)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'taking something out from something else'.
Formation: Noun1 + をぬいた + Noun2
Example (Japanese): このサラダはにんじんをぬいたサラダです。
Example (Romaji): Kono sarada wa ninjin o nuita sarada desu.
Example (English): This is a salad with the carrots removed.

Meaning: This is a way to express 'minus' or 'except for' some specific noun.
Formation: Noun + ぬいて
Example (Japanese): 私たちは、彼ぬいて全員が集まることができました。
Example (Romaji): Watashitachi wa, kare nuite zen'in ga atsumaru koto ga dekimashita.
Example (English): We were able to gather everyone except for him.

Meaning: Expresses the concept of doing something completely or thoroughly.
Formation: Verb-stem + ぬく
Example (Japanese): 彼は一日中本を読みぬく。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa ichinichijuu hon o yominuku.
Example (English): He will read the book all day long.

Grammar Point: Noun+のいかんだ (Noun no ikan da)
Meaning: Depends on; up to
Formation: Noun + のいかんだ/Noun + のいかんでは
Example (Japanese): 彼が来るのいかんで決めよう。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga kuru no ikan de kimeyou.
Example (English): Let's decide depending on whether he comes or not.

Grammar Point: Noun のいかんでは (Noun no ikan de wa)
Meaning: It depends on the Noun
Formation: Noun + のいかんでは
Example (Japanese): 試験の結果のいかんでは、大学の入学許可を得られるかどうかが決まります。
Example (Romaji): Shiken no kekka no ikan dewa, daigaku no nyuugaku kyoka o erareru ka douka ga kimarimasu.
Example (English): Whether you can get permission to enter university depends on the result of the exam.

Grammar Point: Noun のいかんにかかわらず (Noun no ikan ni kakawarazu)
Meaning: Regardless of, irrespective of.
Formation: Noun + のいかんにかかわらず
Example (Japanese): 結果のいかんにかかわらず、彼は決定を後悔しなかった。
Example (Romaji): Kekka no ikan ni kakawarazu, kare wa kettei wo koukai shinakatta.
Example (English): Regardless of the outcome, he didn't regret his decision.

Grammar Point: Noun のいかんによっては (Noun no ikan ni yotte wa)
Meaning: Depending on the matter; depending on noun
Formation: Noun + のいかんによっては
Example (Japanese): 天気のいかんによっては、ピクニックを延期しましょう。
Example (Romaji): Tenki no ikan ni yotte wa, pikunikku o enki shimashou.
Example (English): Depending on the weather, we should postpone the picnic.

Grammar Point: Noun のいかんによらず (~ no ikan ni yorazu)
Meaning: Means 'regardless of', 'irrespective of', or 'no matter'
Formation: Noun + のいかんによらず
Example (Japanese): 試験の結果のいかんによらず、自分を信じ続けてください。
Example (Romaji): Shiken no kekka no ikan ni yorazu, jibun o shinji tsudzukete kudasai.
Example (English): Regardless of the test results, keep believing in yourself.

Grammar Point: Noun のごとき Noun (A no gotoki B)
Meaning: Expresses 'like' or 'as if'; something/someone resembles something else strongly.
Formation: Noun1 + のごとき + Noun2
Example (Japanese): 彼は神のごとき存在だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kami no gotoki sonzai da.
Example (English): He is an existence like a god.

Grammar Point: Noun のことだから (〜no koto dakara)
Meaning: Because it is about ~, considering it's ~
Formation: Noun + のことだから
Example (Japanese): 彼のことだから、きっと大丈夫だと思う。
Example (Romaji): Kare no koto dakara, kitto daijoubu da to omou.
Example (English): Because it's him, I think it will certainly be fine.

Grammar Point: Noun の 嫌いがある (Noun no kirai ga aru)
Meaning: Have a dislike for a particular Noun
Formation: Noun + の嫌いがある
Example (Japanese): 彼は魚の嫌いがあるので、寿司を食べません。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa sakana no kirai ga aru node, sushi o tabemasen.
Example (English): He has a dislike for fish, so he doesn't eat sushi.

Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'Before doing something; on the verge of'.
Formation: Noun + の手前
Example (Japanese): 試験の手前、遊びに行くのはやめた方がいい。
Example (Romaji): Shiken no temae, asobi ni iku no wa yameta hou ga ii.
Example (English): Just before the exam, it's better to stop going out to play.

Meaning: Used to express the extreme or utmost point of something.
Formation: Noun + の極み
Example (Japanese): 彼の料理の極みは、誰もマネできない。
Example (Romaji): Kare no ryouri no kiwami wa, daremo mane dekinai.
Example (English): The pinnacle of his cooking is something nobody can imitate.

Meaning: Expresses 'the height of', 'the extreme of' something.
Formation: Noun + の至り
Example (Japanese): 彼の冗談には驚きの至りだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare no joudan ni wa odoroki no itari da.
Example (English): His jokes are the height of surprise.

Grammar Point: Noun はいざ知らず (~ wa iza shirazu)
Meaning: ‘I can understand it for ~, but for …? (surprising)’
Formation: Noun + はいざ知らず, Noun + とは/なんて/しかし etc.
Example (Japanese): 彼が遅れるのはいざ知らず、彼女まで遅刻するとは意外だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga okureru no wa iza shirazu, kanojo made chikoku suru to wa igai da.
Example (English): Well, I can understand him being late, but even her...? That's surprising.

Grammar Point: Noun はおろか～すら (Noun wa oroka ～sura)
Meaning: Expresses 'not to mention ~, even ~'.
Formation: Noun1 はおろか, Noun2 すら/さえ ～
Example (Japanese): 彼は走るはおろか、速く歩くことすらできない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa hashiru wa oroka, hayaku aruku koto sura dekinai.
Example (English): He can't even walk fast, let alone run.

Grammar Point: Noun はおろか～まで (~wa oroka ~made)
Meaning: Means 'not just A, but even B'; 'let alone A, even B'.
Formation: Noun1 + はおろか + Noun2 + まで
Example (Japanese): 彼は英語はおろか、日本語までペラペラなんです。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa eigo wa oroka, nihongo made perapera nan desu.
Example (English): He is not just fluent in English, but even in Japanese.

Grammar Point: Noun はおろか～も (Noun wa oroka ～ mo)
Meaning: 'Not only...but also', 'not to mention', 'to say nothing of'
Formation: Noun + はおろか + Noun + も
Example (Japanese): 絵を描くことはおろか、字さえ書けない。
Example (Romaji): E wo kaku koto wa oroka, ji sae kakenai.
Example (English): Needless to say drawing pictures, he can’t even write letters.

Grammar Point: Noun はさておき (~ wa sateoki)
Meaning: Means 'putting aside', 'aside from', 'notwithstanding'.
Formation: Noun + はさておき
Example (Japanese): 試験の結果はさておき、この学期はとても学ぶことが多かった。
Example (Romaji): Shiken no kekka wa sateoki, kono gakki wa totemo manabu koto ga ookatta.
Example (English): Aside from the exam results, I learned a lot this semester.

Grammar Point: Noun + はどうであれ (~ wa dou de are)
Meaning: This phrase means 'regardless of' or 'no matter how…'.
Formation: Noun + はどうであれ
Example (Japanese): 天候はどうであれ、試合は行われます。
Example (Romaji): Tenkou wa dou de are, shiai wa okonawaremasu.
Example (English): No matter what the weather is, the match will be held.

Meaning: Expresses a state in which something is entirely covered or filled with something else.
Formation: Noun + まみれ
Example (Japanese): 彼は泥まみれになって帰ってきた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa doro mamire ni natte kaette kita.
Example (English): He returned home covered in mud.

Grammar Point: Noun もさることながら Noun も (A mo saru koto nagara B mo)
Meaning: Means 'not only... but also'; the second noun is especially emphasized.
Formation: Noun1 + もさることながら + Noun2 + も
Example (Japanese): 彼の歌唱力もさることながら、ダンスも素晴らしい。
Example (Romaji): Kare no kashou-ryoku mo saru koto nagara, dansu mo subarashii.
Example (English): Not only his singing ability but also his dancing is wonderful.

Meaning: Used to express 'as well as', 'also', or 'at the same time'.
Formation: Noun + も兼ねて
Example (Japanese): 散歩も兼ねて、公園に行きました。
Example (Romaji): Sanpo mo kanete, kouen ni ikimashita.
Example (English): I went to the park, also for a walk.

Meaning: Used to express that combined with something else, it caused a certain outcome.
Formation: Noun + も相まって
Example (Japanese): 気候も相まって、この地域は農業に適しています。
Example (Romaji): Kikou mo aimatte, kono chiiki wa nougyou ni tekishiteimasu.
Example (English): Combined with the climate, this area is suitable for agriculture.

Grammar Point: Noun を おいて他に Verb ない (〜wo oite hoka ni〜nai)
Meaning: Means 'apart from ~ there's nothing else,' implying the Noun is the best or most suitable choice.
Formation: Noun + をおいて他に + Verb negative form
Example (Japanese): この仕事を彼に任せる人をおいて他にいない。
Example (Romaji): Kono shigoto wo kare ni makaseru hito wo oite hoka ni inai.
Example (English): Apart from him, there's no one else to entrust this job to.

Meaning: Used to indicate means, methods, or time; 'with', 'by means of', 'at'.
Formation: Noun + をもって
Example (Japanese): 彼は誠実さをもって人々に信頼されています。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa seijitsusa wo motte hitobito ni shinrai sarete imasu.
Example (English): He is trusted by people with his honesty.

Grammar Point: Noun をものともせずに (Noun wo mono tomo sezu ni)
Meaning: Expresses the idea that 'despite something, action was carried out', translating to 'without being fazed by something'.
Formation: Noun + をものともせずに
Example (Japanese): 彼女は怖さをものともせずに、暗闇の中へ進んで行った。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa kowasa wo mono tomo sezu ni, kurayami no naka e susunde itta.
Example (English): Despite her fear, she went ahead into the darkness.

Grammar Point: Noun をよそに (~wo yoso ni)
Meaning: Despite; Notwithstanding; Regardless of
Formation: Noun + をよそに
Example (Japanese): 経済危機をよそに、彼は高級な車を買った。
Example (Romaji): Keizai kiki wo yoso ni, kare wa koukyuu na kuruma wo katta.
Example (English): Despite the economic crisis, he bought a luxury car.

Grammar Point: Noun を余儀なくされる (Noun wo yogi naku sareru)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of being forced into a certain situation, 'to be compelled', 'to be obliged'.
Formation: Noun + を + 余儀なくされる
Example (Japanese): 彼は経済的困難により、退学を余儀なくされた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa keizai-teki konnan ni yori, taigaku wo yogi naku saremashita.
Example (English): Due to financial difficulties, he was forced to drop out of school.

Grammar Point: Noun を前提として (Noun wo zentei toshite)
Meaning: Used to express 'on the assumption of', 'based on'.
Formation: Noun + を前提として
Example (Japanese): 成功を前提として、ビジネスプランを作成しました。
Example (Romaji): Seikou wo zentei toshite, bijinesu puran wo sakusei shimashita.
Example (English): We made a business plan on the assumption of success.

Grammar Point: Noun を前提にして (Noun wo zentei ni shite)
Meaning: Assuming; presupposing; on the assumption of.
Formation: Noun + を前提にして
Example (Japanese): 好天を前提にして、明日のピクニックの計画を立てました。
Example (Romaji): Kouten wo zentei ni shite, ashita no pikunikku no keikaku wo tatemashita.
Example (English): We planned tomorrow's picnic assuming fine weather.

Grammar Point: Noun を境にして (Noun wo sakai ni shite)
Meaning: Means 'as a turning point', 'since (time)', or 'from (time) on'.
Formation: Noun + を境に(して)
Example (Japanese): 父の死を境にして、彼の性格が一変した。
Example (Romaji): Chichi no shi wo sakai ni shite, kare no seikaku ga ippen shita.
Example (English): His personality changed completely since his father's death.

Grammar Point: Noun を機にして (~wo ki ni shite)
Meaning: To take the opportunity to; taking the occasion to; on the occasion of.
Formation: Noun + を機にして
Example (Japanese): 引っ越しを機にして、家具を新しくしました。
Example (Romaji): Hikkoshi wo ki ni shite, kagu wo atarashiku shimashita.
Example (English): I took the opportunity of moving to get new furniture.

Grammar Point: Noun を皮切りに / を皮切りにして (Noun wo kawakiri ni / wo kawakiri ni shite)
Meaning: Used to indicate the starting point of some series of events or actions; 'starting with', 'beginning with'.
Formation: Noun + を皮切りに / を皮切りにして
Example (Japanese): 彼はその論文を皮切りにして複数の研究を開始した。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa sono ronbun o kawakiri ni shite fukusū no kenkyū o kaishi shita.
Example (English): Starting with that thesis, he started multiple research projects.

Grammar Point: Noun を皮切りにして (Noun wo kawakiri ni shite)
Meaning: Used to express 'Starting with', 'Beginning with'
Formation: Noun + を皮切りに (して)
Example (Japanese): 彼はその日を皮切りにして毎日ジムに通い始めました。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa sono hi o kawakiri ni shite mainichi jimu ni kayoi hajimemashita.
Example (English): Starting from that day, he began to go to the gym every day.

Grammar Point: Noun を禁じ得ない (〜wo kinjienai)
Meaning: 'Cannot help but do', or 'inevitable'
Formation: Noun + を禁じ得ない
Example (Japanese): この結果には驚きを禁じ得ない。
Example (Romaji): Kono kekka ni wa odoroki o kinjienai.
Example (English): I can't help but be surprised at this result.

Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'through' or 'via'; going through some process or phase.
Formation: Noun + を経て
Example (Japanese): 彼は苦労を経て成功を手に入れた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kurō o hete seikō o te ni ireta.
Example (English): He achieved success through hardships.

Meaning: Based on; taking into account; in light of
Formation: Noun + を踏まえて
Example (Japanese): 過去の結果を踏まえて、新たな計画を立てました。
Example (Romaji): Kako no kekka o fumaete, aratana keikaku o tatemashita.
Example (English): Based on previous results, we have made a new plan.

Grammar Point: Noun を限りに (Noun wo kagiri ni)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'as of', 'with', or 'from', indicating the end of something or a point of change.
Formation: Noun + を限りに
Example (Japanese): 今年度を限りに、この大学での教授活動を終えるつもりです。
Example (Romaji): Konnendo o kagiri ni, kono daigaku de no kyouju katsudou o oeru tsumori desu.
Example (English): I intend to end my teaching activities at this university as of this academic year.

Meaning: Indicates 'like' or 'as' something or someone; 'equivalent to', 'around'.
Formation: Noun + 並み
Example (Japanese): 彼はプロのボクサー並みの力を持っています。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa puro no bokusaa nami no chikara o motte imasu.
Example (English): He has power equivalent to a professional boxer.

Meaning: Expresses a condition or requirement for something to be established: 'on the assumption that', 'under the condition of'.
Formation: Noun + 前提で
Example (Japanese): 説明できる英語力がある前提で、この仕事を引き受けてください。
Example (Romaji): Setsumei dekiru eigo-ryoku ga aru zentei de, kono shigoto o hikiukete kudasai.
Example (English): Please take on this job on the assumption that you have enough English skills to explain.

Grammar Point: Verbる / Noun(である) + 限り(は) (kagiri (wa))
Meaning: Expresses 'as long as', 'while this condition is true'.
Formation:
Verb-dictionary form + 限り(は)
Noun(である) + 限り(は)
Example (Japanese): 私が生きている限りは、あなたを支えます。
Example (Romaji): Watashi ga ikite iru kagiri wa, anata o sasaemasu.
Example (English): As long as I'm alive, I will support you.

Meaning: Expresses doing something while doing another; 'while', 'on the occasion of'.
Formation: Verb (dictionary or -ます stem) + がてら
Example (Japanese): 散歩がてらに郵便局へ行った。
Example (Romaji): Sanpo gatera ni yūbinkyoku e itta.
Example (English): I went to the post office while taking a walk.

Meaning: Often used in the pattern 'Xこそすれ、Y〜ない', meaning 'One might do X, but definitely not Y'.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + こそすれ、(絶対に)～ない
Example (Japanese): 彼は友達を助けこそすれ、自分を卑下することはありません。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa tomodachi o tasuke koso sure, jibun o higesuru koto wa arimasen.
Example (English): He might help his friends, but he never belittles himself.

Meaning: Expresses 'being forced to do something' or 'being made to do something'.
Formation: Verb-casual (non-past) + させられる
Example (Japanese): 彼に無理やり飲ませられた。
Example (Romaji): Kare ni muriyari nomaserareta.
Example (English): He forced me to drink against my will.

Grammar Point: Verb ざるを得ない (~ zaru wo enai)
Meaning: 'Cannot but', 'have no choice but to', 'forced to'
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ざるを得ない (する → せざるを得ない)
Example (Japanese): この仕事が嫌ならもう辞めざるを得ない。
Example (Romaji): Kono shigoto ga iya nara mō yamezaru o enai.
Example (English): If you hate this job, you have no choice but to quit.

Meaning: Expressing regret for not having done something; not being able to; missing the chance to do it.
Formation: Verb-ない form (remove ない) + ずじまい
Example (Japanese): 日本へ来たのに、一度も富士山を見ずじまいで帰国してしまった。
Example (Romaji): Nihon e kita noni, ichidomo Fuji-san o mizu jimai de kikoku shite shimatta.
Example (English): I came to Japan but ended up going home without ever getting to see Mt. Fuji.

Meaning: Means 'Even without doing (X), (Y) can still happen'.
Formation: Verb-negative stem + ずとも
Example (Japanese): 朝ごはんを食べずとも、働くことができます。
Example (Romaji): Asagohan o tabezu tomo, hataraku koto ga dekimasu.
Example (English): Even without eating breakfast, I can work.

Grammar Point: Verb ずにはおかない (~zuni wa okanai)
Meaning: Expresses 'cannot help but...', 'will definitely...', or 'must do something'.
Formation: Verb-ない form (remove ない) + ずにはおかない
Example (Japanese): 彼が困っていると聞いたら、助けずにはおかない。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga komatte iru to kiitara, tasukezuni wa okanai.
Example (English): If I hear he is in trouble, I cannot help but assist him.

Grammar Point: Verb ずにはすまない (Verb zuni wa sumanai)
Meaning: 'Cannot do without...', 'unavoidable', 'have to'.
Formation: Verb-ない form (remove ない) + ずにはすまない
Example (Japanese): この問題を解決しないと、社会全体が影響を受けるので、解決せずにはすまない。
Example (Romaji): Kono mondai o kaiketsu shinai to, shakai zentai ga eikyō o ukeru node, kaiketsu sezu ni wa sumanai.
Example (English): Since this issue will affect the entire society if not resolved, we cannot do without solving it.

Grammar Point: Verb そうにない (Verb sou ni nai)
Meaning: Expresses unlikelihood or that something does not seem likely to happen.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + そうにない
Example (Japanese): 彼はそんなに早く走れそうにない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa sonna ni hayaku hashire sō ni nai.
Example (English): He doesn't seem likely to run that fast.

Grammar Point: Verb そうもない (〜sou mo nai)
Meaning: Expresses negative potential; 'it doesn't seem like...', 'it's not likely...'.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + そうもない
Example (Japanese): 今日中に仕事を終えそうもない。
Example (Romaji): Kyōjū ni shigoto o oesō mo nai.
Example (English): It doesn't seem like I'll finish my work today.

Meaning: Expresses that as soon as one action finishes, another begins immediately.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + そばから
Example (Japanese): 掃除をするそばから子供たちが散らかす。
Example (Romaji): Sōji o suru soba kara kodomo-tachi ga chirakasu.
Example (English): As soon as I clean, the kids mess it up.

Grammar Point: Verb たが最後 (〜ta ga saigo)
Meaning: Emphasizes 'once something happens, there is no going back'; 'once', 'as soon as', etc.
Formation: Verb-casual, past (た form) + が最後
Example (Japanese): 彼が一度怒ったが最後、誰も彼を止めることはできません。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga ichido okotta ga saigo, dare mo kare o tomeru koto wa dekimasen.
Example (English): Once he gets angry, no one can stop him.

Grammar Point: Verb たことにしてください (~ ta koto ni shite kudasai)
Meaning: Asking someone to pretend or accept that something has already happened or taken a certain state.
Formation: Verb (past, casual) + ことにしてください
Example (Japanese): 昨日のことは忘れたことにしてください。
Example (Romaji): Kinou no koto wa wasureta koto ni shite kudasai.
Example (English): Please act as if you have forgotten about yesterday.

Grammar Point: Verb たら Verb たで (~ tara ~ tade)
Meaning: Conveys that if something happens (or doesn’t happen), there is a particular consequence or situation either way.
Formation: Verb-た form + ら + (same Verb-た form) + で
Example (Japanese): 行ったら行ったで大変だし、行かなかったら行かなかったで後悔しそうだ。
Example (Romaji): Ittara itta de taihen da shi, ikanakattara ikanakatta de kōkai shisō da.
Example (English): If I go, it’s a hassle; if I don’t go, I’ll regret it.

Grammar Point: Verb たら きりがない (Verb tara kiri ga nai)
Meaning: Indicates an endless or unending cycle once an action is started; 'if one starts doing something, it will not stop.'
Formation: Verb-た form + ら + きりがない
Example (Japanese): このエンジンを修理したら、またすぐ壊れて、直したらきりがない。
Example (Romaji): Kono enjin o shuuri shitara, mata sugu kowarete, naoshitara kiri ga nai.
Example (English): If I fix this engine, it breaks again, and if I fix it again, it never ends.

Meaning: Expresses that once a certain action happens, the situation changes irreversibly—usually in a negative way.
Formation: Verb-た form + ら最後
Example (Japanese): このゲームを始めたら最後、時間の経つのを忘れてしまいます。
Example (Romaji): Kono gēmu o hajimetara saigo, jikan no tatsu no o wasurete shimaimasu.
Example (English): Once you start this game, you completely lose track of time.

Grammar Point: Verb つ Verb つ (Verb tsu Verb tsu)
Meaning: Expresses two alternating actions happening repeatedly.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + つ + Verb-ますstem + つ
Example (Japanese): 朝から晩まで働きつ勉強しつで、疲れてしまった。
Example (Romaji): Asa kara ban made hataraki tsu benkyō shi tsu de, tsukarete shimatta.
Example (English): I’ve been working and studying from morning till night, and now I’m exhausted.

Grammar Point: Verb てからというもの (Verb te kara to iu mono)
Meaning: Expresses that ever since a certain event happened, a condition has continued until now.
Formation: Verb-て form + からというもの
Example (Japanese): 彼女と別れてからというもの、一人で過ごす時間が増えました。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo to wakarete kara to iu mono, hitori de sugosu jikan ga fuemashita.
Example (English): Ever since I broke up with her, I've spent more time alone.

Meaning: Emphasizes 'only by doing something, a certain result or realization can occur.'
Formation: Verb-て form + こそ
Example (Japanese): 実際に使ってこそ、その価値を理解できる。
Example (Romaji): Jissai ni tsukatte koso, sono kachi o rikai dekiru.
Example (English): You can only understand its value by actually using it.

Meaning: Expresses a repeated pattern or cycle, often implying a frustrating outcome; 'whenever X happens, Y happens again.'
Formation: Verb-て form + は
Example (Japanese): 彼女に会っては、いつも緊張してしまいます。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo ni atte wa, itsumo kinchō shite shimaimasu.
Example (English): Whenever I meet her, I get nervous.

Grammar Point: Verb ては Verb (~ te wa ~)
Meaning: Expresses a repeated pattern of action; translates as 'every time', 'whenever', etc.
Formation: Verb-て form + は + Verb
Example (Japanese): 私が通勤しては、電子書籍を読んでいます。
Example (Romaji): Watashi ga tsūkin shite wa, denshi shoseki o yonde imasu.
Example (English): Whenever I commute, I read e-books.

Meaning: Expresses 'even if it means doing...', 'no matter what it takes'.
Formation: Verb-て form + までも
Example (Japanese): 試験に合格するために、寝る時間を削ってまでも勉強します。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ni gōkaku suru tame ni, neru jikan o kezutte mademo benkyō shimasu.
Example (English): I will study to pass the exam, even if it means cutting down on sleep.

Grammar Point: Verb てみせる (Verb te miseru)
Meaning: 'Show by doing', 'demonstrate', 'prove by action'.
Formation: Verb-て form + みせる
Example (Japanese): 彼はそのパズルを解いてみせた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa sono pazuru o toite miseta.
Example (English): He solved the puzzle to show me.

Grammar Point: Verb てやまない (Verb te yamanai)
Meaning: Used with certain emotional/mental verbs to show a strong, unceasing emotion: 'can't stop', 'never cease to'.
Formation: Verb-て form + やまない (common with certain verbs)
Example (Japanese): 私は母を思ってやまない。
Example (Romaji): Watashi wa haha o omotte yamanai.
Example (English): I can't stop thinking of my mother.

Grammar Point: Verb ないではおかない (~ nai de wa okanai)
Meaning: Means 'cannot help but do', 'will definitely do', or 'is bound to happen'.
Formation: Verb-ない form + ではおかない
Example (Japanese): 彼女は毎回遅刻をしては、先生に怒られないではおかない。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa maikai chikoku o shite wa, sensei ni okorarenaide wa okanai.
Example (English): Every time she's late, she inevitably gets scolded by the teacher.

Grammar Point: Verb ないではすまない (Verb nai dewa sumanai)
Meaning: 'Cannot end without doing', 'must do'—an unavoidable moral or social necessity.
Formation: Verb-ない form + ではすまない
Example (Japanese): 失敗をしたら、謝らないではすまない。
Example (Romaji): Shippai o shitara, ayamaranai de wa sumanai.
Example (English): If you make a mistake, you have to apologize—there’s no way around it.

Grammar Point: Verb ないまでも (Verb nai made mo)
Meaning: 'Even if not to the extent of...', 'although not completely...'.
Formation: Verb-ない form + までも
Example (Japanese): 全てを理解しないまでも、基本的なことは分かってほしい。
Example (Romaji): Subete o rikai shinai made mo, kihonteki na koto wa wakatte hoshii.
Example (English): Even if you don't understand everything, I'd like you at least to grasp the basics.

Grammar Point: Verb ないものだろうか (Verb nai mono darou ka)
Meaning: Expressing hope or wonder if something can be done: 'Isn't there a way...?', 'Can't we...?'
Formation: Verb-negative (often negative potential) + ものだろうか
Example (Japanese): もっと時間があれば、ここに来られないものだろうか。
Example (Romaji): Motto jikan ga areba, koko ni korarenai mono darou ka.
Example (English): If I had more time, wouldn't it be possible to come here?

Grammar Point: Verb ないものでもない (Verb nai mono demo nai)
Meaning: Expresses the idea that it's not entirely impossible or non-existent: 'It's not that I don't...', 'It's not that there aren't...'
Formation: Verb-negative form (ない form) + ものでもない
Example (Japanese): 旅行に行きたいと思わないものでもない。
Example (Romaji): Ryokou ni ikitai to omowanai mono demo nai.
Example (English): It's not that I never want to travel.

Grammar Point: Verb の ない Noun (~ no nai ~)
Meaning: Used to modify a noun with a negative verb form; 'a Noun without (Verb)'.
Formation: Verb in negative form + の + Noun
Example (Japanese): 笑いのない人生は、つまらない。
Example (Romaji): Warai no nai jinsei wa, tsumaranai.
Example (English): A life without laughter is boring.

Grammar Point: Verb ば きりがない (〜ba kiri ga nai)
Meaning: Indicates there's no end once you start listing, doing, or saying something: 'If one starts to..., there will be no end.'
Formation: Verb-conditional form (ば) + きりがない
Example (Japanese): 悪口を言い始めればきりがない。
Example (Romaji): Waruguchi o iihajimereba kiri ga nai.
Example (English): Once I start speaking ill of someone, there's no end.

Grammar Point: Verb もしないで (~ mo shinai de)
Meaning: Means 'without even doing'.
Formation: Verb (masu stem) + もしないで
Example (Japanese): 調べもしないで、答えを書きました。
Example (Romaji): Shirabe mo shinai de, kotae o kakimashita.
Example (English): I wrote the answer without even investigating.

Meaning: Expresses a strong denial or refusal: 'I would never...', 'No way I would...'.
Formation: Verb (masu stem) + やしない
Example (Japanese): こんな時に泣きやしない。
Example (Romaji): Konna toki ni naki-yashinai.
Example (English): I would never cry at a time like this.

Grammar Point: Verb よう (~ you / ~ you ni)
Meaning: Expresses 'the way/manner of doing something' or 'in order to / so that / try to'.
Formation: Verb (dictionary or negative form) + ように (する / etc.)
Example (Japanese): この問題を解くように努力します。
Example (Romaji): Kono mondai o toku you ni doryoku shimasu.
Example (English): I will try to solve this problem.

Grammar Point: Verb ようか Verbるまいか (Verb you ka Verb ru mai ka)
Meaning: Expresses indecision: 'Should I do it or not?'.
Formation: Verb-volitional form + か + Verb-volitional negative form (まい) + か
Example (Japanese): 彼に話そうか話すまいか、本当に迷っている。
Example (Romaji): Kare ni hanasou ka hanasu mai ka, hontou ni mayotte iru.
Example (English): I'm really unsure whether to talk to him or not.

Grammar Point: Verb ようが Verb るまいが (Verb you ga Verb ru mai ga)
Meaning: Expresses 'whether or not', 'no matter if something happens or not'.
Formation: Verb-volitional form + が + Verb-negative volitional form + が
Example (Japanese): 彼が来ようが来るまいが、パーティーは始まります。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga koyou ga kurumai ga, paatii wa hajimarimasu.
Example (English): Whether he comes or not, the party will start.

Grammar Point: Verb ようがない (〜you ga nai)
Meaning: Expresses 'no way to do something,' 'impossible to do'.
Formation: Verb (masu stem) + ようがない
Example (Japanese): 電車が混んでいて、動きようがない。
Example (Romaji): Densha ga konde ite, ugoki you ga nai.
Example (English): The train is so crowded that I can't move.

Grammar Point: Verb ようと Verbる まいと (Verb you to Verb ru mai to)
Meaning: This structure indicates that regardless of whether one does (verb) or not, the outcome/attitude remains unchanged.
Formation: Verb-volitional + と + Verb-negative volitional (～まい) + と
Example (Japanese): あなたが来ようと来るまいと、パーティーは予定通りに始まります。
Example (Romaji): Anata ga koyou to kuru mai to, paatii wa yotei doori ni hajimarimasu.
Example (English): Whether you come or not, the party will start as scheduled.

Grammar Point: Verb ようにも (〜you ni mo)
Meaning: Used to express 'even though one wants to do something, one can't for some reason'.
Formation: Verb-volitional form + にも + (reason/potential negative, etc.)
Example (Japanese): もう少し速く走ろうにも、足が痛くて無理だ。
Example (Romaji): Mou sukoshi hayaku hashirou ni mo, ashi ga itakute muri da.
Example (English): I'd like to run a bit faster, but I can’t because my leg hurts.

Grammar Point: Verb ようにも Verb れない (〜you ni mo 〜renai)
Meaning: Expresses the inability to do something even if one wants/tries.
Formation: Verb-volitional form + にも + (potential negative form / reason)
Example (Japanese): 彼を信じようにも信じられない証拠がある。
Example (Romaji): Kare o shinjiyou ni mo shinjirarenai shouko ga aru.
Example (English): Even if I want to believe him, there's evidence that prevents me from doing so.

Grammar Point: Verb ようもない (~you mo nai)
Meaning: Expresses 'it's impossible to do something'.
Formation: Verb-ます stem + ようもない
Example (Japanese): この問題は解きようもない。
Example (Romaji): Kono mondai wa toki you mo nai.
Example (English): It's impossible to solve this problem.

Grammar Point: Verbる がままに (〜ga mama ni)
Meaning: Expresses 'letting something happen as it is'; 'just as something does'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + がままに
Example (Japanese): 窓を開けるがままにしておいたら、風が部屋に入ってきました。
Example (Romaji): Mado o akeru ga mama ni shite oitara, kaze ga heya ni haitte kimashita.
Example (English): I left the window open as it was, and the wind came into the room.

Grammar Point: Verbる が早いか (verb-ru ga hayai ka)
Meaning: Expresses 'as soon as...' or 'the moment when...'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + が早いか
Example (Japanese): 部屋に入るが早いか、彼はテレビをつけた。
Example (Romaji): Heya ni hairu ga hayai ka, kare wa terebi o tsuketa.
Example (English): No sooner had he entered the room than he turned on the TV.

Grammar Point: Verbる くらいなら (〜ru kurai nara)
Meaning: Expresses preference to avoid something: 'rather than...', 'if it comes to doing X, I'd rather...'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + くらいなら
Example (Japanese): 一人で行くくらいなら、家にいるほうがましです。
Example (Romaji): Hitori de iku kurai nara, ie ni iru hou ga mashi desu.
Example (English): I'd rather stay at home than go alone.

Grammar Point: Verbる こと なし に (Verb-ru koto nashi ni)
Meaning: Used to express 'without doing something'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ことなしに
Example (Japanese): 試験を勉強することなしに、合格しました。
Example (Romaji): Shiken o benkyou suru koto nashi ni, goukaku shimashita.
Example (English): I passed the exam without studying.

Grammar Point: Verbる ことのないように (Verb-ru koto no nai you ni)
Meaning: Expresses the desire or effort to prevent something: 'so as not to...', 'to avoid...'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ことのないように
Example (Japanese): 車をなくすことのないように、駐車場で必ずロックしましょう。
Example (Romaji): Kuruma o nakusu koto no nai you ni, chuushajou de kanarazu rokku shimashou.
Example (English): Lock your car in the parking lot so you don't lose it.

Grammar Point: Verbる ときりがない (verb-ru to kiri ga nai)
Meaning: Used to indicate that something can go on endlessly or without limits.
Formation: Verb-casual + と + きりがない
Example (Japanese): 彼の悪口を言うときりがない。
Example (Romaji): Kare no waruguchi o iu to kiri ga nai.
Example (English): If we start talking about his faults, there's no end.

Grammar Point: Verbる ともなく Verb (Verb-ru tomonaku Verb)
Meaning: Used to express 'without a particular intention', 'unconsciously', or 'before one knows it'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ともなく + Verb
Example (Japanese): 遠くを見るともなく窓の外を眺めた。
Example (Romaji): Tooku o miru tomonaku mado no soto o nagameta.
Example (English): I found myself gazing out the window, not really looking at anything in particular.

Grammar Point: Verbる ともなしに Verb (Verb-ru tomonashi ni Verb)
Meaning: Expresses doing something unintentionally or without conscious thought.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ともなしに + Verb
Example (Japanese): 本を読むともなしに眠ってしまった。
Example (Romaji): Hon o yomu tomonashi ni nemutte shimatta.
Example (English): I ended up falling asleep while reading the book without really meaning to.

Meaning: Expresses 'as soon as' or 'the moment'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + なり
Example (Japanese): 家に帰るなり、すぐに寝た。
Example (Romaji): Ie ni kaeru nari, sugu ni neta.
Example (English): As soon as I got home, I went to sleep.

Grammar Point: Verbる にとどまらず～も (Verb-ru ni todomarazu ~ mo)
Meaning: Expresses 'not only… but also', 'not limited to…'.
Formation: Noun / Verb-dictionary form + にとどまらず + も/ほかのこと
Example (Japanese): 彼は仕事にとどまらず、ボランティア活動もしている。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa shigoto ni todomarazu, borantia katsudou mo shite iru.
Example (English): He does not just work; he also does volunteer activities.

Grammar Point: Verbる にはあたらない (Verb-ru ni wa ataranai)
Meaning: Used to say 'there is no need to...', 'it’s not necessary to...'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + にはあたらない
Example (Japanese): パニックに陥るにはあたらない。
Example (Romaji): Panikku ni ochiiru ni wa ataranai.
Example (English): There’s no need to panic.

Meaning: Indicates that doing the verb is impossible or difficult, even if one wants to.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + にも + (reason it can't be done)
Example (Japanese): 明日雨が降ったとしても、傘を持つにも荷物が多すぎる。
Example (Romaji): Ashita ame ga futta to shite mo, kasa o motsu ni mo nimotsu ga oosugiru.
Example (English): Even if it rains tomorrow, I have too much luggage to bring an umbrella.

Grammar Point: Verbる にも Verb れない (Verb-ru ni mo Verb-re nai)
Meaning: Expresses: 'Even if I try/want to do something, I cannot.'
Formation: Verb-volitional + にも + Verb-potential negative
Example (Japanese): 彼を理解しようにも理解できない。
Example (Romaji): Kare o rikai shiyou ni mo rikai dekinai.
Example (English): Even if I try to understand him, I can't.

Grammar Point: Verbる べからざる Noun (Verb-ru bekara zaru Noun)
Meaning: Used to express what should not be done; 'must not', 'should not'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + べからざる + Noun
Example (Japanese): 人を裏切るべからざる行為だ。
Example (Romaji): Hito o uragiru bekara zaru koui da.
Example (English): Betraying others is an act that must not be done.

Grammar Point: Verbる べからず (〜ru bekara zu)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'must not do' or 'should not do'.
Formation: Verb-ru + べからず
Example (Japanese): 嘘をつくべからず。
Example (Romaji): Uso o tsuku bekara zu.
Example (English): One must not tell lies.

Meaning: Expresses the meaning of 'in order to', 'for the purpose of'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + べく
Example (Japanese): 成功するべく、日々努力しています。
Example (Romaji): Seikou suru beku, hibi doryoku shite imasu.
Example (English): In order to succeed, I am working hard every day.

Grammar Point: Verbる べくもない (Verb-ru beku mo nai)
Meaning: Means 'it's impossible to...' or 'there's no way to...'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + べくもない
Example (Japanese): その問題はとても難しく、解くべくもない。
Example (Romaji): Sono mondai wa totemo muzukashiku, toku beku mo nai.
Example (English): That problem is so difficult that it's impossible to solve.

Grammar Point: Verbる までもない (〜ru made mo nai)
Meaning: It's not necessary to the extent of; no need to.
Formation: Verb-る + までもない
Example (Japanese): そんなに心配するまでもない。
Example (Romaji): Sonna ni shinpai suru made mo nai.
Example (English): There's no need to worry that much.

Grammar Point: Verbる ものとする (〜ru mono to suru)
Meaning: Assuming or deciding something as...
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ものとする
Example (Japanese): ここでの話し合いは秘密とするものとします。
Example (Romaji): Koko de no hanashiai wa himitsu to suru mono to shimasu.
Example (English): The discussions here are to be kept confidential.

Grammar Point: Verbる や否や (Verb-ru ya ina ya)
