Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'as soon as', 'the moment...'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + や否や
Example (Japanese): 彼女が家に帰るや否や、すぐにテレビをつけました。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo ga ie ni kaeru ya ina ya, sugu ni terebi o tsukemashita.
Example (English): As soon as she returned home, she turned on the TV.

Grammar Point: Verbる 始末だ (〜ru shimatsu da)
Meaning: Indicates a (often unfortunate) result or conclusion of an action.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + 始末だ
Example (Japanese): 忘れてしまって、パスポートを家に置いてくる始末だった。
Example (Romaji): Wasurete shimatte, pasupooto o ie ni oite-kuru shimatsu datta.
Example (English): I ended up leaving my passport at home because I forgot.

Grammar Point: Verbる 嫌いがある (～ru kirai ga aru)
Meaning: Tendency to do a negative action; have a bad habit of ~.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + 嫌いがある
Example (Japanese): 彼女は遅刻する嫌いがある。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa chikoku suru kirai ga aru.
Example (English): She has a tendency to be late.

Grammar Point: いつまで～のやら (itsumade ~ no yara)
Meaning: Expresses uncertainty regarding duration; 'don't know when... will end'.
Formation: いつまで + Verb (dictionary form) + のやら
Example (Japanese): この試験勉強はいつまで続くのやら。
Example (Romaji): Kono shiken benkyou wa itsumade tsuzuku no yara.
Example (English): I don't know when this exam study will end.

Grammar Point: ～が Verb られる (〜ga Verb rareru)
Meaning: Expresses potential or ability to do something; 'can', 'able to'.
Formation:
❶ (Group 1) Verb:  書く → 書ける / 飲む → 飲める, etc.
❷ (Group 2) Verb-ます stem + られる (食べる→食べられる、見る→見られる)
Example (Japanese): 彼がこの問題を解けると思いますか？
Example (Romaji): Kare ga kono mondai o tokeru to omoimasu ka?
Example (English): Do you think he can solve this problem?

Meaning: Expressing unexpected outcomes; 'just when I thought...', 'but...'.
Formation: Sentence + かと思いきや (Verb plain form, i-/na-Adjective, or Noun + だ + かと思いきや)
Example (Japanese): 明日は晴れるかと思いきや、まさかの雨が降った。
Example (Romaji): Ashita wa hareru ka to omoikiya, masaka no ame ga futta.
Example (English): I thought it would be sunny tomorrow, but unexpectedly it rained.

Meaning: Expresses the reason or cause; 'because', 'due to', 'as a result of'.
Formation: Noun / Verb / Adjective + がゆえに
Example (Japanese): 愛情がゆえに、彼は彼女を許した。
Example (Romaji): Aijou ga yue ni, kare wa kanojo o yurushita.
Example (English): Because of love, he forgave her.

Grammar Point: ～がゆえの Noun (〜ga yue no Noun)
Meaning: Expresses the reason or cause for something; 'because of', 'due to'.
Formation: Noun / Verb-dictionary form + がゆえの + Noun
Example (Japanese): 愛がゆえの悲しみ。
Example (Romaji): Ai ga yue no kanashimi.
Example (English): Sadness due to love.

Grammar Point: ～から Noun に 至る まで (〜kara 〜ni itaru made)
Meaning: Expressing range from one thing to another; 'from...to', 'ranging from...to'.
Formation: Noun (start) + から + Noun (end) + に至るまで
Example (Japanese): このバンドの曲は、青年から老人に至るまで、人々に愛されています。
Example (Romaji): Kono bando no kyoku wa, seinen kara roujin ni itaru made, hitobito ni aisarete imasu.
Example (English): The songs of this band are loved by people ranging from the young to the elderly.

Meaning: To seem like; as if; as though.
Formation: Verb-て + ごとく / Noun + の + ごとく
Example (Japanese): 彼は鳥のごとく飛んでいるように見えた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa tori no gotoku tonde iru you ni mieta.
Example (English): He looked as though he was flying like a bird.

Meaning: Used to express the reason or premise for a decision or judgment; 'since', 'because'.
Formation: Verb (plain form) + こととて / Noun + の + こととて / (な-Adjective + な) + こととて
Example (Japanese): 彼は裁判に勝つために全資産を使うこととて、弁護士に頼んだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa saiban ni katsu tame ni zenshisan o tsukau koto tote, bengoshi ni tanonda.
Example (English): Since he's using all his assets to win the trial, he hired a lawyer.

Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'was able to do without'; 'managed to avoid'.
Formation: Verb-ず form + に + すんだ
Example (Japanese): 彼は事故を起こさずにすんだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa jiko o okosazu ni sunda.
Example (English): He managed to avoid having an accident.

Grammar Point: ～だろうとなかろうと (〜darou to nakarou to)
Meaning: Expresses 'regardless of whether it is or isn't'.
Formation: Noun / i-Adjective / na-Adjective / Verb + だろうとなかろうと
Example (Japanese): 試験が難しいだろうとなかろうと、全力で頑張ります。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ga muzukashii darou to nakarou to, zenryoku de ganbarimasu.
Example (English): Regardless of whether the exam is difficult or not, I will do my best.

Meaning: Expresses the speaker's intention or plan.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + つもりだ
Example (Japanese): 明日は早く起きるつもりです。
Example (Romaji): Ashita wa hayaku okiru tsumori desu.
Example (English): I plan to wake up early tomorrow.

Meaning: Expresses the speaker's intention or plan; 'with the intention of', 'planning to'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + つもりで
Example (Japanese): 私は日本に住むつもりで日本語を勉強しています。
Example (Romaji): Watashi wa Nihon ni sumu tsumori de Nihongo o benkyou shiteimasu.
Example (English): I am studying Japanese with the intention of living in Japan.

Meaning: Expresses that just doing something is not enough or will not suffice.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ではすまない / い-Adjective + ではすまない / な-Adjective + ではすまない / Noun + ではすまない
Example (Japanese): ただ謝るではすまない。何か行動を取らなければならない。
Example (Romaji): Tada ayamaru dewa sumanai. Nanika koudou o toranakereba naranai.
Example (English): Just apologizing will not suffice. Some action needs to be taken.

Meaning: Expresses a special situation or event due to certain circumstances.
Formation: Noun + とあって / (Sometimes Verb + とあって, depending on context)
Example (Japanese): 春休みとあって、公園は子供たちでいっぱいだ。
Example (Romaji): Haruyasumi to atte, kouen wa kodomo-tachi de ippai da.
Example (English): Because it's spring break, the park is full of children.

Meaning: Expresses a condition; 'if', 'when', 'since'.
Formation: Verb-casual + とあれば / い-Adjective + とあれば / な-Adjective + だとあれば / Noun + だとあれば
Example (Japanese): 無料とあれば、誰でも利用したいと思います。
Example (Romaji): Muryou to areba, dare demo riyou shitai to omoimasu.
Example (English): If it's free, anyone would want to use it.

Meaning: Even if it is said that; Even though; Although.
Formation: Noun + といえども / Verb-plain form + といえども / Adjective + といえども
Example (Japanese): 彼が天才といえども、ミスをすることはあります。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga tensai to iedomo, misu o suru koto wa arimasu.
Example (English): Even though he’s a genius, he still makes mistakes.

Grammar Point: ～といったらありはしない (〜to ittara ari wa shinai)
Meaning: Express extreme exclamation; 'extremely', 'unbelievable', 'unsurpassed'.
Formation: Noun + といったらありはしない / な-Adjective + といったらありはしない
Example (Japanese): 彼の英語の上手さといったらありはしない。
Example (Romaji): Kare no eigo no jouzusa to ittara ari wa shinai.
Example (English): His English is unbelievably good.

Grammar Point: ～といったらありゃしない (〜to ittara arya shinai)
Meaning: Emphasizes that something is to the extreme; 'you have no idea how...', 'it's incredibly...'.
Formation: Verb-casual + といったらありゃしない / い-Adjective + といったらありゃしない / な-Adjective + だ + といったらありゃしない / Noun + だ + といったらありゃしない
Example (Japanese): その店のラーメンは美味しいといったらありゃしない。
Example (Romaji): Sono mise no ramen wa oishii to ittara arya shinai.
Example (English): You have no idea how delicious the ramen at that shop is.

Meaning: Expresses the extreme of something; 'nothing can be more ... than this'.
Formation: い-Adjective + といったらない / な-Adjective + だといったらない / Noun + だといったらない
Example (Japanese): 今日は寒いといったらない。
Example (Romaji): Kyou wa samui to ittara nai.
Example (English): It’s extremely cold today.

Meaning: Highlights a situation or condition that is serious/extreme, often with a negative nuance.
Formation: Verb-casual / い-Adjective / な-Adjective（＋だ） / Noun（＋だ） + ときている
Example (Japanese): 仕事が忙しいときているので、なかなか休みが取れません。
Example (Romaji): Shigoto ga isogashii to kite iru no de, nakanaka yasumi ga toremasen.
Example (English): Because work is so busy, I just can’t take any time off.

Meaning: Indicates a contrasting or inconvenient timing; 'just when...', 'even though...'.
Formation: Verb-ている + ところを / Noun + の + ところを / い-Adjective + ところを / な-Adjective + な + ところを
Example (Japanese): ちょうど映画を見ているところを、停電で真っ暗になった。
Example (Romaji): Choudo eiga o mite iru tokoro o, teiden de makkura ni natta.
Example (English): Just when I was in the middle of watching a movie, the power went out and everything went dark.

Meaning: Indicates a general belief or widely accepted view; 'is considered', 'is seen as', 'is said to be'.
Formation: Verb-casual + とされる / い-Adjective + とされる / な-Adjective + だとされる / Noun + だとされる
Example (Japanese): サッカーは世界で最も人気のあるスポーツとされています。
Example (Romaji): Sakkaa wa sekai de mottomo ninki no aru supootsu to sarete imasu.
Example (English): Soccer is considered the most popular sport in the world.

Grammar Point: ～としたところで (〜to shita tokoro de)
Meaning: Means 'even if' or 'even assuming'; emphasizes that the outcome won’t change.
Formation: Verb-casual + としたところで / い-Adjective + としたところで / な-Adjective + だとしたところで / Noun + だとしたところで
Example (Japanese): 彼が来るとしたところで、何も変わらないだろう。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga kuru to shita tokoro de, nani mo kawaranai darou.
Example (English): Even if he comes, nothing will probably change.

Meaning: Expresses 'if', 'when', or 'assuming that' in a speculative sense.
Formation: Verb-casual + とすると / い-Adjective + とすると / な-Adjective + だとすると / Noun + だとすると
Example (Japanese): 彼が来るとすると、もうすぐ到着するはずです。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga kuru to suru to, mou sugu touchaku suru hazu desu.
Example (English): If he’s coming, he should arrive soon.

Meaning: Used to express 'if it were the case that...', 'if we assume that...'.
Formation: Verb-casual + とすれば / い-Adjective + とすれば / な-Adjective + だとすれば / Noun + だとすれば
Example (Japanese): 彼が嘘つきだとすれば、その話は信じられない。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga usotsuki da to sureba, sono hanashi wa shinjirarenai.
Example (English): If he’s a liar, then his story can’t be believed.

Meaning: Used to express 'if it comes to...', 'when it becomes the case that...'.
Formation: Verb-casual + となったら / Noun + となったら
Example (Japanese): 旅行に行くとなったら、荷造りをしなければいけません。
Example (Romaji): Ryokou ni iku to nattara, nizukuri o shinakereba ikemasen.
Example (English): If it comes to going on a trip, we have to pack.

Meaning: Used to highlight a certain circumstance; 'when it comes to...', 'if it becomes...', 'in the event that...'.
Formation: Verb-casual + となると / い-Adjective + となると / な-Adjective + だとなると / Noun + だとなると
Example (Japanese): 試験となると、多くの学生が緊張する。
Example (Romaji): Shiken to naru to, ooku no gakusei ga kinchou suru.
Example (English): When it comes to exams, many students get nervous.

Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'if it comes to...; when we talk about...; in the case of...'.
Formation: Verb-casual + となれば, い-Adjective + となれば, な-Adjective + だとなれば, Noun + だとなれば
Example (Japanese): 彼がリーダーとなれば、プロジェクトは成功するでしょう。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga riidaa to nareba, purojekuto wa seikou suru deshou.
Example (English): If he becomes the leader, the project will probably succeed.

Meaning: Expresses something that the speaker heard; 'I've heard that', 'I was told that'.
Formation: Simplified phrase + とのことだ
Example (Japanese): 週末にパーティーがあるとのことだ。
Example (Romaji): Shuumatsu ni paatii ga aru to no koto da.
Example (English): I've heard that there is a party this weekend.

Meaning: Even though; although; but
Formation: Noun + とはいえ, な-Adjective + だとはいえ, い-Adjective + とはいえ, Verb-casual + とはいえ
Example (Japanese): 彼は頭が良いとはいえ、少し怠け者だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa atama ga yoi to wa ie, sukoshi namakemono da.
Example (English): Although he is smart, he is a bit lazy.

Meaning: It seems that; apparently
Formation: Verb-casual + とみえて, い-Adjective + とみえて, な-Adjective + だとみえて, Noun + だとみえて
Example (Japanese): 彼は運動が得意とみえて、毎日ジムに行っています。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa undou ga tokui to miete, mainichi jimu ni itteimasu.
Example (English): He seems to be good at exercise, as he goes to the gym every day.

Meaning: It is considered that; It is thought that; It is believed that
Formation: Verb-casual + とみられる, Noun + とみられる
Example (Japanese): 彼の行動は無責任とみられる。
Example (Romaji): Kare no koudou wa musekinin to mirareru.
Example (English): His behavior is considered irresponsible.

Meaning: Expresses the concept of 'when one sees it as', 'viewed as', or 'considering'.
Formation: Verb-casual + とみると, い-Adjective + とみると, な-Adjective + だとみると, Noun + だとみると
Example (Japanese): この問題を数学の視点でとみると、解決策が見えてきます。
Example (Romaji): Kono mondai o suugaku no shiten de to miru to, kaiketsusaku ga miete kimasu.
Example (English): When one sees this problem from a mathematical perspective, a solution begins to emerge.

Grammar Point: どんなに～うが (donna ni ～ u ga)
Meaning: Expresses 'no matter how much...', 'even if...'.
Formation: どんなに + Verb-volitional + うが, どんなに + い-Adjective(～かろう) + が, どんなに + な-Adjective + だろうが
Example (Japanese): どんなに頑張ろうが、彼の速さには追いつけない。
Example (Romaji): Donna ni ganbarou ga, kare no hayasa ni wa oitsukenai.
Example (English): No matter how hard I try, I can't catch up with his speed.

Grammar Point: ～と言わんばかりに (〜to iwan bakari ni)
Meaning: Indicates an action or behavior that strongly implies a certain unspoken message or feeling.
Formation: Verb-volitional + と言わんばかりに, い-Adjective + と言わんばかりに, な-Adjective + だと言わんばかりに, Noun + だと言わんばかりに
Example (Japanese): 彼女は優勝したと言わんばかりに笑った。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa yuushou shita to iwan bakari ni waratta.
Example (English): She laughed as if to say she won.

Grammar Point: ～と言わんばかりの Noun (～to iwan bakari no Noun)
Meaning: Expresses the concept of 'as if to say'; 'almost says'; 'suggests'.
Formation: Verb-plain form + と言わんばかりの Noun
Example (Japanese): 田中さんは嬉しくて飛び上がると言わんばかりの笑顔を見せた。
Example (Romaji): Tanaka-san wa ureshikute tobiagaru to iwan bakari no egao wo miseta.
Example (English): Tanaka showed a smile as if to say he was so happy he could jump for joy.

Meaning: Expresses a state or condition continuing just as it is (e.g. 'from birth', 'while crying', 'in the old way').
Formation: Common set phrases: 生まれながらに, 涙ながらに, 昔ながらに, 子供ながらに, etc.
Example (Japanese): 彼女は生まれながらにして優れた音感を持っている。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa umare nagara ni shite sugureta onkan o motte iru.
Example (English): She has had an excellent sense of pitch from birth.

Meaning: Indicates one action or state happening at the same time as the noun in question (e.g. 'dinner while watching TV').
Formation: Verb-ますstem (or plain minus る) + ながら + の + Noun
Example (Japanese): テレビを見ながらの夕食は、子供たちにとって楽しいだろう。
Example (Romaji): Terebi o mi-nagara no yuushoku wa, kodomotachi ni totte tanoshii darou.
Example (English): Eating dinner while watching TV might be fun for the children.

Meaning: Means 'even though' or 'despite'.
Formation: Verb stem + ながらも, い-Adjective + ながらも, な-Adjective/Noun + ながらも
Example (Japanese): 彼は貧しいながらも、幸せな生活を送っている。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa mazushii nagara mo, shiawase na seikatsu o okutte iru.
Example (English): Despite being poor, he leads a happy life.

Meaning: Expresses the idea 'it's not that it's impossible' or 'it's not that I can't'.
Formation: Verb-ないform + なくはない, い-Adjective－い + くはない, な-Adjective + ではなくはない, Noun + ではなくはない
Example (Japanese): それを終えるのは難しくなくはない。
Example (Romaji): Sore o oeru no wa muzukashiku naku wa nai.
Example (English): It's not that it's impossible to finish it.

Meaning: Expresses 'not impossible' or 'might as well'.
Formation: Verb-ないform + なくもない, い-Adjective－い + くもない, な-Adjective + でもない, Noun + でもない
Example (Japanese): 彼がもうすぐ戻るなら、待つなくもない。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga mou sugu modoru nara, matsu naku mo nai.
Example (English): If he’s coming back soon, waiting wouldn’t be a bad idea.

Meaning: Means 'if it is X, then it's X in its own way', emphasizing unique qualities.
Formation: Noun/Adjective + なら + (same Noun/Adjective) + なりに
Example (Japanese): 彼はまだ初心者なら初心者なりに頑張っている。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa mada shoshinsha nara shoshinsha nari ni ganbatteiru.
Example (English): Since he’s still a beginner, he’s doing his best in his own beginner way.

Meaning: Means 'no need to go that far' or 'not necessary'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + には及ばない
Example (Japanese): ファーストクラスに乗るには及ばない、エコノミーでも十分だ。
Example (Romaji): Faasuto kurasu ni noru ni wa oyobanai, ekonomii demo juubun da.
Example (English): There’s no need to go as far as flying first class; economy is enough.

Meaning: Indicates something is unbearable or not worth doing (e.g., 'unbearable to watch', 'unbearable to listen to').
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + に堪えない, Noun + に堪えない
Example (Japanese): 彼の冗談は聞くに堪えない。
Example (Romaji): Kare no joudan wa kiku ni taenai.
Example (English): His jokes are unbearable to listen to.

Meaning: Used to say that something is 'worth doing' or 'can stand up to' something (the positive counterpart of ～に堪えない).
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + に堪える, Noun + に堪える
Example (Japanese): 彼の歌声は聞くに堪える。
Example (Romaji): Kare no utagoe wa kiku ni taeru.
Example (English): His singing voice is worth listening to.

Meaning: To endure or withstand something; 'endure', 'withstand', 'tolerate'.
Formation: Noun + に耐える
Example (Japanese): 彼は厳しい修行に耐えた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kibishii shugyou ni taeta.
Example (English): He endured the harsh training.

Meaning: Expresses the outcome or final conclusion of a process; 'reached the point', 'led to'.
Formation: Verb-てform + に至った or Noun / Verb-dictionary + に至る (more general).
Example (Japanese): 彼は練習を重ねて、ついにプロのギタリストに至った。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa renshuu o kasanete, tsui ni puro no gitarisuto ni itatta.
Example (English): After repeated practice, he finally became a professional guitarist.

Grammar Point: ～に越したことはない (〜ni koshita koto wa nai)
Meaning: Expresses that something is the best or most desirable course of action; 'nothing better than...'.
Formation: Verb (dictionary form) + に越したことはない, い-Adjective + に越したことはない, な-Adjective/Noun + である + に越したことはない
Example (Japanese): 早く準備するに越したことはない。
Example (Romaji): Hayaku junbi suru ni koshita koto wa nai.
Example (English): It's best to prepare early.

Meaning: Expresses 'not difficult to ~' in a formal/literary sense; e.g., 'not hard to imagine/understand'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + に難くない (commonly with 想像する, 理解する, 察する, etc.)
Example (Japanese): 彼の喜びは想像に難くない。
Example (Romaji): Kare no yorokobi wa souzou ni katakunai.
Example (English): It's not hard to imagine his delight.

Grammar Point: ～のは Noun ぐらいのものだ (〜no wa Noun gurai no mono da)
Meaning: Conveys that 'only (Noun) is the case' or 'nothing but (Noun)'.
Formation: Verb-casual + のは + Noun + ぐらいのものだ, い-Adjective + のは + Noun + ぐらいのものだ, etc.
Example (Japanese): この小説を読むのは暇つぶしぐらいのものだ。
Example (Romaji): Kono shousetsu o yomu no wa hima tsubushi gurai no mono da.
Example (English): Reading this novel is nothing but a way to kill time.

Meaning: Expresses regret or a missed opportunity: 'if only', 'had I but...'.
Formation: Verb-ば + Verb-past + ものを, い-Adjective + ければ + ものを, な-Adjective/Noun + であれば + ものを, etc.
Example (Japanese): 早く起きれば、遅刻しなかったものを。
Example (Romaji): Hayaku okireba, chikoku shinakatta mono o.
Example (English): If only I'd woken up early, I wouldn't have been late.

Meaning: A suffix meaning “looking or seeming like ~” (often appears with nouns/adjectives).
Formation: [Noun/Adjective stem] + びた (forms a 連体形 modifier, e.g., 大人びた人 “an adult-like person”)
Example (Japanese): 大人びた考え方をする子供
Example (Romaji): Otonabita kangaekata o suru kodomo
Example (English): A child who thinks in a very grown-up way

Meaning: A suffix meaning “to appear/to become ~,” often used with certain adjectives or nouns.
Formation: Adjective/Noun + びる (to form a verb)
Example (Japanese): 彼女は年齢より大人びている。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa nenrei yori otona bite iru.
Example (English): She seems older than her actual age.

Meaning: Often appears as a past form of ～ぶる, meaning 'acted/pretended like ~' (or literally 'hit/bashed', depending on context).
Formation: Noun/Adjective + ぶる → ぶった (past tense), e.g., 偉そうぶった, 大人ぶった
Example (Japanese): 彼は何でも知っているかのようにぶった態度を取る。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa nandemo shitteiru ka no you ni butta taido o toru.
Example (English): He takes on an attitude as though he knows everything.

Meaning: Te-form of ～ぶる, meaning 'acting/pretending to be ~'.
Formation: Noun/Adjective + ぶる → ぶって (te-form)
Example (Japanese): 彼は何でも知ったかぶって話をする。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa nandemo shittaka butte hanashi o suru.
Example (English): He talks as if he knows everything.

Meaning: Expresses the amount of time elapsed since doing something last.
Formation: Time expression + ぶり
Example (Japanese): 三年ぶりに彼に会いました。
Example (Romaji): San-nen buri ni kare ni aimashita.
Example (English): I met him for the first time in three years.

Meaning: Used when someone is acting or pretending to be something they are not (often a negative connotation).
Formation: Noun / (Adjective stem) + ぶる
Example (Japanese): 彼はあたかも知っているかのように学者ぶる。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa atakamo shitteiru ka no you ni gakusha buru.
Example (English): He acts like a scholar, as if he knows everything.

Meaning: Expresses a limit or extent; 'it's only up to...', 'no more than...'.
Formation: Verb (dictionary/ない form) + までだ, い-Adjective + までだ, Noun + までだ
Example (Japanese): 彼とは友達までだ。それ以上の関係ではありません。
Example (Romaji): Kare to wa tomodachi made da. Sore ijou no kankei dewa arimasen.
Example (English): With him, it's only friendship—nothing more.

Meaning: Used to dismiss or negate something’s importance; 'it’s nothing at all', 'it doesn’t matter'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + もなんでもない, い-Adjective + もなんでもない, な-Adjective + なもなんでもない, Noun + もなんでもない
Example (Japanese): 100万円を負けるもなんでもない。
Example (Romaji): Hyaku man-en o makeru mo nandemonai.
Example (English): Losing a million yen is no big deal at all.

Meaning: Indicates an assumption or supposition; 'assuming', 'under the assumption that'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ものとして, い-Adjective + ものとして, な-Adjective + なものとして, Noun + のものとして
Example (Japanese): 雨が降るものとして、傘を持って行きました。
Example (Romaji): Ame ga furu mono to shite, kasa o motte ikimashita.
Example (English): Assuming it would rain, I took an umbrella.

Meaning: Emphasizes the reason or purpose for an action; 'in order to', 'for the sake of'.
Formation: Verb-negative stem + んがために
Example (Japanese): 健康を保たんがために、毎日運動をしています。
Example (Romaji): Kenkou o tamotan ga tame ni, mainichi undou o shite imasu.
Example (English): I exercise daily in order to maintain my health.

Meaning: Indicates 'as though about to ~' or 'as if to say ~'.
Formation: Verb-negative stem + ん + ばかりに
Example (Japanese): 彼は何も知らんばかりに、私の質問を無視した。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa nanimo shir-an bakari ni, watashi no shitsumon o mushi shita.
Example (English): He ignored my question as if he didn’t know anything.

Meaning: Indicates no problem or obstacle; 'it’s fine if...', 'there’s no issue'.
Formation: Verb-て form + も差し支えない, Noun + が差し支えない
Example (Japanese): 多少遅くても差し支えないです。
Example (Romaji): Tashou osokute mo sashitsukaenai desu.
Example (English): It’s no problem if you’re a bit late.

Meaning: Indicates the time or occasion when something happens; 'when', 'at the time of'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + 折に, Verb-た形 + 折に, Noun + の折に
Example (Japanese): 父が病気の折に、私は留学していました。
Example (Romaji): Chichi ga byouki no ori ni, watashi wa ryuugaku shite imashita.
Example (English): When my father was ill, I was studying abroad.

Meaning: Expresses an extreme state, often negative; 'utterly', 'extremely', 'boundlessly'.
Formation: な-Adjective（語幹）+ 極まりない, い-Adjective（連用形）+ こと + 極まりない, Noun + の極まりない
Example (Japanese): 彼の失礼な態度は極まりない。
Example (Romaji): Kare no shitsurei na taido wa kiwamarinai.
Example (English): His rude attitude is utterly beyond words.

Meaning: Also expresses an extreme degree or state, typically negative.
Formation: な-Adjective（語幹）+ 極まる, い-Adjective（連用形）+ こと + 極まる, etc.
Example (Japanese): 彼の言動は失礼極まる。
Example (Romaji): Kare no gendou wa shitsurei kiwamaru.
Example (English): His words and actions are extremely rude.

Meaning: Expresses insufficiency or lack; 'not enough', 'insufficient'.
Formation: Noun + (が) 足りない, Verb-casual + ほど/だけ + (が) 足りない
Example (Japanese): 私の日本語の能力はまだまだ足りない。
Example (Romaji): Watashi no nihongo no nouryoku wa madamada tarinai.
Example (English): My Japanese skills are still not enough.

Meaning: Indicates that something is worthy or sufficient to be called/used as ~; 'worthy of', 'enough to ~'.
Formation: Noun/Verb-dictionary form + に足る + Noun
Example (Japanese): 彼は信頼に足る人物だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa shinrai ni taru jinbutsu da.
Example (English): He is a person worthy of trust.

Meaning: Expresses an extreme degree of emotion or reaction; 'I feel so ~', 'as ~ as can be'.
Formation: い-Adjective + 限りだ, な-Adjective + な/である + 限りだ, Noun + の + 限りだ
Example (Japanese): 彼女が急に辞めてしまった。驚きの限りだ。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo ga kyuu ni yamete shimatta. Odoroki no kagiri da.
Example (English): She suddenly quit. I'm as shocked as can be.
